We want someone who is comfortable doing the work themselves, but who does not simply accept unnecessary manual work because “that’s how we do it.”
column9:
>

This role is a combination of keeping things moving today and making sure they work better tomorrow.

Your responsibilities include:

  • Improving how Sales works. You use data, feedback, and your understanding of the day-to-day work to identify where things can be better. That could mean redesigning a workflow, improving reporting, clarifying ownership, creating a better operating rhythm, or removing manual steps that no longer add value.

  • Helping Sales leadership improve performance. You look beyond individual requests and help spot patterns across the Sales organization. Where are deals slowing down? What does the data tell us about why? Are we missing information in HubSpot that would help Sales, Marketing, or leadership make better decisions? You turn those observations into practical recommendations and are comfortable challenging existing ways of working when the data points somewhere else.

  • Owning and improving the Deal Desk. When a deal needs something outside the standard process, you help move it forward. This can include approvals, documentation, commercial questions, vendor or supplier registration, procurement portals, questionnaires, and coordination across internal and external stakeholders. You take care of the immediate need, while also looking for patterns that could make the next request simpler.

  • Owning order-to-cash and collections. You take responsibility for turning booked revenue into collected cash. Collections is a meaningful and hands-on part of the role: monitoring outstanding invoices, following up with customers, picking up the phone when that is the best way to resolve an issue, and working with Sales, Finance, procurement teams, and other stakeholders to clear payment blockers. You also look at the process behind the work — reducing overdue balances, improving follow-up, and finding ways to make order-to-cash more effective over time.

  • Working AI-first. You actively use AI and automation where they can make the work more efficient or improve the quality of the outcome. That might mean analyzing patterns in Sales data, speeding up vendor registration, improving a recurring workflow, or removing repetitive administrative work. As part of RevOps, you are expected to try new approaches, keep what works, and share useful ways of working with the wider team.

  • Connecting the dots across teams. Many commercial processes cross Sales, Finance, Customer Experience, Marketing, Operations, and other parts of the business. You help create clarity around ownership, bring the right people together, and make sure decisions turn into action.

About HappyRobot

HappyRobot is the infrastructure for enterprises to build and orchestrate AI workforces. Our AI workers don't just communicate through voice and email - they make decisions, take action, and run operations autonomously across entire enterprise systems. Born in Y Combinator (S23) and backed by a16z, Base10, Prysm Capital and Eurazeo with over $200M raised, we power critical operations for global enterprises worldwide.

Our platform is battle-tested in the most demanding environments, where AI has real consequences. We started in logistics, built our own voice stack, models, and orchestration layer from the ground up, and are now bringing that infrastructure to every enterprise that runs the real economy. Learn more about our vision in our manifesto.

Role Overview

We are looking for a Deployment Strategist to join our team. In this role, you'll partner with Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) across the full deployment lifecycle, from first discovery conversation to live production. You'll lead use case discovery and scoping with senior customer stakeholders, ship prototypes hands-on to prove value early, then stay close to the build through delivery to bring the strategic, business-value lens to every decision. You're the partner who keeps the work pointed at the highest-impact outcomes, ready to pick up the keyboard alongside the FDE when the moment calls for it.

We're looking for engineers with strategic instincts: people who can write code, but whose deepest strength is the strategic, opinionated lens they bring across every phase of a deployment - spotting where value lives, scoping it realistically, and partnering with engineers to capture it from prototype to production.

At HappyRobot, there's no role seniority or hierarchy. We operate as a team of builders. We execute, we build, we own, and we care deeply about our customers and their success.

What You'll do

  • Strategic Leadership and Use Case Discovery: Partner with Global and Regional C-Level executives and VPs to assess AI opportunities and prioritize the highest-impact use cases. Lead curiosity-driven discovery that surfaces the workflows where AI creates the most business value, well beyond what the customer thought to ask for. Build the trusted relationships that let you present findings and challenge assumptions at the most senior levels, keeping technical delivery aligned with their business priorities.

  • Scoping: Frame impact versus effort with rigor on both axes. On business value, pressure-test the realistic upside, question whether the use case as posed will actually deliver the most impact, and explore whether reframing it or pivoting to an adjacent process would unlock more. The art is deeply understanding how to maximize value of this use case for the customer, not just delivering what was asked for. On technical effort, map integrations, data, and platform constraints, and surface the edge cases and dependencies that shape timelines. Land on a plan that's realistic on both.

  • Prototyping: Build prototypes and demos hands-on. Use our platform and AI-powered coding tools to test ideas end-to-end at light scope. Prove value early, before the customer commits.

  • Program Management: Coordinate work across the active deployments in an account. Be the escalation point for the customer and the watchout partner for the FDE. Stay close enough to the build that you both understand the use case deeply, spot opportunities to capture more value, and catch when work is drifting from the highest-impact path.

  • Prioritization: Sequence use cases within an account so each deployment compounds the next. Make the call on what gets built when, what gets parked, and where to invest discovery and building time.

  • Customer Partnership: Be the main business-side point of contact for the account. Build trust with operational and executive stakeholders day-to-day. Translate AI capabilities into language they can act on.

  • Onsite Embedding: Travel onsite for kickoffs, mapping sessions, and key moments where being on the ground changes the outcome.

  • Product Feedback Loop: Bring field signal back to Product and Engineering. Identify reusable patterns, common edge cases, and where the platform needs to evolve.

Must Have

  • Background that mixes technical depth with strategic instinct, and a real history of building things. Common paths include engineering (Computer Science, electrical, industrial, systems), data science, founding a tech startup, product management, or technical / strategic consulting.

  • Comfortable coding -mostly Python- using LLMs and AI-powered tools like Claude Code to ship prototypes fast.

  • Working understanding of APIs, integrations, and how AI agents sit inside enterprise workflows.

  • Strategic instinct: ability to spot the business value behind a workflow and translate it into impact, effort, and prioritization terms a C-level can act on.

  • Excellent communication skills with both executives and operators. Comfortable translating between business and technical without losing either side.

  • Proven ability to prioritize ruthlessly across multiple workstreams and drive outcomes, not just activity.

  • Founder mindset: highly independent, takes ownership, and thrives in a fast-paced environment.

Why join us?

  • Join a world-class team of engineers and builders.

  • Backed by top investors including a16z, Y Combinator, Base10, Prysm Capital and Eurazeo.

  • Have ownership and autonomy of projects and are encouraged to ship.

  • Comprehensive Benefits including healthcare, dental, vision coverage.

  • Competitive salary + equity in a high-growth startup.

Our Operating Principles


Extreme Ownership

We take full responsibility for our work, outcomes, and team success. No excuses, no blame-shifting — if something needs fixing, we own it and make it better. This means stepping up, even when it’s not “your job.” If a ball is dropped, we pick it up. If a customer is unhappy, we fix it. If a process is broken, we redesign it. We don’t wait for someone else to solve it — we lead with accountability and expect the same from those around us.

Craftsmanship

Putting care and intention into every task, striving for excellence, and taking deep ownership of the quality and outcome of your work. Craftsmanship means never settling for “just fine.” We sweat the details because details compound. Whether it’s a product feature, an internal doc, or a sales call — we treat it as a reflection of our standards. We aim to deliver jaw-dropping customer experiences by being curious, meticulous, and proud of what we build — even when nobody’s watching.

About pplwise
pplwise is a recruiting consultancy for fast-growing technology companies across Europe. Through Recruiting as a Service and Executive Search, we fill key roles for our clients, from start-ups to publicly listed companies. We are filling this position for our client Filics.

About our client: Filics
Filics is reinventing intralogistics with autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) that change how material moves. Its double-runner system makes Filics the first and only AMR that can drive through load carriers such as Euro pallets. This breaks with forklift logic and sets a new standard for efficiency. Filics is a small, hands-on team that solves hard problems with engineering excellence. Leadership goes to those who take initiative and consistently deliver. As Senior Electrical Engineer (m/f/d) at Filics, you will design the electronics at the core of the next generation of robots.

About the role
This is an on-site/hybrid role in Munich, close to engineering and assembly.

Filics doesn’t just use off-the-shelf components. It builds its own custom IP. The robots run on advanced boards that cover a wide range of electrical engineering. On one end is high power, such as battery and motor controllers. On the other end are high-speed interfaces like PCIe, USB and MIPI CSI. The real challenge is making all these subsystems work together as one system. Many of these problems have no textbook solution. Solving them takes solid experience, a deep understanding of the physics and a creative mind.

The EE team is small, and the robot is far from finished. You’ll own your boards end to end: requirements, system design, schematic, layout, design review, sourcing, manufacturing, testing and validation. You’ll keep owning them for as long as they’re in production. You’ll work closely with Embedded Software, Mechanical Engineering, Software and the Production team. As Filics moves from prototypes to series production, your designs need to work reliably at scale, not just in the lab.

What you’ll do

  • Take full ownership of a complex PCB project and get it running in as few revisions as possible

  • Design high-power and high-speed circuits and make sure they work together at system level

  • Design for EMC, manufacturability and testability, and take boards through EMC testing and certification

  • Bring new technical approaches to the team, for example a new converter architecture that enables higher charging power in a smaller package

  • Introduce useful processes from your experience, such as simulation workflows that validate a layout before it goes to production

  • Help with board bring-up and debugging together with Embedded Software, and support Production with clear documentation and training

  • Take over ownership of existing boards so the team shares responsibility

About you

  • Several years designing electronics in an R&

We are setting out to record how our own people handle groceries and to turn those recordings into a training corpus for manipulation policies. Our warehouses already log what happened on every pick and every quality check, so the recordings can carry labels most datasets never get. Making that hold is part of the job.

You decide what makes an hour of footage trainable — before we bank hundreds of them.

What you will own and deliver

  • The capture spec. Cameras, mounts, calibration, and what disqualifies an episode. You write it before we buy the fleet and enforce it after. When the spec and the floor disagree, you go to the floor and find out which one is wrong.

  • Ground truth. Hand pose is the signal that transfers from human video to robot policies, and warehouse reality — work gloves, occlusion, cold halls — is exactly where the published models struggle. You own how we measure that and how we close the gap.

  • The evaluation harness. The corpus only counts if a policy can train on it. You build the harness that decides which hours make the bank, and you hold the trainability bar as the volume grows.

  • The first training runs. Once hours bank, you post-train open robot-learning models on our data and run the first task evaluations.

  • Judgment before spend. The field moves monthly. You read what is published, reproduce the claims we depend on, and steer our capture before the money is spent, not after.

The scope

This is a seat on a small, newly created team: an operations lead who runs capture on the floor, a data engineer who owns the pipeline, and you: the machine-learning voice in the room. This is not a research-scientist role, and no publication record is required. The job is to make a corpus trainable and to train the first policies on it.

What we are looking for

  • PyTorch, and computer vision with real 3D geometry. Camera calibration, pose estimation, SLAM fundamentals. You have debugged an extrinsic calibration at least once in your life and know why it drifted.

  • You can read a paper and reproduce it. Our pipeline is assembled from published work, and your job is knowing which claims survive contact with a chilled warehouse hall.

  • You know what policies train on. Familiar with the current robot-learning stack and policy classes well enough to know what the training side will demand of the data before the data exists.

  • Dataset instincts. You have trained on data you collected yourself, and you know the failure modes that only show up at training tim..

  • Comfortable as the only ML voice. You make the call, write it down, and revisit it when the pilot data says otherwise.

We are setting out to record how our own people handle groceries and to turn those recordings into a training corpus for manipulation policies. Our warehouses already log what happened on every pick and every quality check, so the recordings can carry labels most datasets never get. Making that hold is part of the job.

You decide what makes an hour of footage trainable — before we bank hundreds of them.

What you will own and deliver

  • The capture spec. Cameras, mounts, calibration, and what disqualifies an episode. You write it before we buy the fleet and enforce it after. When the spec and the floor disagree, you go to the floor and find out which one is wrong.

  • Ground truth. Hand pose is the signal that transfers from human video to robot policies, and warehouse reality — work gloves, occlusion, cold halls — is exactly where the published models struggle. You own how we measure that and how we close the gap.

  • The evaluation harness. The corpus only counts if a policy can train on it. You build the harness that decides which hours make the bank, and you hold the trainability bar as the volume grows.

  • The first training runs. Once hours bank, you post-train open robot-learning models on our data and run the first task evaluations.

  • Judgment before spend. The field moves monthly. You read what is published, reproduce the claims we depend on, and steer our capture before the money is spent, not after.

This is a seat on a small, newly created team: an operations lead who runs capture on the floor, a data engineer who owns the pipeline, and you: the machine-learning voice in the room. Meet DeepL

DeepL is a global AI product and research company focused on building secure, intelligent solutions to complex business problems. Over 200,000 business customers and millions of individuals across 228 global markets today trust DeepL's Language AI platform for human-like translation, improved writing and real-time voice translation.
Founded in 2017 by CEO Jaroslaw “Jarek” Kutylowski, DeepL now has around 1,000 passionate employees and is supported by world-renowned investors including Benchmark, IVP, and Index Ventures.

Our goal is to become the global leader in trusted, intelligent AI technology, building products that drive better communication, foster connections, and create a meaningful impact. To achieve this, we need talented people like you to join our journey. If you’re ready to shape the future of AI and grow your career in a fast-moving, purpose-driven environment, DeepL is your next destination.

What sets us apart

What sets us apart is our blend of cutting-edge AI technology, meaningful work, and a culture where people truly thrive. We’re a team of innovators, researchers, and creators driven by a shared purpose to unlock human potential by making work simpler, smarter, and more connected.

When we share what it’s like to work at DeepL, the reactions are overwhelmingly positive. This might be because of our technology that helps millions of people and businesses communicate and work better every day, or because of the trust, curiosity, and care that shape our culture.

What we know for sure is this: being part of DeepL means joining a team dedicated to innovation, growth, and well-being. Discover more about life at DeepL onLinkedIn,Instagram, and our Blog.

Meet the team behind this journey

You will join the Hybrid Platform Engineering track, which builds and operates the compute layer underpinning DeepL's products and research: the Kubernetes control plane, node lifecycle, networking, storage and core cluster services, across both on-prem and cloud infrastructure. Today that spans hybrid infrastructure in Europe - including large on-prem GPU clusters powering DeepL's research and hundreds of on-prem GPU nodes serving production inference - as well as AWS regions across the globe running the product. The track is deepening this hybrid model, unifying how workloads run across on-prem hardware and AWS to give product and research teams a self-service foundation they can build on.
column5:
margin-bottom:0px""> 

Your responsibilities

  • Take ownership of the reliability, capacity and cost efficiency of DeepL's compute infrastructure, CPU and GPU: the hybrid platform serving our products across AWS and on-prem, and the on-prem clusters powering our research, including their hardware lifecycle

  • Shape the platform's architecture: bring strong technical positions, weigh them on their merits with your peers, and commit to decisions serving the best outcome

  • Design, build and operate production-grade Kubernetes clusters across cloud and on-prem infrastructure, taking them from design through to long-term operation

  • Drive the technical work of deepening the hybrid model - unifying how workloads run across on-prem hardware and cloud, especially AWS and supporting research as it adopts cloud-native technology and ways of working

  • Define infrastructure-as-code and platform standards that hold across the track, and strengthen observability and security so the platform's behaviour is legible to the teams that depend on it

  • Mentor engineers across the infrastructure track and raise the technical bar of the group, through design reviews, architecture decisions and the everyday habits that keep the platform maintainable

  • Build consensus across engineering teams and turn it into shipped change, shaping platform direction at track level

  • Lead incident response for hybrid infrastructure, driving remediation through to root cause, and help sustain an on-call rotation the team can carry for the long term
column7:

  • Deep, hands-on Kubernetes expertise: you have designed, built and operated clusters at scale, through their full lifecycle

  • Depth at scale in either public cloud or on-prem infrastructure, plus the credibility to work in the other. AWS experience is preferred, and bare-metal or data centre experience is strongly valued

  • Networking and Linux depth you can debug with: you can follow a problem from a container through the host to the network edge

  • Infrastructure as code with Terraform or equivalent, and GitOps delivery with tooling such as ArgoCD, applied to environments you have owned in production

  • Software engineering skills in at least one major language, Go or Python preferred, at the level of building tooling other engineers rely on

  • A track record of technical ownership spanning several teams: you create clarity where a mandate crosses team boundaries, hold clear technical positions, change them on evidence and carry other engineers with you

  • Strong incident-management and reliability-engineering discipline, and the ownership mindset to build more resilient systems

The world’s best healthcare, for free. It's not a new idea, it's called the NHS. But the largest healthcare provider is fundamentally broken. Patient satisfaction is at an all time low, and the biggest reason cited is lack of access. So we’re on a mission to fix it with technology that actually works.

We're building the front door of UK healthcare, creating a future where one billion NHS appointments are transparent and instantly bookable, and patients are guided to the right service first time using AI.

We're developing critical national infrastructure. Today, 26% of GP practices in England use our patient registration software, while one in five GP practices in London use Bookable Search to help new patients find and book appointments seamlessly.

Our latest product, Bookable Navigator, extends this vision by automatically booking appointments for existing patients.

We operate from within a working GP practice in East London 🏥 We're backed by Y Combinator, Innovate UK and the NHS Clinical Entrepreneur Programme, and were previously ranked the 8th fastest-growing startup in the UK and 33rd fastest-growing in Europe 🚀

🎯 Goal expectations

As our Revenue Operations Manager, you’ll own the tooling and data that let’s Healthtech-1 scale across the NHS.

You’ll work closely across the GTM teams, deploy internal tooling with AI, turn Attio into our source of truth, and build an intelligent GTM motion on top.

This is an IC role, not a people management role. One week you might be rolling your sleeves up with the growth team, to be one or two steps ahead in identifying what the team need to hit their targets, and building internal tooling with AI to support the team. The next week you might be deep in the data, bringing company-wide data sources together to aide growth strategy planning e.g. identifying high demand areas in our marketplace, where we need to increase supply.

You will own and maintain Attio (our CRM), including its infrastructure, workflows and data hygiene across accounts and products. You will also own all our GTM tooling (e.g. Aircall, Calendly, Granola) and keep them running and improving. You will build a lot of tooling yourself using AI (e.g. dashboard, maps). You will run practice enrichment and data scraping pipelines so our data on customers stays current and usable.

Objective 2: Give the team and leadership clear visibility

You will build and maintain dashboards tracking company growth, cycle targets and product adoption. You will own reporting on practice numbers and growth trends. You will maintain tracking so leadership always has clear visibility on where deals are at.

Objective 3: Enable the growth team to sell more

The Growth team are your customer. You will build and maintain quality lead lists for AEs. You will support AEs with operational queries, targets and tooling. You will help new growth hires ramp faster through better tooling and playbooks.

Objective 4: Drive operational improvement

You will find and build automations and workflow improvements that save the team time. You will spot friction in how the growth team operates and fix it. You will actively look for ways to help the team drive more revenue.

⚠️ This role is not for everyone

This is a high-ownership, high-expectation role. You'll be working in a fast-moving healthtech environment where accuracy, speed, and proactivity all matter at the same time.

You probably won't enjoy this role if you:

Synthesia is the world’s leading AI video platform for business, used by over 90% of the Fortune 100. Founded in 2017, the company is headquartered in London, with offices and teams across Europe and the US.

As AI continues to shape the way we live and work, Synthesia develops products to enhance visual communication and enterprise skill development, helping people work better and stay at the center of successful organizations.

Following our recent Series E funding round, where we raised $200 million, our valuation stands at $4 billion. Our total funding exceeds $530 million from premier investors including Accel, NVentures (Nvidia's VC arm), Kleiner Perkins, GV, and Evantic Capital, alongside the founders and operators of Stripe, Datadog, Miro, and Webflow.

About the role

For years, avatars have been something you watch. You write a script, we render a video, someone presses play. That model has taken AI video a long way but it has a ceiling. A video can't answer a question. It can't read the room. It can't role-play a tough conversation and adapt when you push back.

We're changing that. Interactive Avatars listen, talk, and respond in real time
column2: inside your product, your website, or your internal tools. You bring the logic and the language model
column3:
we power the avatar layer: the speech, the expression, the listening, the sense that there's someone actually there.

It's early. Interactive Avatars is in closed beta today, and the teams building on it are pushing it into places we didn't expect - AI sales reps, always-on support agents, interactive trainers, onboarding guides. We're hiring a Product Manager to own it and take it from beta to a platform that thousands of developers build on.

This is a role with real scope. You'll help define what a real-time avatar API should be, the surface developers integrate against, the experience end users feel, and the commercial model that makes it a business. You'll work directly with the engineering and research teams building the real-time avatar stack, and with the design partners already live in the beta.
column5:
margin-bottom:0px""> 

The problem you're solving

Today, a developer who wants a lifelike, real-time avatar in their product has to stitch together a streaming pipeline, a rendering layer, an agent, and a set of hard real-time problems - latency, interruption handling, listening behavior, expressiveness, consistency across sessions, most of which have nothing to do with the product they're actually trying to build.

We have the avatar technology and a working beta. What we need is a PM who can turn that into an API a developer can integrate in an afternoon, trust in production, and build a real business on top of, all while holding a quality bar high enough that the experience feels human, not uncanny.
column7:
margin-bottom:0px""> 

What you'll be doing

  • Owning the end-to-end Interactive Avatar API. This is the developer-facing surface (SDK, integration patterns, docs), the real-time experience quality, and the path from closed beta to general availability, and defining what the roadmap looks like over the coming cycles

  • Getting close to the developers and teams building on the beta: understanding how they integrate, where the API fights them, which real-time behaviors make or break the experience, and what ""production-ready"" means to them

  • Translating that understanding into a clear product direction. What to build, in what order, and why, and keeping the team aligned as the strategy evolves

  • Working closely with the engineering and research teams building the real-time avatar stack
column8:
contributing clear specs, sound judgment on trade-offs (quality vs. latency vs. cost), and the context that helps them build the right thing the first time

  • Partnering with go-to-market and commercial teams to define how the API is packaged, priced, and sold - a real-time API has a fundamentally different business model from batch video, and shaping that is part of the job

  • Defining and tracking the metrics that tell us whether the product is working across adoption, integration success, real-time quality, reliability, and the commercial signals that prove it's a business

    • Who you are

    You've owned a developer-facing product before like an API, an SDK, or a platform and you know that the product is the developer experience. You understand that adoption is won or lost in the first hour of integration, and that trust is won or lost the first time something breaks in production. You build accordingly.

    You're comfortable in a space where the roadmap isn't fully formed. You don't need a clean brief to get started. You can talk to developers, watch them integrate, synthesize what you see, and come back with a point of view. You're also honest about what you don't know and willing to update when the evidence changes.

    You care about the detail, and you can hold a quality bar for something subjective and hard: a real-time avatar either feels present and responsive or it feels off, and the difference lives in latency, interruption handling, expressiveness, and consistency. You know how to make that bar concrete and defend it.

    You think commercially. A new API isn't just a technical surface. It's a business, and you have instincts (or scar tissue) around how developer products get adopted, packaged, and monetized.

    Requirements:

    • 5+ years in product, with direct experience owning a developer-facing API, SDK, or platform product. The vertical doesn't matter, the platform depth does

    • Comfortable operating in an early-stage, 0→1 environment where discovery and delivery happen in parallel and the roadmap is still being shaped

    • Strong technical fluency: you can hold a credible conversation with engineers about real-time systems, latency, and integration trade-offs, and make good calls without needing every answer handed to you

    • Strong written communication: you can write a spec, a strategy doc, or an API design rationale that others can act on without a follow-up conversation

    • Real-time / streaming media, conversational AI, or applied-AI product experience is a strong plus but not a prerequisite.

    • Instinct for the commercial side of a developer product - adoption, packaging, and monetization is a plus.

    • Based in London or open to regular in-person time.

    Our culture

Sessions are the experiences where employees learn through conversation, companies lrun a survey at scale, and AI becomes a direct participant in how work gets done - not just a tool behind the scenes.

We are building a dedicated Risk and Compliance Assurance function in the Second Line of Defence, and we are seeking a Senior Risk and Assurance Manager to own a single view of the second-line risk and control environment across Trustly's EU and UK regulated entities.

As the Senior Risk and Assurance Manager, you will lead entity-level assurance and second-line risk oversight for Trustly’s EU and UK regulated entities, supported by the Global Enterprise Risk Management framework. This role will be part of a wider community of risk and assurance managers, which will also cover specific compliance domains (such as Financial Crimes Prevention, Safeguarding, Consumer Protection, ICT and Resilience).

The focus of this role is the regulated entities in the UK and EU. About us

People assume the supply chain is an automated, algorithmic system. In reality, hundred of thousands of operators acting as the glue between organisations and systems, doing work the world depends on, with tools that have barely changed in decades and spending hours a day on email. Nexcade is building the agentic operating system for those people, transforming the way people communicate and optimise the $1T spend on logistics every year.

Our agents are live in production with leading global Freight Forwarders, pricing millions in freight every week, and we are rapidly expanding the platform to touch every part of the logistics lifecycle.

Our founders, Dan and Tasho, spent years at Sedna and Palantir working with supply chain companies on problems like this one. We have raised $8.5M to make this a reality from top VCs and angels who backed or founded Synthesia, n8n and other world-class companies.

How we work

  • Everybody builds, founders included. The whole company is technical and runs on coding agents. You will not be asked to write production software, but you will use agents for discovery synthesis, specs, prototypes and data analysis rather than doing them by hand.

  • Closely with customers and design partners, so what we ship changes how they operate.

  • At pace. Fast cycles and quick iterations, on the product and on how we work.

  • End to end. If you see something broken or missing, you have the freedom (and the responsibility) to fix it.

  • In person, in London. We value synchronous communication.

  • Debate rigorously, decide quickly, execute relentlessly.

  • Enjoy the journey. Hard problems, good colleagues.

The role

We’re building the AI platform freight forwarders rely on. We started with quoting and are expanding across the shipment lifecycle. As Product Lead, you will be central to that expansion, helping decide where we focus and turning those decisions into products customers depend on.

What you’ll do:

  • Own product outcomes: Own the roadmap, priorities and performance of specific products, from defining the customer problem through launch, rollout and adoption. Partner with the founders on overall product direction and strategy.

  • Build from customer insight: Work closely with freight forwarders across commercial and operational roles. Understand how they work, identify the problems customers share and build products for those needs rather than one-off solutions.

  • Prototype and build: Turn ideas into working prototypes and early product versions, using AI tools and code to test them with customers. Work hands-on with engineering to take promising ideas into production, not just write specs and hand them over.

  • Drive product expansion: Build a clear view of the market, including where we win, where we do not compete and why customers choose us. Use that understanding to identify the next workflows Nexcade should enter and turn them into products that grow revenue.

  • Raise the standard of product thinking: Define success measures, test assumptions and examine accuracy, edge cases and second-order effects before scaling. Write clear specs and decision documents, including a written recommendation on the hard calls.

  • Build the product operating system: Establish a clear planning and decision-making cadence without adding bureaucracy. Make sure product meetings are well prepared, teams have the context they need and decisions translate into shipped work.

  • Make product and platform trade-offs: Work closely with engineering to decide when to invest in shared capabilities and when a faster, product-specific approach is right.

What we look for

  • Strong product judgement: You have owned meaningful product work in a complex B2B product and can show how your decisions changed customer behaviour or business results. You define success clearly and test assumptions, accuracy and edge cases before scaling.

  • Product taste: You can turn complex workflows into products that feel simple, coherent and trustworthy. You care about the details that make people choose to use them.

  • Technical fluency: You work effectively with strong engineers, understand trade-offs across architecture, AI, data and integrations and bring the customer and product perspective to choices about speed, quality and reuse.

  • Excellent judgement: You get beyond what customers ask for to understand how their work really happens and distinguish repeatable needs from bespoke requests. You use customer and market insight to make product choices that drive adoption, expansion and revenue.

  • High agency and directness: You take ownership, hold a high bar and disagree openly and constructively. You are comfortable with ambiguity, fast iteration and changing priorities.

  • Obsess over the problem: You are drawn to complex, messy problems in industries the economy depends on and want to understand how the people and systems behind them really work. Industry experience is a bonus, but not required.

Why join

The biggest product choices are still ahead: how deep we go, where we expand and how everything fits together. Our product is already live with leading freight forwarders and this role will shape what comes next. You will build AI for the work that keeps global trade moving, alongside a team from Palantir, Raft, Faculty, UnlikelyAI and Oxford. You will get meaningful equity in the company you help build.

column2:

column3:

  • Pilotage de la performance procédé : analyser quotidiennement le fonctionnement de la ligne, identifier les écarts et contribuer à la définition des actions d’amélioration.

  • Analyse des dérives : diagnostiquer les dysfonctionnements procédés — colmatage, dérives granulométriques ou aérauliques — et proposer des plans d’actions correctifs.

  • Exploitation des données : structurer les relevés, analyser les résultats et formaliser des recommandations techniques.
column4:

column5:

column6:

  • Culture sécurité : veiller au respect strict des consignes HSE dans un environnement classé Seveso Seuil Haut, inscrit dans une démarche conforme aux référentiels ISO 9001, ISO 14001 et ISO 45001.

About DITTO

DITTO is a science-led brand redefining menstrual health. As a fast-growing, VC-backed business, we're scaling a new standard in menstrual wellbeing — empowering anyone with cycle symptoms to understand, support and optimise their health every day, not just during their period. Developed by female scientists and powered by biotechnology, the Cycle Supplement is backed by over 100 clinical trials and validated in its own clinical trial.

Beyond the capsule, DITTO is building a movement — combining credible science, thoughtful design, and inclusive storytelling to change how menstrual health is perceived and supported. As we grow, performance creative will be central to how we convert attention into action.

You will sit at the intersection of data and creativity — turning science into content that stops the scroll and drives sales. This is a hands-on, high-ownership role. You will define what makes a potential customer stop, engage, and convert — and then build the systems to do it at scale.

You are not just briefing others. You are embedded in the work from the first concept through to post-production feedback and the next iteration. If you are equally energised by diving into data and dreaming up ideas, this role was built for you.

About FoodLabs

FoodLabs is Europe's leading early-stage VC and venture studio, backing founders who are shaping the future of the food, health, and climate value chains. We build companies from zero, putting capital, our own team, and hands-on operating time behind a founding team before there's a product or even a name. The studio's work spans wherever a market and the data or infrastructure underneath it are broken enough to justify building the fix from scratch.

About The General Data Corporation

General Data is the infrastructure for licensing proprietary data: The platform runs the whole deal from request to delivery, with privacy checks, rights evidence and contracts built in. The vision is to become the system of record between AI and the world’s private data, the data that has never been published but that the next generation of AI depends on. On one side are enterprises, AI labs and robotics teams that need real-world data, and on the other are companies whose operations generate it. General Data is the data infrastructure for the modern economy, connecting every party so that data can be licensed safely, transparently and at scale.
column2:
>

Why this is a unique opportunity

AI has absorbed the public internet, and its next gains will come from private, real-world data, yet today these deals still run on email, WhatsApp and brokers, with no visibility into what was checked, who holds the rights, or whether personal data was removed. Labs are already paying for this data, and regulation like GDPR and the EU Data Act makes a trusted, verifiable layer a necessity.

General Data is VC-backed and looking for its technical co-founder. Together with Founder &
column3: CEO Louai Allani, you will own the product and architecture, shape the company’s direction as an equal partner and build the team from the ground up.
column4:

  • Supplier intake: Build connectors for where companies actually keep their data: Databases, document stores, ticketing systems, machine logs, and sensor and video archives.
column5:

  • ML and data quality: Build anonymisation across text, tables, images and video, plus re-identification checks, deduplication, quality scoring and tooling that turns raw records into training-ready data.
column6:

senior-control-systems-engineer-lausanne-423621,Fusionality,Senior Control Systems Engineer,"

Fusionality is building the measurement, simulation and control stack of the fusion energy reactors of the future.

Our technology enables effective and reliable operation, monitoring, and analysis of high-temperature plasmas in fusion devices — which will one day provide clean, practically limitless power to the grid. We have spun out of EPFL’s Swiss Plasma Center and have just completed our pre-seed fundraise.
We are looking for a Senior Control Systems Engineer to join our founding team in Lausanne and help build our core technology.

This job is for you if you are a passionate engineer with deep knowledge cutting across real-time / embedded systems, software and hardware, and excited about building the systems to monitor and control real-world fusion plasmas.
• Implement real-time control, analysis, data acquisition systems in the kHz to MHz range, as individual contributor and in a team.
• Integrate solutions across a variety of company products and services as well as on our in-house test beds.
• Provide technical leadership within a growing real-time control and software engineering team that you will help to build.
• Translate customer needs into requirements and specifications.

• Experience taking hard-real-time acquisition and control loops from incomplete requirements through to commissioning on hardware, in domains such as automotive, robotics, embedded, electrical and/or scientific instrumentation.
• ‘Full stack’: familiarity with all aspects of real-time technologies, from physical/DAQ, real-time software frameworks and middleware, real-time OS and integration.
• Fluency in a mix of high-level and low-level languages such as C, C++, Rust, MATLAB/Simulink, Python. Obsession with code quality, testing and reliability.
• Experience with distributed real-time systems, real-time networking and field buses and/or SCADA is an advantage.
• Experience with embedded/μC/FPGA technologies and/or safety critical systems is an advantage.
• The unique opportunity to play a foundational role at a dynamic, fast-growing startup, shaping the technical solutions and products from the ground up.
• The opportunity to build cutting edge technology to monitor and control plasmas in real fusion devices, working side-by-side with leading plasma and control experts.
• Great working conditions, located in Lausanne, Switzerland, a city and country known for its high quality of life.
• Competitive salary and equity compensation and benefits including immigration assistance.

If you are excited about joining our team, send your CV including information about a real-time system you have taken into operation. We're looking forward to hearing from you.

Administration to lead its corporate functions and ensure the effective running of its Swiss site.

This broad leadership role combines a solid finance background with strong corporate governance and practical operational management.   • Manage relationships with external legal advisers, insurers and corporate service providers.

  • Coordinate site procedures and business continuity arrangements with relevant specialists.

  • Provide clear financial visibility to support business decisions and resource allocation.

  • Maintain appropriate financial controls, spending discipline and approval processes.

  • Monitor costs and commitments with budget owners and programme teams.

  • Support investor reporting, financing activities and due diligence when required.

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world.

We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today.

Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.

We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.

This is a hybrid sales and customer success role for someone with real scientific depth. You'll be the primary point of contact for customers — from first conversation through ongoing engagement. That means understanding what a protein design team is actually trying to achieve, helping them pick the right assays, making sure their experiments are set up correctly, and translating results back into language that's useful for their programs.

  • Running technical sales calls where you discuss binding kinetics, expression systems, and assay design, not just pricing

  • Onboarding new customers and helping them design their first experiments on the platform

  • Monitoring ongoing accounts, flagging issues early, and proactively suggesting next steps based on their results

  • Working with the biology team to troubleshoot when a customer's experiment doesn't go as expected

  • Identifying expansion opportunities within existing accounts — new targets, new assay types, larger campaigns

You won't be handed a script. You'll need to understand the science well enough to earn trust from PhD-level protein engineers and CSOs, while also being commercially sharp enough to close deals and grow accounts.

Responsibilities

column3:
>start in overleg

Krijg jij energie van het bouwen van slimme datamodellen die economische groei voorspellen nog voordat alle cijfers binnen zijn? Duik jij graag in data, ontdek je nieuwe databronnen en wil je met jouw analyses échte impact maken op officiële bbp-ramingen?
Dan is deze stage in nowcasting en econometrie precies wat je zoekt.
column4:
>

Dit is jouw uitdaging

Bij het ramen van de kwartaalcijfers van het bbp (economische groei) gebruiken we voor een aantal bedrijfstakken momenteel een relatief eenvoudige methode: de ontwikkeling van het aantal banen dient als benadering voor de economische activiteit. Dit gebeurt omdat directe en tijdige broninformatie ontbreekt. Een belangrijk gevolg hiervan is dat we de eerste ramingen later vaak moeten bijstellen wanneer er meer volledige data beschikbaar komt bij de definitieve raming (ongeveer anderhalf jaar later).

Het is aan jou om deze methodiek te verbeteren.

Je gaat een geavanceerder model ontwikkelen waarmee we de economische activiteit van deze bedrijfstakken kort na afloop van de verslagperiode nauwkeuriger kunnen inschatten. Dit wordt ook wel “nowcasting” genoemd. Het doel is om dichter bij de uiteindelijke realisatie te zitten en daarmee het aantal en de omvang van latere bijstellingen te verkleinen.

Een belangrijk onderdeel van jouw opdracht is om te onderzoeken welke databronnen tijdig beschikbaar zijn en we kunnen gebruiken als input voor dit model. Vervolgens ga je met behulp van historische data eerdere verslagperiodes simuleren. Zo kun je analyseren of jouw voorgestelde methode daadwerkelijk beter presteert dan de huidige aanpak, bijvoorbeeld door te kijken naar kleinere bijstellingen.

Tot slot ontwikkel je een werkende productiestraat in R, zodat de nieuwe methode praktisch toepasbaar wordt binnen het ramingproces.
column5:

bij CBS Den Haag

We verwelkomen je binnen de sector Nationale Rekeningen, bij het team Aanbod- en gebruiktabellen, dat bestaat uit ruim 25 mensen. Het team maakt de kwartaal- en jaarramingen van het bruto binnenlands product (bbp), en de economische groei. We zijn gedreven onderzoekers en producenten van cruciale informatie, waaronder de economische groei, en continu op zoek naar verbeteringen.

De nationale rekeningen vormen de officiële overzichtsstatistiek van de nationale economie. Het nationaal inkomen, de economische groei, het overheidstekort en het beschikbaar inkomen van huishoudens zijn enkele belangrijke macro-economische indicatoren die aan de hand van de nationale rekeningen worden vastgesteld.

Op zoek naar een statistiekstage?
Analyseer bij het CBS weegmethoden en non-respons met R en draag bij aan betere statistieken voor Nederland.
column3:
>

Dit is jouw uitdaging

Het CBS trekt steekproeven onder de Nederlandse bevolking om diverse statistieken te maken. Hierbij is sprake van selectieve non-respons. Om voor deze non-respons te corrigeren, voeren we een zogenaamde weging uit, waarbij personen een gewicht krijgen op basis van hun onder- of oververtegenwoordiging in de respons. Personen met achtergrondkenmerken die ondervertegenwoordigd zijn in de respons, krijgen dan een groter gewicht dan personen met achtergrondkenmerken die oververtegenwoordigd zijn. Zie bijvoorbeeld [1] voor algemene informatie over wegen.

Bij het uitvoeren van een weging zijn er diverse zaken om rekening mee te houden. Zo kan niet voor alle achtergrondkenmerken worden gecorrigeerd voor scheefheid, omdat de gewichten dan te extreem zouden worden. Daarnaast is het vaak verstandig om überhaupt niet voor te veel achtergrondkenmerken te corrigeren, omdat dit een negatieve invloed heeft op de marges van de schattingen voor de doelvariabelen van een onderzoek. Ook is er een relatie met de doelvariabelen in het onderzoek: op het moment dat er een samenhang is tussen een achtergrondkenmerk en de doelvariabelen van een onderzoek, is het wenselijk om wél voor dat achtergrondkenmerk te corrigeren als dat kenmerk scheef in de respons zit. Het is daarom vaak verstandig om toch zo veel mogelijk te corrigeren voor scheefheid in achtergrondkenmerken.

Het CBS heeft een reguliere werkwijze voor het opstellen en uitvoeren van wegingen voor reguliere onderzoeken. Een optie die nog niet wordt gebruikt, maar wel interessant lijkt, is het uitvoeren van een zogenaamde voorweging. Hierbij wordt de weging min of meer in twee stappen uitgevoerd, waardoor er mogelijk voor meer en/of andere achtergrondkenmerken gecorrigeerd kan worden. Wellicht is het mogelijk om eerst een correctie uit te voeren voor non-respons en vervolgens een verdere weging uit te voeren die meer focust op de doelvariabelen van het onderzoek en de achtergrondkenmerken die daarmee correleren. Dit soort vragen speelt zowel bij de reguliere steekproeven die bij het CBS worden uitgevoerd als bij potentiële nieuwe toepassingen. In deze stage ga je aan de slag om verschillende opties voor de weging te analyseren, te kijken naar de verschillen tussen deze opties en te bepalen welke keuze de voorkeur heeft.

Afhankelijk van de resultaten zouden weegmethoden aangepast kunnen worden, met directe impact op de statistieken van het CBS.

[1] https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/onze-diensten/methoden/statistische-methoden/throughput/throughput/wegen-als-correctie-voor-non-respons

Tijdens deze afstudeerstage bij het CBS duik je in echte data, werk je met R en draag je bij aan betere statistieken voor Nederland.
column3:
>

Dit is jouw uitdaging

Het CBS trekt steekproeven onder de Nederlandse bevolking om diverse statistieken te maken. Hierbij is sprake van selectieve nonrespons. We ondernemen diverse pogingen om de respons zo gelijkmatig mogelijk te laten zijn (naar diverse achtergrondkenmerken van personen). We proberen daarbij zo veel mogelijk respons binnen te krijgen, maar kijken tegelijkertijd ook naar de samenstelling van de respons. In het bijzonder kijken we daar bij diverse onderzoeken naar in de vorm van doelgroepgericht benaderen [1].

Omdat het verzenden van brieven steeds duurder wordt, wordt de afweging tussen kwaliteit en kosten ook voor onderzoeken die alleen via internetwaarneming plaatsvinden steeds relevanter. Bij dit soort onderzoeken worden meerdere brieven verstuurd als personen niet direct de vragenlijst invullen. Omdat deze brieven steeds duurder worden, lijkt het voor de hand te liggen om geen herinneringen te sturen naar personen die nog niet gerespondeerd hebben, maar tegelijkertijd ook tot groepen behoren die al voldoende gerespondeerd hebben. In zekere zin zou dit ook een doelgroepgerichte benadering zijn.

In deze stage ga jij aan de slag met een van de kernprocessen binnen het CBS: het trekken en uitbaten van de steekproef.
Dit raakt de kern van onze processen: zonder data van goede kwaliteit kunnen we geen hoogwaardige statistieken maken.
Jij gaat kijken naar de gevolgen voor onze statistieken van diverse keuzes die we bij het design kunnen maken. Zijn er verschuivingen in de samenstelling van de respons en zo ja, kunnen we begrijpen waarom die verschuivingen er zijn? En, misschien nog wel belangrijker, is er nog iets te merken van eventuele verschuivingen bij het maken van de statistieken? Wat gebeurt er als je bepaalde groepen weglaat uit de respons?

🌟 Jouw rol en impact

Jij bent een Product designer die energie krijgt van:

  • Doelgroep begrijpen: Je spreekt kinderen, ouders en leerkrachten, bezoekt scholen en combineert observaties met gedrags- en gebruiksdata.

Je werkt samen met collega’s uit Product, Engineering, Educatie, Data, Marketing en Design. Je wordt ook onderdeel van de design guild binnen Futurewhiz: een plek om design werk te bespreken, kennis te delen en elkaar te helpen groeien.

Als erfahrene:r Produktionscontroller (m/w/d) übernehmen Sie die fachliche Verantwortung für ein kleines, erfahrenes Team und bleiben gleichzeitig nah am operativen Tagesgeschäft. Ihr fachliches Know-how ist bei uns ebenso gefragt wie Ihre Fähigkeit, Aufgaben zu strukturieren, Prioritäten zu setzen und die unterschiedlichen Stärken im Team zusammenzubringen.
column4:
>

Unser Produktionscontrolling ist eng mit den Abläufen unserer Produktionsstandorte verzahnt. SAP bildet dabei das Herzstück unserer täglichen Arbeit und die zentrale Datenbasis für Abrechnung, Kalkulation und Analyse. Gemeinsam mit Ihrem Team möchten wir unsere Prozesse kontinuierlich weiterentwickeln und die Möglichkeiten von Digitalisierung und Automatisierung noch stärker nutzen. Sie schauen gemeinsam, wo neue Lösungen einen echten Mehrwert schaffen, Abläufe erleichtern und mehr Raum für die analytischen Aufgaben des Controllings ermöglichen.
column5:
>

Folgende Aufgaben erwarten Sie an unserem Standort in Hamburg-Wilhelmsburg:

  • Sie übernehmen die fachliche Führung und Weiterentwicklung unseres kleinen Teams im Produktionscontrolling, koordinieren Aufgaben und sorgen gemeinsam für verlässliche Abläufe im Tagesgeschäft.

  • Sie verantworten die Abrechnung unserer Produktionsaufträge für die Abpackbetriebe der CAFEA-Gruppe, analysieren die Ergebnisse und arbeiten dabei eng mit unseren Produktionsstandorten zusammen.

  • Sie behalten Herstellkosten, Bestände sowie die Auftrags- und Kostenstellenrechnung im Blick und stellen gemeinsam mit den relevanten Schnittstellen eine verlässliche Datenbasis in SAP sicher.

  • Sie verantworten Kalkulationsläufe sowie relevante Sonderauswertungen und interne Kalkulationen und leiten aus den Ergebnissen die passenden Fragestellungen und Handlungsbedarfe ab.

  • Gemeinsam mit Ihrem Team entwickeln Sie Prozesse, Auswertungen und unser Berichtswesen weiter und nutzen Digitalisierung und Automatisierung dort, wo sie die tägliche Arbeit sinnvoll unterstützen.

  • Darüber hinaus bringen Sie Ihr Know-How in standortübergreifende CAFEA-Projekte ein und arbeiten mit unterschiedlichen Fachbereichen und internationalen Kolleginnen und Kollegen zusammen.
column6:
>

Was Sie mitbringen

Sie sind fachlich gerne mittendrin, können gleichzeitig den Überblick behalten und haben Freude daran, Menschen, Zahlen und Prozesse zusammenzubringen? Dann passen Sie möglicherweise ziemlich gut zu uns.

Ob Ihr beruflicher Weg über ein betriebswirtschaftliches Studium, eine kaufmännische Ausbildung mit entsprechender Weiterbildung oder über mehrjährige praktische Erfahrung geführt hat, ist für uns dabei weniger entscheidend. Wichtig ist uns, dass Sie über fundierte Erfahrung im Controlling, idealerweise im Produktions- oder Werksumfeld, verfügen und betriebswirtschaftliche Zusammenhänge sicher beurteilen können.

Sie haben bereits erste Verantwortung für andere übernommen, beispielsweise als fachliche Führungskraft, Stellvertretung, Projektleitung oder in einem kleinen Team? Perfekt. Sie müssen bei uns keine langjährige Führungskarriere mitbringen. Viel wichtiger ist, dass Sie gerne Verantwortung übernehmen, Orientierung geben, zuhören und Ihr Wissen mit anderen teilen.

    Du entwickelst bestehende Arbeitsweisen, Qualitätsstandards und Prozesse weiter und sorgst dafür, dass erfolgreiche Ansätze nachhaltig im Team verankert werden.

  • Fundierte SEA-Expertise:
    Du verfügst über mehrjährige Erfahrung im Suchmaschinenmarketing und kennst die Anforderungen an Planung, Steuerung und Optimierung komplexer performanceorientierter SEA-Maßnahmen.

  • Operatives Plattformverständnis:
    Du kennst die operative Kampagnensteuerung aus eigener Erfahrung und kannst Accountstrukturen, Set-ups und Optimierungsentscheidungen in Google Ads und Microsoft Advertising fachlich sicher beurteilen.

  • Strategisches Denken:
    Du ordnest Performance-Daten und operative Fragestellungen strategisch in einen größeren Zusammenhang ein, hinterfragst bestehende Maßnahmen und leitest daraus fundierte Empfehlungen und Weiterentwicklungen ab.

  • Kritischer Blick:
    Du hinterfragst bestehende Maßnahmen und Prozesse konstruktiv, identifizierst Verbesserungspotenziale und treibst deren Weiterentwicklung mit eigenen Impulsen voran.

  • Steuerungs- und Beratungskompetenz:
    Du kannst fachliche Anforderungen klar formulieren, operative Teams zielgerichtet begleiten und unterschiedliche Stakeholder auf Augenhöhe zu einer gemeinsamen Lösung führen.

  • Trackingverständnis:
    Du bringst fundierte Kenntnisse in Conversion-Tracking, Attribution, GA4 und idealerweise Google Tag Manager mit.

  • Kommunikationsstärke:
    Du kannst komplexe Zusammenhänge verständlich vermitteln, Empfehlungen nachvollziehbar begründen und sicher vor unterschiedlichen Ansprechpartner:innen präsentieren.

  • Eigenverantwortung und Organisation:
    Du arbeitest strukturiert, selbstständig und mit hohem Qualitätsanspruch und behältst auch bei komplexen Themen, Prioritäten und Stakeholdern den Überblick.

  • Sprachkenntnisse:
    Sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift runden dein Profil ab.

Wir bei emetriq sind ein Team von Experten, das mit Leidenschaft und Fachkenntnissen zusammenarbeitet, um das Unternehmen und uns selbst weiterzuentwickeln. Unsere Werte basieren auf Vertrauen, Agilität, Selbstorganisation und Eigenverantwortung – ohne starre Hierarchien, dafür mit klaren Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten.

Mut zur Veränderung, Arbeiten auf Augenhöhe und teamübergreifende Zusammenarbeit prägen unsere Kultur. Wir suchen Menschen, die unsere Motivation und Begeisterung teilen.

Unsere Benefits

  • Hybrides Arbeiten: Dein Hauptstandort ist Bonn oder Hamburg: In Bonn bist du zweimal pro Woche vor Ort und gelegentlich in Hamburg. In Hamburg arbeitest du in der Regel einmal pro Woche im Büro und mindestens einmal im Monat in Bonn. An den übrigen Tagen entscheidest du selbst, ob du im Büro oder von zu Hause arbeitest.

  • Vergünstigungen: Personalkaufpreise für Telekomprodukte und eine Benefit-Card ohne Zuzahlung

  • Verpflegung: Getränke, Siebträgermaschine, Snacks und Dachterrasse inklusive

head-of-engineering-munich-90360,comstruct ICT,Head of Engineering,"

Construction is one of the largest industries in the world, yet it is inefficient, wasteful, and incredibly complex. Rising cost pressure and increasing complexity are pushing the industry to its limits. At comstruct, we are on a mission to fundamentally change how construction companies operate and we are looking for people who want to build that future with us.

comstruct develops autonomous AI agents that reimagine the entire material procurement process, from requisition to posted invoice. Our platform takes over repetitive and error-prone tasks across the material flow, enabling construction companies to focus on what truly matters: building. Backed by a €12.5M funding round with investors such as Google Ventures and 20VC, we are now entering our next growth phase and are looking for exceptionally driven and ambitious individuals to help scale our product.

Trusted by some of the world's largest construction companies (including Vinci), we are just getting started. To take our product to the next level, we are looking for a Head of Engineering who wants to build both the platform and the team behind it, at the intersection of AI, software, and one of the most complex industries in the world.

As our engineering team grows past 10 people across three teams, we need a technical leader who can own hiring, coaching, and org design end-to-end — freeing our CTO to focus on building and discovery, while making sure every engineer has the structure, feedback, and growth path to do their best work.

🚀 What we are looking for:

- You have 6+ years of software engineering experience, including meaningful time in high-growth startups or scale-ups

- You have led engineering teams of 10+ people, ideally managing managers or leads, not just individual contributors

- You are technical enough to be a real sparring partner in architecture and system design conversations, not a distant people manager

- You have built or scaled a technical recruiting engine before and know how to raise the hiring bar

- You are AI-first and use modern AI-assisted engineering workflows yourself

- You are structured and calm under ambiguity, and can design an org from scratch rather than just running an existing one

- Full professional proficiency in German and English

🚀 You have ownership to drive initiatives like:

- Redesigning comstruct's engineering org structure and career ladder as we scale past 10 engineers

- Building a recruiting engine that consistently brings in A-players across all three engineering teams

- Establishing the coaching, feedback, and performance rhythms that let every team lead grow into a strong manager

- Your own idea: You have an idea how we can 10x the value of our platform or our team? Go for it!

📚 How are we setting you up for success:

- A very clear path to success. You can turn the things you build from a team to a broader Engineering leadership function

- A competitive salary and equity options, as we want you to be a fully committed part of our team

- Mentorship from both experienced colleagues and external mentors, supporting you in turning ideas into reality and scaling them effectively

- Direct access to our customer champions to iterate on and refine your product ideas

- Top notch hardware, daily dinners in the office, learning and development budget, Wellpass subscriptions and yearly company off-sites &

account-manager-munich-259684,Carwow,Account Manager (m/w/d),"

Werde Account Manager (m/w/d) mit Fokus Digital Media bei Carwow in München.

Du verkaufst unsere digitalen Mediaprodukte YouTube, Meta und Data an Automobilhersteller, Partner und Mediaagenturen und begleitest die Kampagnen von der Buchung bis zur Aussteuerung.

Du bist dir nicht ganz sicher, ob die Position zu dir passt? Bewirb dich und lass es uns gemeinsam herausfinden.



Unsere Mission

Carwow ist Europas führende Plattform für den Autowechsel. Wir verändern, wie Menschen Autos kaufen, verkaufen und leasen. Mit Technologie, Medien und Automotive Expertise haben wir uns von einer reinen Bewertungsplattform zu einem der größten Online-Marktplätze entwickelt.

Unsere Reichweite geht weit über die eigene Plattform hinaus: 10 Mio. YouTube Abonnenten und mehr als 350 Mio. Online Leser pro Jahr in der Gruppe. Genau diese Reichweite und unsere Daten machen wir jetzt für Werbekunden auch außerhalb von Carwow nutzbar.

Dein Impact @ Carwow

Du baust die Säule Digital Media, Audiences und Data im deutschen OEM &
column2:
Media Team aus. Unsere Brand Partnerships Manager:innen verkaufen Retail Media auf der Plattform. Du sorgst dafür, dass Carwow auch in den Mediaplänen der Agenturen fest gesetzt ist.

Dafür hast du drei Produkte im Gepäck. Du schnürst daraus Pakete, die zu den Zielen der Partner passen und verbindest sie mit unserem Retail Media Angebot zu einer durchgängigen Media Story bis zum Kauf. So wächst ein noch junger Umsatzstrom zu einem festen Standbein, und du prägst ihn von Anfang an mit.

YouTube: Bewegtbildkampagnen im Carwow Umfeld und mit Carwow Zielgruppen, von Awareness bis Klick

Meta: Kampagnen auf Facebook und Instagram, ausgesteuert auf Menschen, die gerade nachweislich ein Auto suchen

Data: Datenberatung auf Basis der Carwow Daten, verbunden mit unserem Verständnis des deutschen Automarkts

Und neue Produkte: Weitere Formate und Ideen, die wir gerade entwickeln. Du bringst ein, was Kunden und Agenturen brauchen, und führst neue Produkte in den Markt ein


Deine Aufgaben als Account Manager mit Fokus Digital Media

  • Du verantwortest den Umsatz mit YouTube, Meta und Data im deutschen Markt und baust ihn gezielt aus (genau hier brauchst du eine ""Hunter Mentalität"" im Vertrieb)

  • Du bist erste Ansprechperson für die Mediaagenturen der Automobilhersteller, von den großen Networks bis zu den spezialisierten Häusern, und kennst dort Planung, Einkauf und Strategie

  • Du gewinnst gemeinsam mit unseren Brand Partnerships Manager:innen die Marketing und Mediaverantwortlichen der OEMs für unsere Digitalprodukte

  • Du beantwortest Briefings mit Mediaplänen und Angebote, die sich an den KPIs der Kunden messen lassen, und überzeugst mit starken Pitches

  • Du bringst gewonnene Kampagnen sauber in die Buchung: Angebot, Auftrag, Übergabe an Media Operations und Abstimmung von Assets, Laufzeiten und Tracking

  • Du steuerst laufende Kampagnen gemeinsam mit Media Operations aus, optimierst auf die vereinbarten KPIs, ordnest Reportings für Kunden ein und machst aus guten Ergebnissen Folgebuchungen und Jahresvereinbarungen

  • Du entwickelst mit Produkt, Analytics und Media Operations unsere Angebote weiter und bringst zurück, was Agenturen wirklich brauchen

    ... und du pflegst deine Pipeline und deinen Forecast so, dass wir uns darauf gemeinsam verlassen können

Dein Profil


Hinweis: Niemand erfüllt alle Anforderungen zu 100 %. Wenn du dich stark mit der Rolle identifiziert und Lust auf richtig guten Mediavertrieb hast, freuen wir uns trotzdem auf deine Bewerbung. Denn wir wollen gemeinsam mit dir wachsen.

  • Du bringst mehrere Jahre Erfahrung im digitalen Mediavertrieb mit, zum Beispiel bei einem Vermarkter, Publisher, einer Plattform oder auf Agenturseite

  • Du kennst die deutsche Agenturlandschaft und hast idealerweise ein belastbares Netzwerk in den Agenturen

  • Du hast digitale Kampagnen selbst aufgesetzt und ausgesteuert, idealerweise in DV360 (YouTube) und im Meta Ads Manager, und sprichst über CPM, Reichweite und Conversion so sicher wie über Markenziele

  • Du arbeitest gern mit Daten und kannst aus Zahlen eine Geschichte machen, die ein Kunde versteht und kauft

  • Du präsentierst komplexe Sachverhalte zielgruppengerecht und überzeugend, vor der Planer:in genauso wie vor der Marketingleitung

  • Du arbeitest strukturiert und zuverlässig, auch wenn mehrere Angebote und Buchungen gleichzeitig laufen

  • Du sprichst Deutsch auf muttersprachlichem Niveau sowie verhandlungssicheres Englisch

    Benzin im Blut ist kein Muss, Neugier auf die Automobilbranche schon.



Unser Interview Prozess

  • Talent Screen (telefonisch) mit unserem Recruiting Team - ca. 30 Minuten

  • Video Interview (online) mit dem Fachbereich - ca. 30 Minuten

  • Case Study (vor Ort) mit dem Fachbereich - ca. 60 Minuten

  • Final Values &
column3:
Team Fit (vor Ort oder online) nach Möglichkeit im Anschluss an deine Case Study - ca. 30 Minuten


Und was springt für dich dabei raus?

Bei uns findest du ein innovatives, vielfältiges und lockeres Arbeitsumfeld im Herzen Münchens. Dazu kommen:

  • Ein wettbewerbsfähiges Gehaltspaket mit variablem Anteil

  • 28 Urlaubstage, die mit der Betriebszugehörigkeit auf bis zu 35 Tage steigen, plus Sonderurlaub für Umzüge, Hochzeiten und mehr

  • Hybrides Arbeiten (3 Tage Office, 2 Tage Home Office, für dessen Ausstattung du ein Budget von 500 Euro on top bekommst)

  • Eine Bezuschussung der betrieblichen Altersvorsorge

  • Eine vergünstigte Mitgliedschaft im Urban Sports Club

  • ... sowie eine ehrliche Work Life Balance

Vielfalt und Inklusion sind fest in unserer Unternehmenskultur verankert. Wir freuen uns über jede Bewerbung und treffen unsere Entscheidungen fair, transparent und ausschließlich auf Basis von Fähigkeiten, Erfahrung und Potenzial.

about us

Every 10 minutes, 18 million conversations happen between businesses and consumers around the world.

For decades, the consumer side of those conversations sucked: long queues, robotic menus, repeated explanations, and advice that is often unhelpful. Most people today still cannot simply say what their problem is in natural language when communicating with businesses.

AI changes that. For the first time, companies can have natural conversations with customers at massive scale. Every B2C company - from energy providers to telcos to insurers - will use AI agents to talk to their customers. The number of conversations businesses will handle is going to explode in the coming years.

At telli, we are solving the challenges that come with that shift. Today, leading B2C companies like Sky are already using telli to deploy thousands of voice agents to provide their customers with a new experience. But building a first voice agent is easy, getting it to drive real outcomes for customers and businesses is the hard part. telli helps companies build, deploy, and improve consumer-facing AI voice agents at scale. This will become one of the most important software categories of the next decade, and we intend to win it.

We are a small, AI-pilled team that likes to solve hard problems. Be it engineering, product, or GTM - we build, experiment, and move fast, while heavily leveraging the capabilities of AI models. All of us like to challenge ourselves and take real ownership over what we do, all while still staying humble and keeping a low-ego culture.

Check out our principles to see how we work.

UNSER PURPOSE BEI PLANCRAFT

Gemeinsam das Rückgrat des europäischen Handwerks aufbauen – mit moderner Software und smarten AI-Lösungen.
Wir entwickeln nicht einfach nur Software – wir haben die Mission, Handwerkerinnen und Handwerksbetrieben mehr Raum zu schaffen, indem wir sie mit einer praxisnahen SaaS-Lösung ausstatten, die so arbeitet wie sie: schnell, effizient und ohne unnötigen Admin-Aufwand. Unterstützt durch smarte AI-Funktionen genau dort, wo sie im Alltag wirklich helfen. Mit Tier 1 Investoren aus Europa und den USA wie Headline und Creandum sowie über 30.000 Handwerkerinnen als Kundenbasis skalieren wir europaweit, um aus einzelnen, verstreuten Betrieben vernetzte und erfolgreiche Communities zu machen.
Wir glauben an zero admin, nicht zero personality – und wir entwickeln jede Funktion mit den Menschen im Blick, die die Sicherheitsschuhe tragen, nicht die Anzüge. Wir haben Bock, die Zukunft zu gestalten, zusammen als Team, und sind bodenständig in unserer Mission, die Macherinnen von morgen zu unterstützen.

DEINE MISSION BEI UNS

Als Customer Support Specialist (f/m/d) bist du verantwortlich dafür, unseren Kund:innen über alle Kanäle hinweg schnellen, präzisen und empathischen Support zu bieten. Du übernimmst ihre Fragen und Probleme vom ersten Kontakt bis zur Lösung, hilfst Handwerker:innen dabei, plancraft erfolgreich im Arbeitsalltag einzusetzen, und bringst wertvolle Erkenntnisse aus dem Support ein, um unser Produkt und die Customer Experience kontinuierlich zu verbessern.

Deine Verantwortlichkeiten

  • Du übernimmst den gesamten Lifecycle von Kundenanfragen über E-Mail, Chat und Telefon – von der ersten Einordnung und Analyse bis zur Lösung, Nachverfolgung und dem Abschluss.

  • Du bist die erste Anlaufstelle für Handwerker:innen bei Produktfragen, technischen Problemen und Fragen zu ihren Workflows.

  • Du sorgst für schnelle und qualitativ hochwertige Lösungen, steuerst deinen Backlog eigenständig und behältst First Response und Resolution Times im Blick.

  • Du übernimmst End-to-End-Verantwortung für deine Fälle und arbeitest bei Bedarf eng mit Customer Success, Product und Engineering zusammen.

  • Du dokumentierst und kategorisierst Fälle sauber und nachvollziehbar und lieferst damit wertvolle Informationen für Ursachenanalysen.

  • Du erstellst und pflegst Help-Center-Artikel, Macros und interne Playbooks, um Self-Service-Angebote auszubauen und unseren Support skalierbarer zu machen.

  • Du erkennst wiederkehrende Probleme, UX-Hürden und Wissenslücken frühzeitig und übersetzt diese Erkenntnisse in konkrete Vorschläge für Produkt- und Prozessverbesserungen.

  • Du hilfst Kund:innen dabei, zentrale plancraft Workflows erfolgreich zu nutzen, löst Blocker und vermittelst Best Practices klar und praxisnah.

  • Du unterstützt die Weiterentwicklung unserer Support-Automatisierungen und AI-Workflows durch Tests, Feedback und kontinuierliche Verbesserung.

  • Je nach Erfahrung übernimmst du eigene Spezialisierungsthemen, beispielsweise als Feature Champion oder bei Onboarding Sessions und Webinaren.

DEIN PROFIL

Must-haves

  • Du hast einen starken Kundenfokus und kommunizierst klar, professionell und empathisch – auch in herausfordernden Gesprächen.

  • Du gehst Probleme strukturiert und analytisch an und findest pragmatische Lösungen.

  • Du übernimmst Verantwortung für Kundenanliegen und treibst sie eigenständig bis zur Lösung.

  • Du arbeitest gerne im Team und bringst eine bodenständige, kooperative Arbeitsweise mit.

  • Du hast ein gutes technisches Verständnis und gehst sicher mit digitalen Tools und Software um.

  • Deutschkenntnisse auf C1/C2-Niveau sowie Englischkenntnisse auf mindestens B2-Niveau.

Nice-to-haves

  • Du bringst erste Erfahrung im Customer Service, Customer Support oder Customer Success mit.

  • Du hast Erfahrung mit Handwerksbetrieben oder kennst deren Arbeitsalltag und typische Workflows.

  • Du hast bereits mit Tools wie Intercom, HubSpot, Slack, Google Workspace oder Stripe gearbeitet.

  • Du verfügst über zusätzliche Sprachkenntnisse in Spanisch, Italienisch, Polnisch oder Niederländisch.
