Project leadership and delivery

  • Lead partner projects from scoping to delivery, as a key point of contact alongside the technical program managers.

  • Write technical scopes that define objectives, deliverables, success criteria, and timelines.

  • Prepare regular technical reports and presentations for partners and internal teams.

Science and campaigns

  • Apply and extend our platform to partner problems, using simulation, machine learning, data-driven optimisation, or experiments as the project requires.

  • Design and steer discovery campaigns, including agentic and closed-loop campaigns with partner labs.

  • Assess when models, simulations, and data can be trusted, and contribute to validating them against experiments.

Bridging experimental and computational teams

  • Translate platform recommendations into clear, executable experimental plans, and translate lab realities back into requirements for internal teams.

  • Make sure data from partners and our own workflows are clean, structured, and consistent.

  • Work closely with partner labs, including on-site visits at key stages of a project.

Capability and product development

  • Build and automate workflows that run reliably at scale within our platform.

We're backed by $73M from Left Lane Capital, Base10 Partners, and Eurazeo, and we're a team of around 300 builders who move fast, say things straight, and own each outcome.

Our next goal? Become Europe's most-used legal product.

Why Lexroom?

  • Shape the Standard: Be part of the team setting the benchmark for legal AI in Europe.

  • Work with the Best: Collaborate with exceptional colleagues in a culture that values competence, curiosity, and ambition.

  • Deliver Meaningful Results: Your contribution will directly influence how legal professionals work—faster, clearer, and more efficiently.

At Lexroom, we leave buzzwords behind. Here, you’ll build something that lasts: a trusted platform, a strong reputation, a new standard for the legal world.

Role
As a Legal Engineer, you will own the construction, maintenance, and strategic development of our Proprietary Database — the single most important asset behind the reliability our users trust.   • Be the voice of the user: collect and synthesize feedback from practicing lawyers and translate it into actionable input that steers product development in the right direction.

Quandela is a global leader in quantum computing, designing, building, and delivering cutting-edge quantum solutions for research and industry. Its offerings include very energy-efficient quantum computers for data centers, full-stack quantum computing solutions accessible via the cloud, and algorithm access services for academic and industrial customers. Following a pragmatic, step-by-step roadmap, Quandela has been deploying industrial-grade systems since 2023 while developing future generations of fault-tolerant quantum computers capable of scaling through the integration of thousands of photonic components. Quandela is committed to making quantum computing accessible to all in order to address the most complex industrial and societal challenges. Learn more at: Quandela | Leading Photonic Quantum Computing Solutions

Description of the Project

As a Quantum Applications Engineer, you will work at the intersection of quantum algorithms, real-world applications and customer projects.

Your mission will be to identify relevant problems that can be addressed using Quandela's quantum computing technology, assess their feasibility and define how meaningful performance should be measured.

Working directly with industrial and academic partners, you will translate real-world challenges into quantum computing problems, evaluate potential approaches and establish the appropriate benchmarks against classical methods.

This is a highly technical role with strong exposure to customers and partners. It is particularly suited to someone with a background in quantum algorithms who wants to apply that expertise to practical use cases rather than focus exclusively on theoretical research.

Your Key Responsibilities

    • Identify and assess quantum use cases by working with customers, industrial partners and internal teams to understand their challenges and translate them into relevant computational problems.
    • Perform feasibility studies to determine whether and how these problems can be addressed using current and near-term quantum computing technologies, with a particular focus on NISQ approaches.
    • Define meaningful benchmarks, including relevant problem instances, expected outputs, accuracy targets and classical baselines to objectively evaluate quantum approaches.
    • Explore promising application domains and contribute to application roadmaps, from near-term demonstrations to longer-term utility-scale applications.
    • Evaluate scientific, industrial and economic value to help prioritize the applications where quantum computing can have the greatest impact.
    • Design and maintain strategic demonstrations and Proofs of Concept, working with internal teams or external software partners depending on the project.
    • Follow customer projects throughout their lifecycle, including projects where algorithm development is performed by external partners.
    • Present technical work to customers and partners, explaining quantum approaches, results, limitations and opportunities to both technical and non-specialist audiences.
    • Collaborate closely with Quandela's algorithm, machine learning, product, project management, sales and engineering teams.

Depending on the strategic interest of a project, you may also contribute directly to the development and implementation of quantum algorithms in Python.

What will make you successful

You do not need to know every possible quantum application from day one.

What matters is your ability to approach an unfamiliar problem, ask the right questions, understand its computational structure and determine whether quantum computing provides an interesting direction to explore.

You are comfortable navigating between research and practical applications: scientifically rigorous enough to challenge an algorithmic approach, pragmatic enough to assess its real-world relevance, and comfortable enough with people to discuss your conclusions directly with customers.

Requirements

You have a strong technical background in quantum computing and quantum algorithms, combined with the curiosity and communication skills required to explore real-world applications.

You ideally bring:

  • A PhD in quantum computing, quantum information, physics, applied mathematics, computer science or a related field, or a Master's degree combined with relevant professional experience.
  • A first professional experience in a similar environment is strongly preferred.
  • Strong understanding of quantum algorithms, particularly approaches applicable to current or near-term quantum computers.
  • Knowledge of NISQ algorithms and variational quantum algorithms.
  • Good programming skills, particularly in Python.
  • The ability to understand a complex industrial or scientific problem and translate it into a computational and algorithmic framework.
  • A rigorous approach to benchmarking quantum and classical methods.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent communication skills and the confidence to present technical topics directly to customers, partners and broader audiences.

About us

EggAI is a fast-growing AI consulting and development startup. We build agentic AI solutions for enterprise clients. We are growing in several European markets.

The role

You will own the design of a shared AI platform for our clients. The platform has two parts. An AI Control Plane governs what agents may do, through identity and delegated permissions, policy enforcement, approvals, budgets and durable audit records. A managed AI Runtime is where the agents run. Both integrate with the client's identity, security, delivery and audit services.

You will set the architecture, define how services and controls fit together, and make sure what the team builds is sound, assured and ready for production. The role reaches across engineering, security, audit, risk and the client's architecture function. You will take designs through their governance, record the decisions, and give the engineers a design they can build and the client a design they can approve.

You will be EggAI's accountable architecture lead on the engagement, leading design for a delivery team of platform engineers. You make the technical decisions within the team's remit, recommend on the rest, and secure the client's approval where their architecture or risk governance requires it. 

What you will do

- Own the architecture of the AI Control Plane and AI Runtime and keep it aligned with the client's architecture standards, cloud substrate, API gateway, identity provider and audit services.
- Define service interfaces and contracts. Decide where each security and policy control is enforced: in the gateway, the control plane, the runtime or the client's own services.
- Keep the design record. Write architecture decision records (ADRs) and record every deviation from the client's standards or our reference designs for a client decision.
- Take designs through the client's architecture and risk forums. Secure approvals in time for dependent work, so that design precedes implementation.
- Lead design and quality review across all platform services. Review engineers' changes, cross-service tests and fault exercises with the CTO.
- Define how the architecture will be proven. Agree acceptance criteria with engineers and client control owners for each interface, control and infrastructure contract, including behaviour when a dependency fails, and review the test evidence showing they are met.
- Hold the build to the design's principles: policy enforced outside the agent, decisions recorded before actions take effect, fail closed with stop always available, and audit evidence that is administered independently of the people who build and run the platform, reconciled against what actually happened, and readable with the client's own tools.
- Maintain the inventory of platform controls. Record for each one whether it is enforced or only monitored, whether it is implemented, tested or still open, and what evidence it produces, so acceptance reviews work from a current record and coverage gaps are visible.
- Assess proposed technology, scope and dependency changes for their effect on the design, controls, effort and running costs, and give the programme lead a clear basis for plan and cost decisions.
- Evaluate new runtimes and managed services against the platform's control requirements. Compare shared controls with provider-native ones on integration effort, operating cost and assurance gaps, separate what is verified from what is assumed, and recommend whether to adopt, change the design or hold scope.
- Lead the technical assessment of production readiness. Review recovery, containment and fault-exercise evidence, and give the programme lead a clear view of what is ready and what is not.
- Stay with the platform through go-live and the support period after it. Resolve the architectural issues that production exposes, and decide when a fix is a design change rather than a defect.
- Prepare the client's receiving engineers to maintain the design. Lead the architecture parts of training and handover, and leave documentation, decision records and guidance they can extend without you.

Essential experience

- You have been the accountable solution or platform architect for systems that went into production, and have led engineers through building them.
- You have delivered cloud platforms into production in a regulated environment and taken designs through formal architecture and risk governance.
- You know a major cloud platform in depth: networking, identity, secrets, Kubernetes and managed services. Azure is strongly preferred.
- You have hands-on experience with API gateways, identity and delegation using OAuth and OIDC, and policy as code.
- You work with infrastructure as code, GitOps and software supply-chain controls, and understand how they underpin reproducible environments, conformance tests and release assurance.
- You have designed systems that must produce audit evidence and fail safely: durable records, immutable storage, separation of duties and deny-by-default access. You have sound judgement about retries, partial failure, idempotency, identity propagation and recovery.
- You write clear architecture decision records and can explain and defend a design to senior architects, risk owners and engineers.

Nice to have

- Delivery in financial services or banking.
- LLM or agent platforms in production, including model gateways, agent orchestration and protocols such as MCP and A2A.
- Audit, evidence retention or AI risk controls, including EU AI Act, PRA or FCA expectations.
- Products in this space such as Kong, Open Policy Agent or Microsoft Foundry.

Practical details

- Hybrid working and client-site attendance will depend on the engagement.
- You will need to complete the background and security checks required by the client.

Design, build, and scale production-grade AI systems that power the next generation of intelligent commerce.

You will work at the intersection of Software Engineering, Machine Learning, and Generative AI to build AI-native products, agentic systems, and platform capabilities used by Mirakl customers and internal teams.
This is a freelance position based in Paris or Bordeaux, with 1 day of remote work per week.
Generative AI and AI Agents are fundamentally reshaping commerce software and the way our teams work on a day to day basis.

At Mirakl, AI is becoming a core part of our product strategy. From Catalog Transformer and content generation to AI Agents and Agentic Commerce, we are building the next generation of commerce software. And we have the same ambition for our teams around AI products and adoption.
We are looking for a Senior AI Engineer to transform the way our internal teams work, and to have a significant impact on the agentic side of our Saas products.
You won't be joining a company that's thinking about AI. You'll be joining one that's already building it.
• Design, build, and deploy production-grade AI systems for both Mirakl internal operations.
• Develop solutions leveraging: LLMs, RAG, AI Agents, Multimodal AI and Evaluation frameworks.
• Architect complex agentic workflows including tools, memory, retrieval, planning, and guardrails.
• Rapidly prototype new capabilities and evolve them into scalable, reliable AI production systems.
• Connect AI systems to internal platforms, business applications, and data sources across the company.
• Enable AI agents to interact with systems such as CRM, data platform, Drive, Jira, support tools, and internal knowledge bases.
• Design robust orchestration layers between models, APIs, tools, retrieval systems, and business workflows.
• Ensure reliability, observability, scalability, and maintainability across the entire AI stack.
• Partner with end users, business teams, Product Managers, and Engineers to identify high-value opportunities for AI.
• Run pilots and experiments, gather qualitative and quantitative feedback, and measure business impact.
• Analyze usage patterns, failure modes, costs, latency, and performance metrics.
• Continuously improve accuracy, reliability, adoption, and user experience through data-driven iteration.
• Implement evaluation frameworks, guardrails, validation layers, and monitoring systems.
• Design AI systems that are secure, explainable, and production-ready.
• Ensure compliance with data security, governance, and access control requirements.
• Document architectures, capabilities, limitations, KPIs, and operational best practices.
• Build a scalable ecosystem of AI systems and agents that empower both internal teams and customers.
• Support teams in adopting AI-powered workflows and integrating AI into their daily operations.
• Contribute to AI engineering standards, reusable frameworks, and best practices across the company.
• Act as a champion for AI-driven ways of working and help shape Mirakl's transition toward Agentic Commerce.

    • Context

    Vocca builds AI voice agents that answer patient calls, book and reschedule appointments, triage emergencies, and free up administrative staff so care teams can focus on care. The product is live and used daily in hundreds of healthcare facilities, just a few months after launch.

    We are scaling fast: our target is €1M of signed ARR per month by the end of December 2026. The liberal segment (private practices and groups, ~€10–30k ARR per account) needs to contribute heavily.

    This is a full-cycle new-business role: you own everything from cold outreach to signature, and you build your own territory.

    Your mission

    Generate €400k ARR in year one in new business on the liberal segment, owning the full cycle from prospecting to signed deals.

    Expected outcomes

    1 month:

    • Get up to speed on our pitch, our product, and our market (types of centers, buying journey…)

    • Make your first prospecting calls, demos, and initial sales conversations

    • Close your first simple deals independently.

    3 months:

    • Build a stable pipeline, with at least 30 active opportunities at different stages

    • Improve our call scripts and email sequences

    • Work closely with the Ops team to ensure smooth deployments

    • Identify weak signals from the field and feed into the product roadmap

    • Full autonomy by month 3 on pitch, product, ICP, and qualification

    6-12 months:

    • Manage complex sales cycles (groups, multi-site, multiple stakeholders)

    • Contribute to structuring our sales playbook

    • Participate in training new Sales hires (onboarding, coaching, sharing learnings)

    What the role looks like day to day

    Build your own pipeline

    • Generate qualified meetings across every sales channel: cold calling first, plus email, LinkedIn, events, and networking

    • Create your own network and get referred to new decision-makers

    • Run phoning, email campaigns, and inbound screening from day one

    Own the full sales cycle

    • Deep discovery, sharp pitch, and efficient closing with practice and group decision-makers

    • Master the Vocca sales playbook to move deals stage to stage

    • Work closely with Ops to ensure smooth deployments (~1 month post-signature)

    Make the engine better

    • Keep Attio (CRM) spotless and your week tightly planned across prospecting, meetings, and networking

    • Surface field signals into the product roadmap and improve our scripts and sequences

    What sales look like on the liberal segment

    • Deal size from 15K to 30K

    • 1 month sale cycle

    • ICP : group of independent practitioners

    This role is for you if

    The prerequisites:

    • You build qualified pipeline from cold. You've done real cold calling on cold targets : people you're interrupting, not warm inbound or an existing book you upsell. You know how to create a network and earn referrals from new decision-makers.

    • You've run SMB/mid deals end to end. You've personally sourced and closed your own deals for at least 6 months, on fast, slightly pushy cycles (€10–20k average basket). You listen actively, you're convincing and assertive, and you're comfortable being pushy.

⚡ Notre équipe Customer Success

L’équipe Customer Success accompagne les établissements de santé une fois nos solutions déployées.

Sa mission : faire en sorte que les professionnels de santé utilisent Lifen au bon niveau, dans la durée, et qu’ils en tirent un bénéfice concret au quotidien.

Ce poste n’est pas un rôle d’Account Manager ou de CSM orienté renouvellement, upsell ou gestion contractuelle. Il ne s’agit pas non plus de piloter le déploiement technique ou de prendre en charge le support.

Ton terrain de jeu commence une fois les solutions en place : comprendre comment elles sont réellement utilisées, identifier ce qui limite leur adoption et construire les actions permettant de faire évoluer durablement les usages.

Tu rejoindras l’équipe en charge des établissements publics les plus stratégiques. Ton portefeuille regroupera des organisations aux tailles, configurations, pratiques et contraintes très différentes. Tu devras être capable de comprendre rapidement ce qui se passe chez chaque client, de distinguer les symptômes des causes et de mobiliser les bons leviers, côté client comme chez Lifen.

Le poste couvre les trois produits Lifen Care déjà déployés chez nos clients.

Ta mission peut se résumer simplement : comprendre pourquoi nos solutions ne sont pas encore utilisées à leur plein potentiel dans certains établissements et faire évoluer durablement ces usages.

🎯 Ce que tu feras chez nous

  • Prendre en main un portefeuille d’environ 35 hôpitaux et cliniques et construire, pour chacun, une lecture précise des usages, des interlocuteurs clés, du contexte organisationnel, des points de blocage et des opportunités.

  • Construire une véritable stratégie de portefeuille. Tu ne pourras pas accompagner 35 établissements avec le même niveau d’intensité : à toi d’identifier où ton intervention aura le plus d’impact, quels comptes nécessitent une attention immédiate et lesquels peuvent être accompagnés de manière plus scalable.

  • Diagnostiquer les freins à l’adoption à partir des données d’usage, des échanges avec les clients et de ta compréhension de leur environnement. Une baisse d’usage peut avoir des causes très différentes : configuration, organisation, processus internes, compréhension du produit, changement d’interlocuteur ou inadéquation entre l’usage réel et l’objectif initial.

  • Transformer ce diagnostic en plans d’action concrets. Selon les situations, cela pourra passer par de la formation, une évolution des pratiques, une modification de configuration, la mobilisation de nouveaux interlocuteurs ou un travail avec nos équipes Produit, Support ou Customer Operations.

DR

  • We're building the SAP/NetSuite of the AI era for mid-sized companies in the real-world economy, starting with their supply chain operations (buy, sell, stock, produce)

  • Founding deployment strategist: you deploy two things into real factories, in the same project, the ERP that runs their operations, and the AI agents that work inside it. Every client goes from signed contract to go-live on the date we promised, running on Piston, with agents already doing part of the work

  • A rare shape: someone who has led client projects that landed in industrial companies, who is genuinely AI-native, and who will write the deployment playbook for the team and our system integrator partners

  • €3M Pre-seed (Top-tier VCs)

  • €45–60k + equity

What this role is (and isn't)

Most ERP deployments are people moving data around for a year. Incumbents quote six figures for it, and the client gets the same software they had, just newer. Ours run in eight to twelve weeks and deliver two things at once: a new ERP that runs buying, selling, stock and production, and AI agents inside it that read the orders, recompute the production load, prepare the purchases, and ask a human only when it matters.

This is not a product or a sales role, you are a deployment strategist. In one project, you replace a company's ERP and you put AI agents to work inside it.

Why now

Since day one, the founders have run every deployment themselves. Clients are now coming in faster than we can handle, and we need someone to own deployments. You work directly with Eric, CEO, who also leads product. That puts you as close as it gets to what success means at Piston: the success of our clients.

What you'll do

  • Deploy the ERP, with AI. The client's sales, purchasing, stock and production move onto Piston: data migrated from their old ERP and their Excel files, configuration built from their own documents, training, go-live. AI does the heavy lifting, you do the judgment.

  • Put the first AI agents live, during the ERP deployment. You decide what each agent does on its own, what it hands to a human for approval, and you make sure it's still running three months later.

  • Write the deployment playbook. Every go-live feeds a playbook that our next deployment hires and our system integrator partners will follow.

  • Map where the client's time goes. On site, you find the work that eats people's days: re-keying orders, chasing suppliers, rebuilding the same Excel every month. That map is the backlog of the next agents.

  • Teach humans to work with agents. The people you deploy with have never supervised software that acts on its own. You show them how to trust it, check it and correct it.

  • Hold the date and the budget. You size each deployment before the contract and protect that budget.

  • Use the tools engineers build for you. Our engineers build the tools that let you deploy on your own: AI-assisted data migration from the client's old ERP and Excel files, and a builder for screens and agents. You tell them what slows you down, they make it disappear.

  • Agentify your own work. On top of the tools our engineers build, you create your own agents for the deployment itself: configuration checks, test scenarios, training material, status reports. Every manual step you repeat twice becomes an agent for the next deployment.

What you bring

You bring the energy to deploy AI at scale in industrial companies. You learn fast from discovery, and you're as comfortable with founders and leadership teams as with operators on the shop floor.

Must have

  • Customer-facing project experience. Two years or more managing client projects in an industrial environment, typically in consulting (operations, supply chain, transformation). You've held deadlines, managed stakeholders, and delivered.

  • AI-native, for real. You use LLMs every day, and you've built things with them: automations, agents, prompts that run in production (Claude, GPT, n8n, Make, scripts, whatever works). You know what an agent can do alone, where it breaks, and where a human must stay in the loop.

  • Listening before configuring. You translate what people say into what the system and the agents must do, and you notice when the two don't match.

  • At ease in front of clients: Plant directors, finance, shop-floor operators. You can hold a room, and say no in it.

  • A full load, gladly. Around 150 project days a year, several deployments running at once.

  • Fluent English and French, both required. Our first clients work in French, our team writes in English, and you may support our deployments in the United States.

Nice to have

  • You've automated a real operations process end to end, with measurable hours saved

  • You've already taken a complex B2B software live

  • Comfortable with AI

  • You've worked around manufacturing or food operations: lots, BOMs, production orders, campaigns

  • Seed / Series A experience, where nobody's job description holds for long

Talent beats checklists. If you're intrigued, apply anyway.

How we'll measure success

  • ERP go-lives on the date we promised

  • Days spent against the plan we sold

  • Agents still running three months after launch, and the hours of work they take off the client's hands

What you'll get

  • €45–60k + equity

  • World-class peers

  • The first hire of our deployment team: you write the playbook that future hires and our system integrator partners will follow, and you grow with the team it builds

  • A front-row seat on how AI agents change the way real companies operate

  • Regular company offsite (2–4 times per year) in great locations

  • Ideal equipment and setup

  • Remote-first (France), about 20% of your time on client sites

Process

We value efficiency and clarity. The entire process takes no more than 2 weeks:

  1. 30-minute intro call with Florian (CRO)

  2. 60-minute deployment deep dive with Eric (CEO)

  3. 30-min cultural-fit interview with Eugène (CTO)

  4. 2 days paid assessment, on a real client situation.

  5. Offer: If it's a match, we move fast.

Interested? Tell us about a client project you led, and something you automated with AI. A short, personal note goes a long way, AI-generated cover letters don't.

Wir sind über 200 Technikexpert:innen mit einer gemeinsamen Leidenschaft für SAP-Technologie, SAP Security und Platform Engineering – und das seit unserer Gründung im Jahr 2012. Wir sehen uns als kreative Köpfe und strategische Wegbereiter:innen, als Umsetzer:innen und Optimierer:innen, immer mit einer gehörigen Portion Spirit und Begeisterung. Genau diese Mischung macht uns aus!

Wir kennen die digitalen Herausforderungen unserer Kundschaft und liefern die passenden Lösungen. Dank unseres tiefen Fachwissens und unserem ausgeprägten technischem Weitblick gelingt es uns, die IT-Landschaften unserer Kunden kontinuierlich an die komplexen und sich ständig verändernden Anforderungen anzupassen.

Mit deiner Expertise…

  • konzeptionieren, implementieren, realisieren und betreiben wir komplexe System- und Infrastrukturumgebungen

  • arbeitest du hands-on in unserem Datacenter mit, von der Verkabelung der Server bis hin zur Installation von Netzwerk-Komponenten

  • verantwortest du Netzwerk- und Server-Systeme inklusive Virtualisierung (z. B. VMware / vSphere / Kubernetes) sowie SAN/NAS-Komponenten

  • bringst du dein Wissen aktiv in Architektur- und Technologie-Entscheidungen ein

  • betreust du die Netzwerkinfrastruktur in den itesys DataCentern (Fortinet / Arista)

  • bringst du dein Wissen aktiv in Architektur- und Technologie-Entscheidungen ein

  • bleibt unsere Umgebung stabil und sicher

Das gelingt dir durch...

  • eine abgeschlossene Ausbildung oder Studium im Bereich IT

  • mehrjährige Erfahrung als Datacenter Engineer, Network Engineer oder in einer vergleichbaren Funktion – idealerweise 7+ Jahre

  • fundierte Erfahrung im operativen Betrieb von Rechenzentrumsinfrastrukturen, vorzugsweise Fortinet und Arista

  • umfassende Kenntnisse in Virtualisierungstechnologien wie VMware, KVM, Kubernetes

  • Erfahrung mit Cloud-Technologien (Azure, AWS, GCP) und Konzepten wie Landing Zones und Bastions Hosts

  • deine ausgeprägte Teamfähigkeit und Kommunikationsstärke, sowie deine eine selbständige und strukturierte Arbeitsweise

  • sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse (mind. B2+, idealerweise C1-Niveau – erforderlich für die eigenständige Kommunikation in Kundenprojekten und technischen Abstimmungen), sowie einen Führerschein der Klasse B

Idealerweise verfügst du über einschlägige Zertifizierungen und weist diese im Lebenslauf aus.

Benefits

Kostenloser Kaffee und Firmenparkplätze - kennst du vermutlich schon, oder?

Wir möchten dir da schon etwas mehr bieten:

Flexibles Jahresarbeitszeitmodell: Bye, 9-to-5! Deine Arbeitszeit kannst du dir bei uns frei einteilen.

Weiterbildung: Bleibe immer up to date – mit bis zu zwei Wochen bezahlter Weiterbildung kein Problem

Zukunftsorientierung: Als globale Tech-Company leben wir am Puls der Zeit und blicken stets in die Zukunft.

Tools: Digitale Werkzeuge – die Essentials deiner Karriere. Bei uns kannst du Laptop und Smartphone aber auch privat nutzen.

Teamspirit: Teambuildings oder Grillabende – wir finden immer einen Grund zusammenzukommen.

Come as you are!: Bei uns geht es um das, was du draufhast – nicht um das, was du anhast. Lieber Casual, Business oder etwas dazwischen - come as you are!

Mehr Ferientage: Die gesetzlich vorgeschriebenen Ferientage sind dir nicht genug? Uns auch nicht, denn mit leeren Batterien arbeitet es sich nicht sehr gut!

Workation & Entsendungen: Eigentlich am Schreibtisch aber mental schon wieder an deinem Lieblingsurlaubsort? Durch Workations und Entsendungen hat das Träumen ein Ende.

Work-Life-Balance: Schon viel davon gehört aber nie erlebt? Bei uns bestimmst du deine Balance.

Was macht es besonders, für uns zu arbeiten?

Bei uns gleicht kein Tag dem anderen – Langeweile gibt es nicht.

Du und deine Kolleg*innen werdet mit Blick auf eure Stärken individuell gefördert. Wir legen Wert auf Weiterbildungen und fördern den teamübergreifenden Wissenstransfer durch unsere Expertenteams. Zudem sind nahbare Führungskräfte und gezieltes Performance Management wichtige Bestandteile unserer Kultur.

Teamwork makes the dream work – ist ja klar, oder?

Jedes Teammitglied erfüllt eine wichtige Aufgabe, ohne die im Ganzen etwas fehlen würde. Wir sind uns sicher, dass diese Wertschätzung motiviert. Nicht ohne Grund sind wir alle mit Freude und Leidenschaft bei der Sache und erreichen dadurch Spitzenleistungen.

Individualität macht uns aus: Teamwork ist uns wichtig, trotzdem verschwindet hier niemand in der Masse.

Arbeiten mit Wohlfühl-Faktor

Den itesys-Spirit haben wir ja schon erwähnt. Teamausflüge, gemeinsame Grillabende oder Office Brunch – wir finden immer einen Anlass zusammenzukommen. Bei uns muss niemand zum Lachen in den Keller gehen: in den Pausen herrscht eine lockere ausgelassene Atmosphäre bei dem alle willkommen sind. Beim Arbeiten kannst du jederzeit auf die Hilfsbereitschaft deiner Kolleg*innen zählen und musst dich nicht davor scheuen, Fragen zu stellen.

Wir freuen uns darauf dich kennenzulernen!

Seit 2012 stehen wir als Schweizer Dienstleister für verlässliche SAP-Landschaften und fundierte Betriebserfahrung. In dieser Rolle verantworten Sie den Betrieb, den Unterhalt und die Weiterentwicklung unserer Rechenzentren, Netzwerke und Firewall-Infrastrukturen. KNOW YOUR TALENTS.

Dein künftiger Arbeitgeber ist ein grosses Schweizer Unternehmen mit öffentlichem Auftrag und mehreren Tausend Mitarbeitenden im Raum Bern. Identity und Access Management läuft heute zu einem guten Teil über einen externen Partner. Das ändert sich jetzt: Die Plattform kommt zurück ins Haus, ein eigenes agiles Team entsteht, und Governance, Rollenmodell und Roadmap werden intern aufgebaut. Du kommst damit zum Zeitpunkt, an dem die grossen Linien noch gezogen werden und Deine Handschrift sichtbar bleibt. Rund 70 Prozent der Arbeit liegen in Organisation, Rahmenbedingungen und Konzeption, rund 30 Prozent in den Systemthemen.

Möchtest Du als

IAM Owner Governance & Plattform (a) 80 bis 100%

nicht nur Teil des Ganzen sein, sondern aktiv Einfluss nehmen und mitgestalten? Dann freuen wir uns darauf, Dich kennenzulernen.

Meine Herausforderungen

  • Die IAM-Roadmap erarbeiten und mit dem verantwortlichen Bereichsleiter zur Entscheidung bringen.

  • Das Business-Rollenmodell für das gesamte Unternehmen entwickeln, inklusive der passenden Solution Architecture.

  • Die heute extern betreute IAM-Landschaft ins Haus zurückholen und den Aufbau des internen Teams mitgestalten.

  • Die IAM-Projekte führen: Provisionierung aus dem SAP-Umfeld, On- und Offboarding externer Mitarbeitender, Neugestaltung der Rezertifizierung, Identity Provider und Verwaltung privilegierter Identitäten.

  • Workshops mit den Fachbereichen planen und moderieren und dort die Anforderungen abholen, die das Rollenmodell tragen muss.

  • Governance, Qualität und Compliance der Zugriffsrechte verantworten und für Audits belastbar machen.

  • Fachbereiche, Systemverantwortliche und Architektur beraten und IAM in Ausbildungssequenzen so vermitteln, dass es verstanden und angewendet wird.

Meine Kompetenzen

  • Mehrjährige Erfahrung im Identity und Access Management, von der Konzeption bis in den Betrieb.

  • Belegbare Projektleitung: Roadmap, Stakeholder, Termine und Budget in eigener Verantwortung.

  • Rollen- und Berechtigungsmodelle, Identity Lifecycle und Rezertifizierung aus der Praxis, nicht nur aus der Theorie.

  • Technisches Verständnis für IAM- und IGA-Plattformen, Verzeichnisdienste und Schnittstellen, ausdrücklich auch On-Premises.

  • Die Fähigkeit, komplexe Zusammenhänge so zu erklären, dass Fachbereich und Technik dieselbe Sprache sprechen, und Workshops sicher zu moderieren.

  • Strukturierte, eigenverantwortliche Arbeitsweise und Freude an der Zusammenarbeit über Bereichsgrenzen hinweg.

  • Von Vorteil: Erfahrung mit einer IGA-Suite wie Omada, SailPoint oder One Identity sowie Einblick in SAP-Berechtigungen. Beides ist willkommen, aber keine Bedingung.

Meine Vorteile

  • Eine Rolle mit echtem Gestaltungsspielraum: Plattform, Prozesse und Team entstehen mit Dir, statt dass Bestehendes verwaltet wird.

  • Eine Linie, die diesen Weg gemeinsam mit Dir gehen will und Entscheidungen zügig trifft.

  • Flexibilität, die wirklich gelebt wird: Homeoffice, Teilzeitmodelle sowie Job- und Topsharing.

📜 Contexte

Dans le cadre du renforcement de l'équipe Sécurité des Procédés d'un site industriel situé à Genève, Suisse, nous recherchons un(e) Ingénieur(e) Sécurité des Procédés (H/F) afin de contribuer à la maîtrise des risques liés aux procédés chimiques et à la sécurité des opérations industrielles.

Rattaché(e) au Département HSE / Sécurité des Procédés, vous évoluerez dans un environnement industriel exigeant et apporterez un support technique aux équipes de Production, de Maintenance et d'Ingénierie.

Votre rôle sera axé sur la prévention des accidents majeurs, la conformité aux standards et réglementations applicables, ainsi que l'amélioration continue de la performance sécurité des procédés du site.

📌 Votre rôle

En tant qu'Ingénieur(e) Sécurité des Procédés, vous interviendrez comme expert(e) technique sur l'ensemble des sujets liés à la sécurité des procédés.

Vous contribuerez à l'identification, à l'évaluation et à la maîtrise des risques procédés sur les installations existantes, les modifications techniques et les nouveaux projets.

Vous travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec les équipes EHS, Ingénierie, Production et Maintenance, ainsi qu'avec des interlocuteurs externes et les autorités locales lorsque nécessaire.

Vos missions

🎯 Responsabilités

🔹 Analyse des risques procédés
• Réaliser et mettre à jour les analyses de risques procédés, notamment les études HAZOP, What-If et LOPA.
• Identifier les scénarios de risques potentiels et recommander les mesures de prévention et de protection adaptées.
• Contribuer aux études de sécurité des installations existantes et des nouveaux projets.

🔹 Sécurité thermique & analyse technique
• Interpréter les résultats d'essais de sécurité thermique tels que DSC, C80 et RC1.
• Identifier des solutions concrètes pour maîtriser les risques liés aux réactions chimiques et aux procédés industriels.
• Analyser des données techniques complexes et formuler des recommandations claires.

🔹 Ingénierie & projets industriels
• Participer aux revues de conception des équipements et des installations industrielles.
• Contribuer aux projets d'investissement et aux modifications d'installations sous l'angle de la sécurité des procédés.
• Veiller à la prise en compte des exigences de sécurité tout au long de la conception.

🔹 Gestion du changement & conformité
• Participer aux processus de gestion du changement (MOC).
• Évaluer l'impact sécurité procédés des modifications techniques et vérifier leur conformité aux exigences applicables.
• Soutenir la mise en œuvre et le suivi des standards de sécurité des procédés conformément à la politique EHS de l'entreprise.

🔹 Support aux opérations & à la maintenance
• Apporter un support technique aux équipes d'exploitation et de maintenance sur les sujets de sécurité des procédés.
• Apporter votre expertise sur des thématiques telles que l'inertage, les pressions, les températures et les compatibilités chimiques.
• Accompagner les équipes dans la mise en œuvre des bonnes pratiques de sécurité des procédés.

🔹 Audits, réglementation & études de sécurité
• Participer aux audits et inspections de conformité réglementaire.
• Contribuer aux analyses quantitatives des risques (QRA), aux études de protection contre les explosions et aux autres évaluations de sécurité.
• Veiller au respect des standards et réglementations applicables en matière de sécurité des procédés.

🔹 Formation & sensibilisation
• Former et sensibiliser le personnel aux principes et bonnes pratiques de sécurité des procédés.
• Promouvoir une culture forte de la sécurité des procédés sur le site.
• Communiquer les exigences réglementaires et techniques aux interlocuteurs concernés.

Vos compétences

💼 Votre profil

• Diplôme d'ingénieur ou Master en génie chimique, chimie ou domaine équivalent.
• Minimum 5 ans d'expérience en sécurité des procédés dans un environnement industriel chimique ou pharmaceutique.
• Expérience confirmée dans la réalisation d'études de sécurité des procédés.
• Maîtrise des méthodologies HAZOP, LOPA, SIL et ATEX.
• Bonne connaissance des standards internationaux de sécurité des procédés tels que API, CCPS, IEC 61511 et SEVESO.
• Capacité à lire et interpréter des P&ID, schémas de procédé et spécifications d'équipements.
• Fortes capacités d'analyse et de résolution de problèmes, avec l'aptitude à synthétiser des informations techniques complexes.
• Excellentes qualités de communication et capacités pédagogiques.
• Esprit d'équipe, proactivité et autonomie.
• Français courant et bon anglais technique, notamment pour la lecture et la rédaction de documents HSE internationaux.

Avantages

🏆 Conditions du poste

• 📍 Lieu : Genève, Suisse
• 🕒 Taux d'activité : 100 %
• 📅 Date de démarrage : flexible

⚠️ Ce poste est ouvert aux candidat(e)s de nationalité suisse ou européenne (UE/AELE), ou titulaires d'un permis de travail valable pour la Suisse.

Sunflower Labs is an internationally operating company providing a fully autonomous, AI-powered drone security system built to protect commercial, industrial, and residential properties. Security that flies ahead of every threat.

About the Role

We are looking for an experienced, hands-on Manufacturing Engineer to join our Manufacturing team and act as the technical bridge between R&D and Production.

You will take ownership of released product data and turn it into stable, documented, and efficient production processes. This includes DFM/DFA review, production readiness, assembly instructions and SOPs, tooling and test-process support, troubleshooting, and continuous improvement.

We are seeking you, a professional with a strong foundation in manufacturing electronic or electromechanical products, hands-on technical troubleshooting, and practical programming or scripting used in production or test environments. Experience with robotics, autonomous systems, or similarly complex hardware is a plus.

Your Responsibilities

R&D to Production / Industrialization :

  • Own the transfer of released products, revisions, BOMs, drawings, specifications, and technical data from R&D into production.

  • Perform DFM/DFA reviews and identify issues affecting manufacturability, assembly, testing, quality, cost, or cycle time.

  • Provide structured manufacturing feedback to mechanical and electrical teams.

  • Define production readiness and ensure engineering changes are correctly implemented on the production floor.

  • Support New Product Introduction (NPI) and transition prototypes into repeatable production.

Production Documentation & Daily Support :

  • Create, approve, and continuously maintain assembly instructions, SOPs, test instructions, inspection instructions, and rework procedures.

  • Ensure production documentation always matches the latest released product revision.

  • Provide day-to-day technical support to technicians and remove process or tooling-related production blockers.

  • Troubleshoot assembly, test, fixture, tooling, and configuration issues and drive root-cause resolution.

  • Work with R&D when production issues require design, software, test, or documentation changes.

Tooling, Lean & Continuous Improvement :

  • Develop, improve, and maintain production fixtures, jigs, test setups, tools, and supporting scripts.

  • Improve assembly sequence, workstation layout, standard work, material flow, and production methods.

  • Reduce rework, waiting time, manual workarounds, process variation, and cycle time.

  • Apply Lean Manufacturing principles such as 5S, standard work, visual management, and continuous improvement.

Requirements

  • Several years of hands-on experience in manufacturing engineering, production engineering, industrialization, NPI, or a similar role.

column3:
>

About Kaizo

At Kaizo, we build a performance development and quality platform for customer support teams. Our AutoQA product uses LLMs to review support conversations against each customer's own quality rubric, automatically and at scale. Behind it sits a microservices-based stream processing platform handling over 200 million events per day (Kafka, Kubernetes on Google Cloud, ElasticSearch, MongoDB, BigQuery), and an LLMOps stack built around LangSmith for experimentation, prompt management, and tracing.

The hard part isn't calling an LLM. It's knowing, with evidence, how well the system performs on every customer's unique rubric, and having a reliable, repeatable way to improve it. That's where you come in.
column5:

  • Translate customer rubrics into AutoQA instructions. Work with real customer quality criteria and turn them into precise, testable instructions that LLMs can score reliably.

  • Run experiments that move accuracy. Design and execute evaluation experiments on large, representative datasets using LangSmith and BigQuery, and track quality with our performance metrics.

  • Build the datasets that make evaluation possible. Curate raw production data into golden datasets with balanced coverage, and generate synthetic data to cover the rare cases that matter most. QA is a discipline of rare occurrences: distributions are skewed, positives are scarce, and resourcefulness beats volume.

  • Build LLM-as-a-judge pipelines to assess system quality internally and make evaluation repeatable.

  • Make results actionable. Your experiments should end in a decision: change a prompt, adjust which tools the system uses, surface context the AI is missing, or flag where new capabilities are needed. You'll work with the AI team to ship those decisions.

  • Evaluate across the full stack. Beyond scoring quality, you'll help validate retrieval (RAG/IR), tool calling, and speech pipelines (transcription and diarization quality).

  • Join customer calls with the team to understand how QA leaders define quality, and feed what you learn back into the product.

Senior Marketing Manager

Location: Europe, Amsterdam preferred (hybrid or remote possible)
Competitive salary
Start date: as soon as possible

Let’s be blunt: Kaizo doesn’t have a real marketing engine yet.

We’ve had marketers before, but the company we are today is a different company. Over the past 18 months we’ve signed enterprise customers like Canva, Instacart, UiPath and Indeed. We’ve also rebuilt our product around a new reality: support teams now run on a mix of human agents and AI agents, and someone has to check the quality of both. Kaizo is the independent Agentic QA layer for that hybrid workforce. We work across helpdesks and Customer Service platforms, and we don’t build AI agents of our own, so we have no reason to mark our own homework.

The problem is that the market doesn’t know this yet. We’re the customer service industry’s best-kept secret.

  • The website architecture has just been rebuilt, but the content is outdated and doesn’t tell today’s story.

  • We have strong enterprise customer stories that nobody has written up.

  • Inbound is no longer enough. AI search has changed how buyers find vendors, so pipeline now has to come from outbound, partners, events and reputation.

  • We’re going to the field and starting to attend international events.

  • Sales doesn’t have all the decks, battlecards and collateral it needs.

  • Outbound has started, and it needs content behind it.


That’s where you come in.

What this role really is

We need a senior marketer who wants to build from scratch, and who sees a blank page as an opportunity, not a threat. You’ll be the one who:

  • Brings the website to life so it reflects who we are today and gets found, by people and by AI search.

  • Turns our enterprise wins into case studies and references that open new doors.

  • Owns our review and analyst presence: a proper G2 strategy, competitor and comparison pages that convert, and support for analyst relations.

  • Gives Sales and CS the content, one-pagers, battlecards and decks that win deals and renewals.

  • Starts product marketing: positioning, launches, and clear messaging on AutoQA, Agentic QA, Insights and AI Coaching for customers and prospects.

  • Builds our brand through thought leadership, PR and executive content on the future of CX quality in an AI-agent world.

  • Owns our social channels and online reputation.

  • Defines and runs a field marketing plan, so Kaizo shows up at the international events that matter to our enterprise ICP.

  • Works with Sales on outbound and partner campaigns, including our helpdesk and Customer Service ecosystem partners.

You won’t inherit a polished machine. You’ll be the architect, the builder and the driver of Kaizo’s marketing.

The deal

  • Location: Amsterdam preferred, flexible across Europe, hybrid or remote possible.

  • Reporting: directly to Thibaud, Co-CEO, as part of the commercial leadership team.

  • Real ownership, a fast feedback loop with Sales and Product, and a seat at the table where positioning gets decided.

Why this matters

Marketing is the missing piece in Kaizo’s growth engine. The product is there, the enterprise customers are there and the deals are there. Now the market needs to know it, and we need demand that scales.

If you succeed, your fingerprints will be all over Kaizo’s next growth chapter:

  • From a handful of enterprise logos → recognised category voice

  • From inbound dependency → repeatable, multi-channel pipeline

  • From scrappy content → thought leadership

→ If you’re looking for a comfortable role with a big team, a big budget and playbooks already written, this isn’t it.
→ If you want to build the marketing engine that takes Kaizo from great product to visible market leader, let’s talk.
column3:

robot-transporter-c-driver-amsterdam-252941,Monumental,Robot Transporter (C Driver),"

We're a growing team of engineers, operators and technicians from diverse backgrounds, including consumer tech, finance and media, and companies like Dyson, Shopify, Meta and Tesla. It's still the early days of building the company, and this is a chance to make an outsized impact on a problem that matters. From day one, you'll be working with an experienced founding team, backed by a $32M Series B led by Khosla Ventures and Plural, alongside other renowned investors.

Monumental is based in the city centre of Amsterdam, in a beautiful facility with a fully equipped workshop and robot testing floor. We build the whole stack in-house, hardware and software. Our work involves building robots in our workshop and houses on real construction sites, so we're onsite five days a week.

Read more on why we believe you should spend your time working on construction, and learn about our vision and company. You might enjoy our YouTube Channel, Based in Europe’s film on how we’re fixing Europe’s housing shortage, or this video by Andreas Klinger of what our office looks like.

About the role

You’ll transport robots that build houses. You’ll load them at our Amsterdam workshop, get them onto construction sites, and bring them back for repairs before their next job. When a team needs a replacement robot to keep building, you’re the person who gets it there.

We’re hiring our first Robot Transporter. We already have 150+ robots in the field and we’re expanding from the Netherlands into the UK and US. You’ll be the first person dedicated to getting our robots, equipment and materials where they need to be, helping more teams build more homes.

Your day could take you from the workshop to several active construction sites, delivering robots, collecting systems for repair and getting equipment to the next crew. You’ll work out the order of stops, what fits in each vehicle, and how to load and secure it safely. You’ll drive a C-licence box truck or B-licence van, work closely with our deployment team, and get to know the robots and the people building with them.

This is practical, physical work with room to take charge. You’ll start by planning alongside the deployment team, then take ownership of routes and transport requests as you learn the sites and loads. Plans change, sites get muddy, and teams depend on you. You’ll see the houses going up and know you helped get them built.

What you'll do

  • Drive. Operate our leased C-licence box truck and our B-licence van across the Netherlands, usually two or more movements a day. When a move needs a flatbed with forklift loading, you arrange it.

  • Plan the day’s transport. Work with the deployment team on the day’s plan: what goes in which vehicle, and the order of drop-offs and pick-ups across sites, our Groningen hub and our Amsterdam locations. Over time, more of this becomes yours to own.

  • Load and secure. Robots, hoisting cages, scaffolding, inventory kits, equipment. You know weight limits, lashing and what it takes to get a 400+ kg system in and out of a vehicle safely.

  • Run deployment logistics. Systems, kits and operational tools out to a new site before the team arrives, back to the workshop when a build wraps, and everything in between.

  • Keep the fleet where it's useful. Move idle systems from one site to another that needs them, and bring systems back for repair so that a broken robot swapped today is a wall going up tomorrow.

  • Own the vehicles. Servicing, inspections, cleaning, fuel, damage reporting and fines. Vehicles are always road-ready.

  • Log every move. Each transport is recorded in our fleet tooling so deployment managers see when their request is planned and the company always knows where every system and kit is.

  • Improve the process. Feed what you see on the road back to the inventory team (packing standards), deployment team (equipment ratios per site) and the team building our transport tooling.

  • Help with inventory in downtime. When there's nothing to move, you work with the inventory team to prepare kits, organise stock and check returned equipment back in.

What we're looking for

  • A valid C licence with Code 95 and a driver card (bestuurderskaart) (required).

  • Professional driving and load securing experience (required). Trucks, ideally box trucks with tail lift, with real responsibility for what was in the back: lashing, weight distribution, awkward loads. Equipment rental, construction logistics, removals or last-mile delivery are all good backgrounds.

  • Comfortable with physical work. Loading heavy systems with the right equipment, early starts, all weather, construction site conditions. You don’t need a robotics or construction background, but you should want to know how the systems you’re moving work.

  • Organised in chaos. You can hold a day with five drop-offs in your head, re-sequence it when a site calls, and still log everything at the end.

  • Reliable and careful. A damaged robot costs a build day. You check straps twice and say no to an overloaded vehicle.

  • Clear communication. You deal with deployment managers, site crews and the workshop every day, in person and on Slack. You raise problems early.

  • Based in the Netherlands. Able to work from Amsterdam and drive to sites nationwide. We can't support relocation or visa sponsorship for this role.

  • English required

Joining Monumental means being at the forefront of a movement aimed at making significant strides in the construction industry. At i3D.net, we provide world-class global coverage with one of the most interconnected networks in the world. Our solutions focus on low latency, zero packet loss, and unmatched scalability, enabling seamless experiences for millions of users worldwide. With dedicated support, bespoke solutions, and cutting-edge technology, we deliver reliable, cost-efficient infrastructure that empowers game developers and businesses to scale effortlessly. Partnering with major names like Nvidia, DuckDuckGo, and Ubisoft, we are shaping the future of gaming and network technology.

Waarom jouw rol belangrijk is

Als Senior Supply Chain Coordinator bij i3D.net speel je een belangrijke rol in de succesvolle realisatie van onze infrastructuurprojecten in Nederland. Je zorgt ervoor dat inkoop, leveranciersrelaties, contractmanagement en financiële beheersing goed op elkaar aansluiten, zodat complexe projecten volgens planning verlopen.

Je opereert op het snijvlak van Supply Chain, Data Center Operations, Finance, technische teams en Legal. Daarbij ben je verantwoordelijk voor de commerciële en contractuele aspecten van infrastructuurprojecten. Van het begeleiden van aanbestedingen en onderhandelen over contracten tot het beheren van contractwijzigingen, meer- en minderwerk, claims en kosten tijdens de uitvoering: jij zorgt voor structuur, overzicht en grip op het proces.

Met jouw werk heb je directe invloed op projectplanningen, kostenbeheersing en de succesvolle uitbreiding van de infrastructuur van i3D.net.

Wat ga je doen?

  • Aanbestedingen en inkoop: Je begeleidt het volledige aanbestedings- en inkoopproces voor infrastructuurprojecten, waaronder het opstellen en uitzetten van offerteaanvragen (RFQ's), het vergelijken en beoordelen van aanbiedingen, het selecteren van aannemers en het voeren van commerciële onderhandelingen.

  • Contractmanagement: Je bent verantwoordelijk voor het beheer van contracten gedurende de volledige projectcyclus. Van de eerste onderhandelingen en contractafspraken tot het afhandelen van contractwijzigingen, meer- en minderwerk en claims tijdens de uitvoering.

  • Leveranciers- en aannemersmanagement: Je bouwt en onderhoudt sterke relaties met aannemers, leveranciers en andere externe partners. Je bewaakt contractuele afspraken, kwaliteitsnormen en oplevertermijnen.

  • Kostenbeheersing en rapportages: Je bewaakt financiële verplichtingen, uitgaven en contractwaarden. Met jouw gevorderde Excel-vaardigheden zorg je voor betrouwbare financiële inzichten en signaleer je tijdig mogelijke risico's.

  • Contractmanagementsystemen: Je ondersteunt bij de selectie, implementatie en ingebruikname van een Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM)-systeem binnen de Supply Chain-afdeling.

  • Samenwerking met stakeholders: Je werkt nauw samen met Finance, Legal, technische teams en externe aannemers om projecten soepel te laten verlopen en besluitvorming te ondersteunen.

  • Procesverbetering: Je signaleert kansen om inkoopprocessen, contractbeheer, kosteninzicht en de algehele efficiëntie van projecten verder te verbeteren.

Who We Are

You've ordered dinner through Just Eat Takeaway. You've bought and sold on OLX. You've paid with PayU. Chances are, you've already used a Prosus company today.

We are Prosus, a global technology company powering some of the world's leading lifestyle ecommerce businesses. Every day, billions of people across India, Latin America, Europe and beyond use our products and services to buy, sell, pay, connect and discover.

Our AI-driven ecosystem spans 100+ companies across ecommerce, food delivery, fintech and experiences, serving billions of consumers worldwide. AI powers how we operate and innovate, with more than 60,000 active AI agents helping our teams build, scale and move faster. Through our investment team, we also back the founders and technologies shaping the future: From robotics and autonomous systems to synthetic biology and frontier AI.

Guided by our five values Innovation, Results, People, Impact, and Entrepreneurship, culture is our competitive advantage. We thrive with experimentation
column2:
we build, we test, we learn, we iterate.

Join us in shaping the future of technology at global scale.

The Opportunity

Toqan is Prosus's internal AI platform — the infrastructure and tooling layer that powers agentic AI-driven products across the entire group.We are building secure, configurable agent runtimes that can operate reliably at scale across different products, channels and use cases..  

You’ll work where distributed systems meet applied AI: orchestrating models and tools, enabling agents to perform long-running work, and turning rapidly evolving AI capabilities into dependable platform primitives. The challenges span asynchronous workflows, isolated execution, extensible integrations, reliability, observability and cost control.

The Toqan platform serves the whole Prosus portfolio and other connected businesses, which means the backend systems you build here have reach far beyond a single team. You'll join a 12-person engineering team in Amsterdam and work closely with product, platform and AI colleagues to ship end-to-end — at pace, without compromising quality.

Who You Are

You are a senior backend engineer who has moved well past following patterns and into setting them. You're comfortable owning architectural decisions on novel infrastructure — the kind where the right answer isn't obvious and the stakes are real. You think in systems, spot failure modes early, and hold a high bar for production quality without letting perfect block good. The 80/20 mindset comes naturally: you know when to go deep and when to ship.

You've likely come from a startup or high-velocity environment where shipping fast wasn't a culture slogan — it was survival. You know how to cut scope without cutting corners, move from zero to production without a safety net, and iterate quickly on systems that are still finding their shape.

You're genuinely curious about the AI and LLM space — not as a trend to track, but as a domain where you've already done hands-on integration work and want to go further. AI tools aren't an afterthought in how you work — you use them daily, whether that's Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, or OpenAI Codex, and you've developed real judgment about where they accelerate work and where they don't. You operate with low ego, share context freely, and thrive in an environment where autonomy and accountability go hand in hand. Ambiguity doesn't slow you down — it's where you do your best work.

What You Bring

  • Strong Go programming skills with a track record of building and operating production backend services

  • Hands-on AWS experience — designing, deploying, and operating cloud-native services at scale

  • Experience integrating LLMs, AI models or tool-calling systems into production applications

  • Familiarity with agentic architectures and protocols such as MCP, A2A

  • A systems mindset, with attention to reliability, scalability, performance and security

  • Experience with CI/CD, automated testing and production observability

  • A record of working across product and platform teams to deliver outcomes end-to-end

  • Regular, thoughtful use of AI coding tools as part of your development workflow

Nice to haves

  • Hands-on experience building agentic AI systems that use tools and execute multi-step workflows

  • Experience building or maintaining event-sourced systems

  • Python programming skills

  • Experience with AI or ML infrastructure and developer productivity tooling

Your Typical Day

No two days look exactly the same. You might design a new capability for the agent runtime, improve how models and tools are orchestrated, investigate a production reliability issue, or take an integration from an early prototype to a secure, observable service.

You’ll spend much of your time building in Go, reviewing code and making architectural decisions with the team. You’ll also work closely with product, platform and AI colleagues to shape requirements, test ideas and ship them safely. Along the way, you’ll improve the testing, deployment and observability foundations that let the team move quickly with confidence.

What We Offer

  • Global Impact: Play a crucial role in shaping the future of global commerce.

  • Growth Opportunities: Expand your expertise through diverse global challenges and unique opportunities.

  • Innovative Culture: Join a forward-thinking team that values strategic insights and fosters continuous innovation.

  • Creative Environment: Engage in work that encourages creativity and constant improvement.

  • Collaborative Atmosphere: Benefit from autonomy and self-management in a supportive and positive workspace.

  • Hybrid Work: Experience the satisfaction of our flexible model tailored to balance work and life.

About Zip

Zip is the AI platform for enterprise procurement — built for humans and agents working together. By orchestrating procurement across teams, tools, and suppliers with the help of AI agents, companies can secure the resources they need to innovate faster than ever before.

The world’s most influential enterprises trust Zip, including T-Mobile, OpenAI, AMD, Mars, Dollar Tree, and more. Together they’ve saved over $8 billion and processed over $500 billion in spend. Zip’s team includes product leaders from Apple, Airbnb, and Meta, as well as former procurement leaders from United Health, Sanofi, MGM Resorts, Discover, and NASA.

Backed by Adams Street, Alkeon, BOND, CRV, DST, Tiger Global, and Y Combinator, Zip has raised $371 million, most recently at a $2.2 billion valuation and has been recognized by Forbes Fintech 50, Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies, Inc. Best in Business, and LinkedIn Top Startups.

Your Role

We’re looking a Solutions Manager with Finance / Procurement System experience (SAP) to lead onboarding for new customers and drive their implementation of our product. We’re also looking for someone who is excited to be hands on and influence our product roadmap.

As every business needs our type of product, you’ll work with a variety of new clients and industries as Zip scales. Current clients include Coinbase, Snowflake, Notion, Canva, Samsara, Databricks.

videograph-in-social-media-content-vollzeit-hamburg-277203,ESH StB-Examensvorbereitung GmbH,Videograph/in – Social Media & Content - Vollzeit (m/w/d),"

Hamburg-Altona · Vollzeit · vor Ort · 4.000–4.300 € brutto/Monat

Du hast ein gutes Gespür für starke Bilder, kannst Ideen schnell in hochwertigen Content übersetzen und arbeitest gleichzeitig gerne mit klaren Briefings und festen Abläufen?

Als Videograph/in bei ESH produzierst du Foto- und Videocontent für unsere Social-Media-Kanäle, Werbeanzeigen, YouTube und unsere Website.

Du begleitest Produktionen von der Vorbereitung über den Dreh bis zur finalen Umsetzung und sorgst dafür, dass aus Ideen zuverlässig veröffentlichungsfertiger Content entsteht.

Dabei bekommst du klare Ziele, Briefings und Markenstandards – und gleichzeitig den Freiraum, deine fachliche und kreative Erfahrung in die Umsetzung einzubringen.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Du planst und realisierst Video- und Fotoproduktionen für unsere Social-Media-Kanäle.

  • Du produzierst Content für Instagram, YouTube, LinkedIn, Werbeanzeigen und unsere Website.

  • Du setzt vorgegebene Content-Ideen, Skripte und Briefings visuell um.

  • Du entwickelst gemeinsam mit unserem Marketing-Team Ideen für neue Formate und Creatives weiter.

  • Du führst Drehs selbstständig durch und sorgst für Kamera, Licht und Ton.

  • Du sichtest und strukturierst aufgenommenes Material.

  • Du schneidest Videos plattformgerecht und bereitest sie für die Veröffentlichung vor.

  • Du übernimmst Farbkorrektur, Tonbearbeitung und Qualitätskontrolle.

  • Du erstellst Einblendungen, Untertitel, Call-to-Actions und einfache Animationen.

  • Du organisierst und archivierst Foto- und Videomaterial nachvollziehbar.

  • Du achtest darauf, dass unsere Inhalte unseren Marken- und Qualitätsstandards entsprechen.

  • Gelegentlich begleitest du uns auf Veranstaltungen, Messen oder externen Drehs.

So sieht dein Arbeitsalltag aus

Deine Arbeit wechselt zwischen Vorbereitung, Produktion und Postproduktion.

An manchen Tagen setzt du mehrere kurze Social-Media-Videos um, an anderen bereitest du einen größeren Dreh vor oder arbeitest konzentriert an Schnitt und Nachbearbeitung.

Du arbeitest dabei nicht ohne Richtung.

Für unsere Inhalte gibt es klare Ziele, Zielgruppen, Briefings und wiederkehrende Formate. Dadurch weißt du, was mit einem Video erreicht werden soll und welche Anforderungen bei der Umsetzung gelten.

Innerhalb dieses Rahmens bringst du deine Erfahrung und Kreativität ein und entscheidest beispielsweise über Bildaufbau, Licht, Kameraführung oder Schnitt.

Wichtig ist uns, dass Projekte zuverlässig fertig werden und Content nicht nur kreativ aussieht, sondern seinen Zweck erfüllt.

Die Stelle passt besonders gut zu dir, wenn …

  • du kreativ bist, aber trotzdem gerne mit klaren Briefings arbeitest,

  • du Ideen schnell in konkrete Ergebnisse umsetzen kannst,

  • du ein gutes Gespür für Social-Media-Content und aktuelle Sehgewohnheiten hast,

  • du gerne mit Menschen arbeitest und Personen vor der Kamera Sicherheit geben kannst,

  • du selbstständig arbeiten und gleichzeitig Feedback gut umsetzen kannst,

  • du auch bei wiederkehrenden Formaten dauerhaft sorgfältig arbeitest,

  • du Deadlines und Absprachen zuverlässig einhältst,

  • du Details wahrnimmst, ohne dich endlos darin zu verlieren,

  • du Verantwortung dafür übernimmst, dass deine Projekte fertig und veröffentlichungsbereit sind,

  • du gerne Teil eines festen Teams bist und langfristig Verantwortung für unseren visuellen Content übernehmen möchtest.

Das solltest du mitbringen

  • Erfahrung in Videoproduktion, Fotografie oder Content-Produktion

  • sehr gutes technisches Verständnis für Kamera, Licht und Ton

  • Erfahrung im Videoschnitt und in der Nachbearbeitung

  • gutes Gespür für Bildsprache, Storytelling und Social-Media-Content

  • Verständnis dafür, wie Inhalte je nach Plattform unterschiedlich aufbereitet werden

  • selbstständige und strukturierte Arbeitsweise

  • hohe Zuverlässigkeit und Disziplin

  • schnelle Auffassungsgabe

  • Fähigkeit, klare Briefings und bestehende Prozesse zuverlässig umzusetzen

  • Offenheit für Feedback und schnelle Umsetzung von Änderungen

  • sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse

Eine Ausbildung oder ein Studium im Bereich Mediengestaltung, Film, Fotografie oder vergleichbar ist von Vorteil, aber keine Voraussetzung.

Auch als Autodidakt/in oder mit Erfahrung aus selbstständiger Tätigkeit oder Agenturumfeld kannst du sehr gut zu uns passen.

Wichtiger als dein Abschluss ist die Qualität deiner bisherigen Arbeit.

Bitte bewirb dich über den Button auf dieser Seite und füge ein Portfolio oder Beispiele deiner bisherigen Videoarbeiten bei.

Deine Einarbeitung bei ESH

Zu Beginn lernst du unsere Marke, Zielgruppen, Content-Formate und bestehenden Abläufe kennen.

Du bekommst Einblick in unsere Social-Media-Kanäle, Werbeanzeigen, bisherigen Produktionen und visuellen Standards.

Anschließend übernimmst du Schritt für Schritt eigene Produktionen und Formate.

Unsere internen Prozesse, Briefings und festen Ansprechpartner helfen dir dabei, schnell zu verstehen, was wir mit unseren Inhalten erreichen möchten.

Unser Ziel ist, dass du Produktionen zunehmend eigenständig planst, umsetzt und bis zur Veröffentlichung verantwortest.

Was gute Content-Produktion für uns bedeutet

Ein Video ist für uns nicht gut, nur weil es schön aussieht.

Guter Content muss Aufmerksamkeit erzeugen, verständlich sein und zur jeweiligen Zielgruppe und Plattform passen.

Deshalb verbinden wir kreative Umsetzung mit klaren Zielen.

Wir testen unterschiedliche Formate und Ideen, werten aus, was funktioniert, und entwickeln erfolgreiche Inhalte weiter.

Dabei erwarten wir keine Perfektion um jeden Preis.

Wichtiger sind eine hohe Qualität, zuverlässige Umsetzung und die Fähigkeit, Content regelmäßig fertigzustellen und zu veröffentlichen.

Das erwartet dich bei ESH

Klare Briefings und Ziele

Du weißt vor einer Produktion, welches Ziel ein Inhalt verfolgt und für welche Plattform und Zielgruppe er erstellt wird.

Kreativer Gestaltungsspielraum

Innerhalb unserer Marken- und Contentstandards kannst du deine fachliche Erfahrung und eigene Ideen in die Umsetzung einbringen.

Eigener Verantwortungsbereich

Du begleitest Produktionen nicht nur in einzelnen Teilschritten, sondern kannst Verantwortung von der Vorbereitung bis zum finalen Ergebnis übernehmen.

Moderne Arbeitsausstattung

Wir stellen dir die technische Ausstattung zur Verfügung, die du für deine Arbeit benötigst, und arbeiten mit modernen Arbeitsplätzen in Hamburg-Altona.

Direkte Zusammenarbeit

Du arbeitest eng mit unserem Marketing-Team und den Personen zusammen, die für unsere Inhalte vor der Kamera stehen. Entscheidungen und Feedbackwege sind dadurch kurz.

Langfristige Perspektive

Wir möchten unseren Video- und Social-Media-Content langfristig intern weiter ausbauen und suchen jemanden, der diesen Bereich dauerhaft mit uns betreut und weiterentwickelt.

Attraktive Vergütung

Je nach Erfahrung und Qualität deiner bisherigen Arbeit liegt dein Gehalt bei 4.000–4.300 € brutto pro Monat.

Mitarbeitervorteile

Über unser Mitarbeiter-Benefit-System bieten wir dir verschiedene Vergünstigungen und Zuschüsse, unter anderem über Probonio.

SumUp's tax function is scaling to match a business that now spans more than 40 entities. This role is a senior partner to the Head of Tax across the Group's tax agenda. You'll lead the implementation and operationalisation of corporate income tax, transfer pricing, and indirect tax strategy, and you'll help shape the positions and policies behind it. You'll bring your own judgement to the most important topics, from how Pillar Two, CbCR, and ATAD III affect our structure to how we manage tax risk in audits, and you'll help the Head of Tax turn those views into a clear Group direction. This role reports to the Global Head of Tax and will have an impact on SumUp's IPO readiness.
• Lead delivery of SumUp's tax agenda across corporate income tax, transfer pricing, and indirect tax, within the Group tax strategy set by the Head of Tax
• Oversee the transfer pricing framework and its implementation, and propose improvements to both substance and automation
• Draft and maintain tax policies, controls, and governance documentation for Group entities, for sign-off by the Head of Tax
• Act as the first point of contact for tax authority audits and controversies, keeping the Head of Tax aligned on positions and exposure
• Provide independent technical judgement on high-stakes tax positions, challenging assumptions and bringing options and recommendations to the Head of Tax
• Partner with Tax Compliance and Tax Operations to keep strategic positions compliant and operationally workable
• Lead the Pillar Two and CbCR implementation, turning requirements into practical plans for affected markets
• Lead, develop, and prioritise the tax team, and deputise for the Head of Tax when required
You'll be great for this role if…

• Senior tax experience across corporate income tax, transfer pricing, and indirect tax in a multinational, combining strategic leadership with hands-on technical delivery. You're comfortable working through the detail yourself, from modelling and documentation to reviewing returns, and you don't need to hand every technical question to an adviser.

• A track record of building in-house tax expertise, with a preference for developing capability internally and using external advisers selectively, for specialist opinions and peer review rather than day-to-day analysis.
• Proven track record developing senior tax team members, including people leadership, prioritisation, and performance development.
• Strong knowledge of European corporate income tax, transfer pricing, and cross-border structuring, along with Pillar Two, CbCR, and EU Directives.
• Experience leading tax audits and controversies, including extensive direct engagement with tax authorities.
• Ability to translate complex regulatory and commercial issues into clear tax positions, communicated confidently to non-tax stakeholders such as finance leadership and auditors.

About Us

At Axle Energy, we’re building the infrastructure that will underpin the decarbonised energy system. Our software moves energy usage to times when electricity is cheap and green, by controlling vehicle charging, heating systems, inverters and home batteries. We control hundreds of thousands of energy assets.

We’re building in a legacy industry and moving gigawatt-hours of electrons in the real world, but we operate at lightning speed, and we’re growing the team to meet customer demand.

We’re proud to be supported by world-leading investors, including Energize Capital and Accel. Read more about what we’re building here.

We’re looking for a commercially sharp, highly autonomous operator to drive Axle’s commercial success in the German market.

Axle has quickly become the leader in our operational markets, and we’re now looking to expand our reach internationally. Our goal is to become the go-to platform for energy flexibility globally, and we’re hiring the person to make that happen.

This role will assess Axle’s participation in German markets and business models from first principles: diving deep into regulations, modelling revenue-per-asset, and trialling new propositions at pace.

You speak German and fluent English. Other European languages are also be an asset.

What you will be doing

  • Owning new customer acquisition end-to-end, from first conversation through to commercial close, setting our partners up to generate meaningful revenue

  • High-level strategy development, defining and executing Axle’s international expansion plans, and assessing the commercial value of German markets and business models

  • Diving deep into policy and regulations, understanding how market access works and what needs doing to achieve it

  • Developing the zero-to-one of the business through partnerships with key stakeholders. You’ll be jumping on the phone (and eventually, getting on the ground) with grid operators, utilities/retailers and potential clients to create and disprove hypotheses as quickly as possible.

  • Acting as a conduit between partners and engineering teams creating fast, structured feedback loops that help translate field insights into meaningful product enhancements

As such, we are looking for a “full-stack operator” who can process highly technical information, ramp up commercial value, and accelerate us into new markets.

You might have previous experience in one or more of the activities above, but we are more interested in your growth potential than your domain-specific expertise. We are looking for people who have built things, developed new relationships, and helped get big projects over the line in complex environments.

This is an opportunity to repeatedly deliver first-of-a-kind projects across the world, become a domain expert, and work at the bleeding edge of global electrification.

What’s in it for you

This is a 12 month fixed-term contract. Compensation is highly competitive and dependent on experience.

We operate with a deliberately flat structure and aim to keep pay equitable across the company, with a 1:1 median ratio between founder and team compensation.
