This is an Atlantic portfolio venture.

About the Venture

AI models have moved faster than most companies’ ability to put them to work. The capabilities are there
column2:
knowing how to combine them effectively is still catching up.

Frontier labs naturally put their own models first. Companies often follow suit, asking one general-purpose model to handle ten very different jobs. We believe there is far more to unlock in the models that already exist, even before the next generation arrives. That is the opportunity we are building around.

We bring closed providers and open-weight models together behind a single API. Our engine breaks requests into their component parts, routes each to the right model within a cost budget, fine-tunes on customer data and checks the result against agreed quality standards. With no proprietary model to promote, we can choose the right combination for the task.

Lower costs matter because of what they make possible: giving a small team the freedom to build something that would previously have required a much larger one.

Our founder brings considerable drive, a hands-on approach and a strong sense of urgency to building the company. Backed by Atlantic at pre-seed, we are growing the engineering team to bring the product into production, with people already waiting to use it.
column3:
>

About the Role

As one of our first platform engineers, you will build the foundations that every product feature depends on: the gateway and router, usage and billing systems, customer key management and the European infrastructure underneath.

Much of that platform is still taking shape. Working directly with the founder, CTO and founding AI engineer, you will help turn early architectural decisions into systems that remain reliable as the product grows.

You will take capabilities from design through to production, thinking through their APIs, failure modes, deployment, observability and ongoing operation. In a team this small, building and running the system belong together. You will also work alongside our founding AI engineer on evals, embeddings and open-weight model serving, bringing platform engineering depth to the ML side of the product.

Agentic engineering is central to how we work. You will operate in an agentic way by default, using coding agents as a core part of how you design, build, test and ship software. You'll develop the harnesses and workflows that allow you to delegate and parallelise work effectively, increasing what a small engineering team can deliver. This requires strong coding fundamentals and the judgement to review, challenge and take responsibility for everything that reaches production.

There is a lot to build and an ambitious timeline ahead. We work with intensity, move quickly from decisions to execution and value people who take initiative and see things through.
column4:
>

What You’ll Work On

Your first area of ownership will depend on your strengths and our priorities. From there, you will contribute across the platform as it develops.

  • Gateway and routing: build a consistent API across model providers, with reliable streaming, fallbacks and safe handling of retries and provider errors.

  • Agentic engineering workflows: build and refine the harnesses, tooling and workflows that enable coding agents to work effectively across the development lifecycle, from implementation and testing to debugging and deployment.

  • Cost optimisation: develop caching, history compression and model selection, measuring savings while keeping estimated costs distinct from actual spend.

  • Usage and billing: build accurate accounting for model calls, usage reports, plan entitlements and invoice reconciliation.

  • Agent infrastructure and integrations: support tool calls, cost limits, human approvals and runs that can recover safely from interruptions, alongside connectors for services such as Gmail, Slack and calendars.

  • Tenancy and secrets: maintain workspace isolation, secure authentication and encrypted customer key management.

  • European infrastructure and model serving: build and operate our cloud infrastructure, including the GPU capacity used to serve open-weight models.

  • Production reliability: make systems observable, migrations reversible and releases safe, with tests that protect data integrity and logs that keep customer content and secrets private.
column5:
>

The platform will evolve quickly. You will need to move comfortably between improving what exists and learning enough about a new problem to build the next piece well.
column6:
>

Our Stack

Our backend is built in Python, with a TypeScript frontend in a shared monorepo.

  • Backend: Python, FastAPI, Pydantic and LiteLLM.

  • Data and queues: Postgres with row-level security and pgvector, Redis and arq.

  • Frontend: Next.js, React and TypeScript.

  • Cloud and infrastructure: Scaleway, Terraform and Kubernetes for GPU workloads.

  • Auth and secrets: Zitadel, Secret Manager and KMS.

  • Observability and testing: OpenTelemetry, Langfuse, Sentry, pytest and testcontainers, alongside frontend testing tools.

You should be comfortable with the core backend technologies and ready to learn the rest as the work requires.
column7:
>

About You

You enjoy the craft of engineering and the responsibility of seeing your work used in production. Faced with an unclear problem, you can identify what matters, make sensible trade-offs and carry a solution through to release without someone planning every step. You naturally look for ways to multiply your output through agentic workflows, rather than approaching every engineering task as something to execute manually.

We are looking for:

  • Experience building and operating production systems: several years of backend engineering with real users, typically three to six, and meaningful ownership of what you shipped.

  • Strong Python fundamentals: confidence with async code, typing and testing. TypeScript experience is a plus.

  • Agentic engineering as a default way of working: you have hands-on experience using coding agents as a core part of your engineering workflow. You know how to break down problems, delegate and parallelise tasks, provide the right context and build effective agentic workflows. Crucially, you have the technical depth to review, debug and take ownership of the resulting code.

  • Platform engineering depth: practical experience with Postgres, Redis, queues, networking and Terraform. Kubernetes experience is useful, particularly for our GPU infrastructure.

  • Sound engineering judgement: clear APIs, tenant isolation, data integrity, partial failure and safe rollouts. You can explain both your decisions and what you chose to leave out.

  • A working understanding of ML systems: familiarity with LLMs, embeddings, evals, model serving and fine-tuning. Experience with LLM APIs, streaming and token costs is a strong plus.

  • A disciplined approach to measurement: you benchmark changes, question assumptions and use evidence to understand whether an improvement holds up.

  • Initiative and drive: you enjoy getting deep into a problem, finding a way forward and putting in the work to make it happen.

  • This is an experienced individual-contributor role, with ownership of the capabilities you build and close collaboration across the founding team.

  • Fluent English is required

Frontier labs naturally put their own models first. Companies often follow suit, asking one general-purpose model to handle ten very different jobs. We believe there is far more to unlock in the models that already exist.

We bring closed providers and open-weight models together behind a single API. Our engine breaks requests into their component parts, routes each to the right model within a cost budget, fine-tunes on customer data and checks the results against agreed quality standards. With no proprietary model to promote, we can choose the best combination for each task.

Lower costs matter because of what they make possible: giving a small team the freedom to build something that would previously have required a much larger one.

Our founder was selected for Slush 20 Under 20, awarded by Anthropic, Slush, Index Ventures and Sifted. We closed our pre-seed round in two weeks and already have people waiting to use the product. We're now looking for a technical co-founder to help turn this opportunity into a company.
column3:

About the Role

As Technical Co-Founder, you will lead the development of our AI efficiency engine, working alongside the founder to turn a compelling technical opportunity into a product.
column4:
>

At the heart of the role is a deceptively simple question: how can we make AI models deliver the same or better results at a fraction of the cost?

You will explore approaches to model routing, fine-tuning, caching and inference optimisation, combining scientific curiosity with the ability to turn promising ideas into measurable improvements.

This is a role for someone who enjoys difficult technical problems, rigorous experimentation and challenging existing approaches. You won't be expected to build every part of the platform yourself. Working alongside our founding AI engineer and backend platform engineer, you will set the technical direction and focus your expertise where it creates the greatest impact.

Agentic engineering is central to how we work. We're looking for someone who already operates this way, using coding agents and developing the workflows and harnesses that allow a small team to move exceptionally quickly without compromising technical quality.

Above all, this is a co-founder role. We're looking for someone who wants to take genuine ownership, work with relentless intensity and help build a company from its earliest stages.
column5:

What You'll Work On

  • Drive AI cost efficiency: develop approaches to reducing inference costs through model selection, routing, caching, fine-tuning, quantization and other optimisation techniques.

  • Experiment and benchmark: design rigorous evaluations to understand the trade-offs between cost, quality and latency, turning technical insights into measurable improvements.

  • Shape the efficiency engine: determine how closed and open-weight models can be combined and optimised to deliver the best outcomes for different tasks.

  • Set technical direction: identify promising opportunities, make key architectural decisions and guide the founding engineers in bringing them to production.

  • Push agentic engineering forward: use coding agents as a core part of your work and develop the harnesses and workflows that allow a small team to operate with exceptional leverage.

  • Build the company: work closely with the founder on technical strategy, attract exceptional talent and help shape the product and business.
column6:

About You

You bring deep technical curiosity, scientific rigour and an entrepreneurial mindset. You enjoy getting into the details, testing hypotheses and finding approaches others might overlook.

We're particularly interested in people who bring:

  • Deep expertise in AI efficiency: meaningful experience optimising the cost or performance of LLMs or other AI systems, with concrete results to show for it. Experience in inference optimisation, routing, fine-tuning or related techniques is particularly relevant.

  • Strong technical foundations: a solid understanding of modern AI models, rigorous experimentation and the ability to translate research into practical improvements.

  • An agentic approach to engineering: you actively use coding agents, know how to orchestrate them effectively and are excited by what small, highly leveraged teams can achieve.

  • A co-founder mindset: you're resourceful, ambitious and comfortable with uncertainty. You take initiative, move quickly and want to build something from the ground up.

  • Technical leadership potential: you have the judgement to make difficult technical decisions and guide others. Previous CTO or engineering management experience is not required.

We're more interested in exceptional depth in AI efficiency and the ambition to build a company than a conventional CTO background.

Fluent English is required

The SandboxAQ AI team is looking for a hands-on Manager, AI Engineering to help us build the future of agentic collaboration, trust and ROI. Our goal is to make agents work well on their own, in teams, and with humans. This includes the following aspects:

12-month fixed-term contract | Global Revenue Systems and AI Team |


About the Role

Our reps spend most of their day in Salesforce, and how it feels to use directly affects how much they sell. We're hiring a Salesforce Developer with a UI/UX focus to redesign the rep experience across our Sales and Revenue teams. You'll join the global Salesforce team for 12 months to make the CRM faster, clearer and more intuitive.

This is a hands-on build role. You'll design the experience and code it in Lightning Web Components, working with Sales, RevOps, Marketing and Data, and directly with the reps who use the result.


What You Will Do


Redesign the rep experience

  • Audit the current Lightning experience (record pages, console apps, list views, home pages) and find where reps lose time to clicks, clutter and missing context.

  • Turn what you find into a prioritised roadmap of UI improvements tied to rep productivity and adoption.

  • Design and prototype improved layouts, workflows and components, and validate them with reps before building.

Build with LWC

  • Develop custom Lightning Web Components (and supporting Apex where needed) that replace clunky standard layouts with focused, usable interfaces.

  • Configure and extend Lightning App Builder pages, Dynamic Forms, Dynamic Actions and console apps to deliver a consistent experience across teams and regions.

  • Build reusable components and follow SLDS conventions so the UI stays consistent and maintainable after your contract ends.

Make it stick

  • Run feedback sessions, usability tests and pilots with reps and managers, and iterate on the results.

  • Track adoption, page performance and user satisfaction to show what each release changed.

  • Create release notes, short walkthroughs and handover documentation so changes land well and the team can maintain what you build.

Work as part of the global team

  • Work within the global team's standards for source control, code review, sandboxes and release management.

  • Partner with admins, architects and data teams so UI changes fit the wider data model, security model and automation.

  • Pass on what you learn about Lightning UX patterns and LWC best practices to the wider team.


What You Will Need


Must have

Overview

This critical role sits at the intersection of Data Engineering and Data Analytics, focusing on transforming raw data into high-quality, trustworthy, and easily consumable datasets and visualisations for business users. The ideal candidate will possess a strong background in SQL, dbt, data modelling, ETL/ELT principles and experience with modern cloud data platforms.

Core Responsibilities

Develop and Maintain Transformation best practices in ELT Pipelines: Design, develop, and maintain efficient and scalable workflows using tools like dbt to transform raw data loaded into our data warehouse (Snowflake) into clean, ready-to-use data models.

Data Modelling: Implement best-practice data modelling and software engineering techniques to ensure data structures are optimised for performance, accuracy, and ease of use in reporting and analytical applications (e.g. CI/CD, testing, lineage).

Data Quality and Testing: Write comprehensive data quality checks, tests, and monitoring scripts to ensure the accuracy, completeness, and reliability of all transformed data assets. Establish and maintain documentation for all data transformations and models.

Collaboration: Work closely with Data Analysts and business users to understand their reporting needs and optimise data models to support their analytical use cases. Collaborate with Data Engineers on data ingestion strategies and platform optimisation.

Performance Optimisation: Tune and optimise SQL queries and data models to reduce latency and improve the performance of our data warehouse and downstream applications.

Tool Adoption: Champion the adoption of modern data stack tools and practices (e.g. Git, CI/CD).

Build scalable, compelling data visualisations in Looker that can be used by large teams.

Required Qualifications

  • Experience: Multiple years of experience in a data-focused role (e.g., Analytics Engineer, Data Analyst, BI Developer).

  • SQL Mastery: Expert-level proficiency in writing and optimising complex SQL queries.

  • Data Transformation Tooling: Hands-on experience with dbt (Data Build Tool) or similar data transformation frameworks is essential.

  • Data Warehousing: Experience working with cloud-based data warehouses such as Snowflake, Google BigQuery, or Amazon Redshift.

  • Data modelling: Solid understanding of data warehousing concepts, ETL/ELT principles, and dimensional modelling techniques.

  • Version Control: Proficiency with Git for collaborative development and version control.

  • Familiarity with reporting/ BI tools like Looker.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Python expertise for automation, integration, and orchestration

  • Experience with Semantic layers

  • Experience with orchestration tools like Airflow.

  • Knowledge of modern software engineering practices applied to data (e.g., modularity, code review, testing).

  • Write the code the job needs - Python, SQL, SOQL or TypeScript.

  • Set clear ownership, and the review discipline that makes shipping fast also means shipping safely.

  • Grow the team's technical depth and commercial judgement in equal measure.

  • Deep background across Revenue Operations, GTM Engineering, Sales Systems, Growth Engineering, or an adjacent technical commercial function in B2B SaaS

You'll be selling a product, not a service, into CISOs, security engineers and AppSec leads, which means the pitch has to work on its own merits rather than on brand recognition. This is a full-cycle closing role: you'll run discovery, demo and negotiation yourself, with support from the CRO on the harder deals while you build that muscle.

You'll carry mid-market opportunities to start, working alongside SDR-sourced pipeline as well as your own prospecting, with a clear path to Senior Account Executive as your quota, deal complexity and independence grow.

What you'll do

  • Run full-cycle new-logo opportunities from qualified meeting through discovery, demo and close, sourced by SDR, Marketing and your own prospecting.

  • Generate some of your own pipeline alongside SDR support, prospecting into a clearly defined ideal customer profile.

  • Run structured discovery calls solo, identifying pain and priorities for your primary buyer.

  • Close mid-market deals with negotiation support from the CRO as you build experience with more complex procurement.

  • Maintain your own weekly pipeline and forecast, developing commit accuracy over time.

  • Work SDR and Customer Success handoffs as directed, keeping CRM records clean and up to date.


What you'll bring

  • 3–5 years' full-cycle closing experience in B2B SaaS, or a strong track record in an adjacent commercial role (for example SDR) ready to step up.

  • A track record at or near 100% of quota (around £500k–£750k) in at least one of the last two years.

  • Real consultative selling instinct: you'd rather understand a prospect's problem than run a script at them.

  • Comfortable prospecting and selling into accounts with little existing awareness of Cytix, energised by the challenge of a cold or lightly-worked start.

  • Visible drive and competitiveness, and a willingness to take on unfamiliar deal types or buyer personas when asked.

  • Genuinely bright and inquisitive: good follow-up questions come naturally to you, and you're genuinely curious about the product and the security market, including how software gets built and secured.

  • Drawn to a business where new challenges show up daily

    • Time off that works for you: Unlimited holiday policy, including a guaranteed 33 days plus your birthday off

    • Flexible hybrid working: Work in a way that helps you do your best work, while staying connected with the team.

    • A stake in what we’re building: Eligible employees can participate in our EMI share option scheme.

    • Healthcare that goes further: After one year’s service, access private healthcare through Vitality, including dental, optical, hearing and therapy cover.

    • More ways to get around: Access our company car salary-sacrifice scheme.

    • Support for growing families: Enhanced maternity and paternity leave.

    About Cytix

    Software never stops changing. Teams ship new code every day, through tickets, pull requests, releases, and increasingly with AI in the mix, but the way security keeps up with all that change hasn't really moved on.

    That's the problem we're solving. Cytix helps organisations understand which software changes actually matter, what should happen next, and how to prove the right call was made. Security understood, in other words.

    We're a small team with big plans, so every person we hire genuinely shapes what Cytix becomes. Contexte de la mission

Dans le cadre d'un programme de construction d'une nouvelle usine industrielle à l'international, prévu sur la période 2028-2032, nous recherchons un profil expérimenté pour intervenir en phase amont d'analyse des besoins et de pré-FEED (Front-End Engineering Design).

La mission consiste à réaliser un audit approfondi de deux usines de production existantes, l'une en France et l'autre en Amérique du Nord, afin d'identifier les bonnes pratiques, les axes d'amélioration et les besoins des différents services.

L'objectif est de recueillir et de formaliser l'ensemble des exigences techniques, fonctionnelles et opérationnelles dans un cahier des charges aussi complet que possible, afin de sécuriser les futures phases d'ingénierie, de conception et de construction de la nouvelle usine.

Missions

  • Organiser et animer des groupes de travail avec l'ensemble des services concernés, notamment :

    • Maintenance

    • Exploitation et production

    • Process industriels

    • Traitement de l'air

  • Conduire des entretiens et des réunions de travail, notamment à distance via Teams, afin de faire émerger les besoins, contraintes et attentes de chaque service.

  • Challenger les interlocuteurs pour identifier les besoins explicites et implicites, anticiper les problématiques et garantir l'exhaustivité des exigences.

  • Recueillir, analyser et consolider les retours d'expérience des deux sites existants.

  • Identifier les exigences techniques, fonctionnelles, organisationnelles et opérationnelles à intégrer dans la conception de la future usine.

  • Définir les besoins d'industrialisation et les exigences relatives aux process de production.

  • Élaborer et structurer un cahier des charges (CDC) complet et détaillé, intégrant les besoins de l'ensemble des parties prenantes.

  • Rédiger les User Requirement Specifications (URS) afin de formaliser les exigences utilisateurs.

  • Participer à la phase de pré-FEED et contribuer à la définition des orientations techniques du futur site industriel.

  • Assurer la cohérence et l'exhaustivité des exigences afin de limiter les oublis, les modifications tardives et les risques lors des phases ultérieures du projet.

  • Faciliter les échanges entre les différents métiers et accompagner la convergence des besoins vers des spécifications communes.

🚀 Apporteur d’affaires indépendant — Développez votre réseau avec PropertyOS

100 % à distance · Organisation libre · Commission sur les ventes issues de vos recommandations

Vous aimez créer des contacts, repérer des opportunités et mettre les bonnes personnes en relation ?

Avec PropertyOS, vous identifiez des propriétaires, bailleurs ou petites agences intéressés par une gestion immobilière plus simple. Vous organisez le rendez-vous : le fondateur assure la démonstration et le closing.

🏡 PropertyOS, c’est quoi ?

PropertyOS est une plateforme SaaS qui centralise les biens immobiliers, les locataires, les finances, les documents et les tâches dans un même espace.

Notre ambition : permettre aux propriétaires et gestionnaires de gagner du temps et de garder une vision claire de leur activité immobilière.

La plateforme est accessible directement en ligne. Nous développons également un réseau de partenaires indépendants pour la faire découvrir à de nouveaux clients grâce à une approche plus personnelle.

🎯 Votre mission : créer des opportunités qualifiées

Votre rôle consiste à :

  • Identifier des propriétaires bailleurs, investisseurs et petites agences susceptibles d’être intéressés.

  • Entrer en contact avec eux et comprendre leur organisation actuelle.

  • Présenter simplement PropertyOS et son intérêt.

  • Vérifier leur intérêt pour une démonstration et pour le budget proposé.

  • Organiser un rendez-vous avec le fondateur.

  • Enregistrer les informations utiles dans PropertyOS Advisor pour préparer l’échange.

Vous vous concentrez sur la prospection et la mise en relation. Le fondateur prend ensuite le relais pour la démonstration détaillée, les questions commerciales, la négociation et la conclusion de l’abonnement.

Vous ne négociez pas les conditions et ne signez pas de contrat au nom de PropertyOS.

⚡ PropertyOS Advisor : votre application partenaire

Vous disposez de PropertyOS Advisor, notre application dédiée aux apporteurs d’affaires.

Pensée pour fluidifier votre activité, elle vous permet de centraliser les informations de vos prospects, suivre vos mises en relation et transmettre le contexte nécessaire à la préparation des rendez-vous.

L’objectif : une prospection organisée et un passage de relais simple, pour donner à chaque opportunité les meilleures chances d’aboutir.

💸 Une rémunération liée aux clients apportés

L’offre mise en avant dans ce partenariat est l’abonnement annuel PropertyOS à 990 €.

Vous percevez une commission pour chaque nouveau client qui souscrit et règle cet abonnement à la suite de votre mise en relation, selon les conditions prévues au contrat.

  • Rémunération à la commission uniquement.

  • Aucun salaire fixe ni revenu garanti.

  • Le montant de la commission et le calendrier de versement sont communiqués avant tout engagement.

  • Les règles d’attribution des prospects, de traitement des doublons et d’annulation sont précisées au contrat.

  • Un rendez-vous seul ne déclenche pas de commission : celle-ci dépend de la souscription et de l’encaissement correspondants.

👋 À qui s’adresse cette opportunité ?

À des personnes autonomes, à l’aise dans les échanges et capables de créer un premier contact de qualité.

Vous pouvez avoir une expérience commerciale, un réseau dans l’immobilier ou simplement une vraie capacité à prospecter avec méthode.

Nous recherchons surtout :

  • De l’écoute, pour repérer un besoin réel.

  • De la clarté, pour expliquer la solution sans faire de promesses excessives.

  • De la régularité, pour développer votre activité.

  • De la rigueur, pour transmettre des informations fiables.

  • Un bon relationnel, pour représenter PropertyOS avec professionnalisme.

Une expérience en prospection, en immobilier ou dans le SaaS est un atout. Vous n’avez pas besoin d’être un expert du logiciel ni un closer confirmé.

🌴 Notre culture : détendue, directe et orientée résultats

Chez PropertyOS, on apprécie les échanges simples, les idées utiles et les personnes qui prennent des initiatives.

Vous organisez librement votre activité : pas d’horaires imposés ni de volume hebdomadaire obligatoire. Cette collaboration peut compléter d’autres activités professionnelles.

Notre façon d’avancer : partager les retours du terrain, améliorer les approches et privilégier des mises en relation pertinentes.

Une ambiance chill, des engagements tenus et des opportunités concrètes.

🤝 Pour bien démarrer

La prise en main comprend :

  • Une présentation de PropertyOS et de ses principaux cas d’usage.

  • La découverte de PropertyOS Advisor.

  • Des repères pour identifier les profils de clients recherchés.

  • Des supports pour présenter la solution.

  • Une explication du processus de mise en relation et de rémunération.

Vous avez un interlocuteur direct pour transmettre vos questions et vos retours.

📋 Cadre de la collaboration

Nature : partenariat indépendant d’apport d’affaires, sans contrat de travail.
Lieu : à distance, depuis la France.
Organisation : libre, sans exclusivité.
Démarrage : à convenir ensemble.

Vous devez disposer d’une activité indépendante déclarée et d’un SIRET pour exercer depuis la France. La micro-entreprise est une possibilité.

Vous pouvez candidater avant d’avoir créé votre activité, mais les formalités nécessaires devront être réalisées pour démarrer la collaboration.

Un contrat écrit définit les missions, les commissions et les conditions du partenariat.

🚀 Intéressé ? Présentez-vous simplement.

Envoyez-nous quelques lignes sur :

  • Votre parcours et votre éventuelle expérience en prospection.

  • Les types de prospects que vous pourriez contacter.

Omnea is the agentic operating system for procurement.

Procurement touches every pound a business spends, yet requests still stall for weeks and approvals get lost in inboxes. Maintenance Engineer DSL-01, you are responsible for building and continuously improving the facility's maintenance, reliability, and asset integrity framework. Reporting to the Engineering Manager, you help ensure the plant operates safely, reliably, and efficiently.

The role starts with a strong Maintenance Engineering focus. Your priority will be to help establish the maintenance and reliability foundation of DSL-01 by answering a fundamental question: ""how do we maintain our assets safely, reliably, and efficiently throughout their lifecycle?""

You will translate reliability studies, equipment criticality assessments, and integrity requirements into practical maintenance plans, inspection programmes, spare parts strategies, and asset management processes.

As the facility moves into stable operations, the focus gradually shifts towards Reliability Engineering, where you will use asset health monitoring, root cause analysis, and continuous improvement to prevent failures and improve long-term asset performance.

Working closely with operations, maintenance, engineering, and external specialists, you will help reduce technical risk and improve asset reliability from day one.

You will:

  • Develop and continuously improve maintenance, inspection, and asset integrity strategies

  • Translate reliability studies, FMECA analyses, and engineering data into practical maintenance plans within the CMMS/EAM system

  • Act as owner of the asset register from a maintenance, reliability, and integrity perspective

  • Support the implementation and continuous development of the facility's CMMS/EAM system

  • Drive reliability improvements through asset health monitoring, KPI analysis, and predictive maintenance techniques

  • Lead Root Cause Analyses (RCA) and implement sustainable corrective actions

  • Monitor and improve reliability performance indicators such as MTBF, MTTR, availability, and inspection compliance

  • Support asset improvement, modification, and long-term replacement strategies throughout the asset lifecycle

Your profile

As a growing company in a rapidly evolving industry, we are looking for people who embrace change and are motivated to actively contribute to building and scaling our business. You are someone who feels comfortable in an entrepreneurial environment, takes ownership, and enjoys turning complex technical challenges into practical solutions.

You recognize yourself in the following:

Must have

  • Fluent in Dutch and English

  • Bachelor's degree in a relevant engineering discipline (i.e. electrical or mechanical)

  • 5+ years of experience in Reliability Engineering, Maintenance Engineering, Asset Integrity, or Asset Management

  • Experience with RCM, FMEA/FMECA, RCA, and maintenance strategy development

  • Experience with CMMS/EAM systems such as SAP PM, Maximo, or IFS

Preferred

  • Experience in chemical, petrochemical, energy, or other process industries like food or FMCG

  • Experience with CMMS/EAM implementation or optimisation

  • Experience with predictive maintenance and condition monitoring

  • Knowledge of ATEX, PED, and asset integrity management

About DSL-01

DSL-01 is SkyNRG’s frontrunning renewable fuels facility in Delfzijl, Netherlands. The plant will produce Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) from residual fats and greases using the HEFA (Hydrotreated Esters and Fatty Acids) pathway, with additional renewable products like butane, propane, and naphtha as by-products.

DSL-01 is the first facility in Europe dedicated entirely to SAF and its by-products. Once operational, it will produce 100,000 tonnes of SAF and 35,000 tonnes of sustainable by-products per year, cutting greenhouse gas emissions by around 80% compared to conventional jet fuel.

Construction started in 2026, with first fuel expected in 2028. The project includes the main facility, pipelines, and temporary work areas. At DSL-01, you will be part of a team building a state-of-the-art industrial plant from the ground up, contributing to a truly sustainable energy future.

Environmental and social responsibility are at the heart of DSL-01. We follow international frameworks and Dutch regulations to manage impacts on people, nature, and local communities. Safety, sustainability, and collaboration guide everything we do.

Bij DeWarmte maken we slimme en betaalbare warmtepompen waarmee we woningen van het gas af helpen. We ontwerpen onze producten zelf, assembleren ze in Utrecht en zorgen samen met onze installatiepartners dat ze bij steeds meer mensen thuis komen te staan.

We groeien hard. Tot nu toe worden al onze warmtepompen geïnstalleerd door externe partners, maar daar komt verandering in. We gaan onze eigen installatieteams opbouwen en zoeken daarom een Hoofdmonteur Warmtepompen die hierin het voortouw neemt.

Je bent een ervaren monteur die graag zelf de handen uit de mouwen steekt, maar ook energie krijgt van het begeleiden van anderen. Je gaat samen met je team op pad, bent verantwoordelijk voor de kwaliteit van de installaties en helpt ons om steeds meer monteurs op te leiden.

Je komt dus niet in een bestaand team terecht. Je helpt het team zelf opbouwen.

Wat ga je doen?

Als Hoofdmonteur ben je verantwoordelijk voor de installatie van onze warmtepompen bij klanten thuis. Je begint met het leiden van ons eerste interne installatieteam en helpt ons om de komende jaren onze eigen installatiecapaciteit verder uit te bouwen.

Je installeert warmtepompen en leidt je team

  • Je gaat samen met een collega-monteur op pad om onze warmtepompen bij klanten thuis te installeren.

  • Je bent verantwoordelijk voor de volledige installatie, van de technische uitvoering en het oplossen van onverwachte problemen tot de oplevering.

  • Je zorgt dat installaties veilig, efficiënt en volgens onze kwaliteitsstandaarden worden uitgevoerd.

  • Je bent het aanspreekpunt voor de klant tijdens de installatie. Je legt uit wat jullie doen, beantwoordt vragen en zorgt dat de klant met een goed gevoel achterblijft.

  • Je stemt waar nodig af met onze werkvoorbereiders en collega's op kantoor over planning, materialen en technische uitdagingen.

Je bouwt mee aan ons interne installatieteam

  • Je begeleidt en traint nieuwe monteurs en helpt hen om zelfstandig installaties uit te kunnen voeren.

  • Je denkt mee over het aannemen van nieuwe collega's en hoe we ons installatieteam verder kunnen uitbreiden.

  • Je helpt onze installatiestandaarden en werkwijzen verder te ontwikkelen.

  • Je signaleert wat er in de praktijk beter of slimmer kan en neemt initiatief om dit te verbeteren.

  • Je deelt feedback vanuit het veld met onze engineers, werkvoorbereiders en productontwikkelaars, zodat we onze producten en installaties continu kunnen verbeteren.

Wie zoeken wij?

We zoeken iemand die zijn vak goed verstaat, verantwoordelijkheid neemt en het leuk vindt om anderen beter te maken. Je hoeft niet eerder een heel team te hebben opgebouwd, maar je moet wel zin hebben om die uitdaging aan te gaan.

  • Je hebt ruime ervaring met het installeren van warmtepompen, cv-installaties of andere verwarmingssystemen. Ervaring met warmtepompen heeft een sterke voorkeur.

  • Je hebt een goede technische basis in installatietechniek, elektrotechniek en/of werktuigbouwkunde.

  • Je kunt zelfstandig installaties uitvoeren, technische tekeningen lezen en onverwachte problemen oplossen.

  • Je hebt ervaring met het begeleiden van andere monteurs, of bent klaar om die verantwoordelijkheid op je te nemen.

  • Je werkt nauwkeurig en veilig en vindt het belangrijk om goed werk af te leveren.

  • Je communiceert makkelijk met klanten en collega's en kunt technische zaken begrijpelijk uitleggen.

  • Je neemt initiatief, denkt in oplossingen en voelt je verantwoordelijk voor het eindresultaat.

  • Je spreekt goed Nederlands en hebt rijbewijs B.

Een relevante mbo-opleiding en certificeringen zoals VCA, NEN 3140 of CO-vakmanschap zijn mooi meegenomen. Heb je nog niet alle benodigde certificaten? Dan kijken we samen wat je nog kunt behalen.

Wat bieden wij jou?

  • Een salaris van €4.000 tot €6.000 bruto per maand op basis van 40 uur, afhankelijk van je ervaring.

  • Een sleutelrol in ons bedrijf: je wordt de eerste Hoofdmonteur van ons interne installatieteam en helpt dit verder uit te bouwen.

  • Veel vrijheid en verantwoordelijkheid: je krijgt de ruimte om mee te denken over hoe we installeren, samenwerken en nieuwe monteurs opleiden.

  • Goed materiaal: een volledig uitgeruste werkbus en professioneel gereedschap.

  • 26 vakantiedagen en 13 ADV-dagen op basis van 40 uur, met de mogelijkheid om te kiezen voor een hogere beloning in plaats van ADV.

solution-engineer-i-amsterdam-134478,Mollie,Solution Engineer I,"

Build with us

Since 2004, we've had one clear goal: to make payments and money management effortless for every business in Europe.

Today, more than 250,000 companies use Mollie to get paid, manage money and grow – with products designed to be simple, scalable, and dependable.

With 950+ Mollies across 14+ locations, we care deeply about autonomy and craft. So we work in small teams, with real ownership, and we trust you to make the right decisions.

We're building for the long term, so we provide the tools you need, processes you can rely on, and a balanced work environment to help you do work you're proud of.

Sound like your kind of place? Let's build together.

Your impact

As a Solutions Engineer I in the Connect team, you'll support the partners who bring processing volume to Mollie, think SaaS platforms and marketplaces. Your core activities are discovery, solution design, and implementation support for partner deals, the work that turns a promising conversation into a working integration.

Beyond the deal itself, you'll join forecasting meetings with the Connect leadership team to give an honest, objective view of technical deal health, and you'll have regular one-on-ones with the partner acquisition managers you support to align on deal details and next steps. You'll also support events and pitches for the commercial team and contribute to process improvement and internal product feedback, so the lessons from one deal make the next one easier.

Solutions Engineers are the bridge between technical and commercial teams at Mollie. Strong discovery means partners get solutions that actually fit, pricing negotiations become smoother, and partner needs and product issues make their way back into the business. That's a direct line to how Mollie expands into new products and partner segments.

What you'll ship

  • Lead technical discovery sessions to deeply understand and map complex merchant requirements.

  • Design and present tailored payment solutions, clearly mapping Mollie’s APIs and products to specific business needs.

  • Build and deliver custom demos, proof-of-concepts (POCs), and technical workshops that prove our value.

  • Act as the technical expert in the room, partnering with Account Executives to overcome objections and close strategic deals.

  • Collaborate directly with Product and Engineering teams, channeling critical merchant feedback to help shape our product roadmap.

What you'll bring

  • 2 to 3+ years of experience in a customer-facing, technical role.

  • Customer-facing experience with a technical product, such as pre-sales, solutions engineering, sales engineering, or technical customer success

  • Comfortable working with APIs, with the ability to demo and build solutions on top of them

  • Strong discovery skills: understanding what a partner needs and judging what's feasible with the product

  • Ability to explain a complex product, including payment methods, sub-products, and the Connect proposition, to both technical and commercial audiences

  • Experience working with both internal and external senior executives stakeholders

  • A technically curious, commercially minded, and customer-minded approach, with clear rules of engagement, comfortable saying no and pushing back when needed

Grow your way

At Mollie, growth is personal. We believe everyone should have the chance to develop their skills, explore new challenges and shape their career on their own terms.

You'll get regular feedback and performance reviews to support your development, with fair and transparent salary reviews along the way. Many Mollies move into new roles or take on new projects to stretch themselves, and we actively hire from within to help you take the next step.

No matter if you're aiming for promotion, exploring a different career path or building new skills, you'll be supported with the tools, trust and opportunities to grow your way.

Unlock your full potential and join us to eliminate financial bureaucracy

If you're excited by the idea of building what's next, for yourself and for thousands of businesses across Europe, we'd love to hear from you. Apply with your CV (in English) using the form below.

Want a peek behind the scenes? Check out what life at Mollie is really like.

AI at Mollie

We believe in Always Be Shipping, and AI brings that philosophy to life across every team, every role, every day.

AI is core to how we build. It helps us move faster, simplify work and make smarter decisions, creating real impact for the businesses we serve. We're looking for people who are excited to use AI to shape the future of finance with us.

At Graviton, we don't believe the best trading strategies come from following established playbooks. They come from asking better questions. Why does a pattern exist? What is driving it? Is it real or just noise? Can it be explained, modelled and turned into an edge?

As a Quantitative Researcher, you'll work on those questions every day. You'll investigate market behaviour, develop quantitative models, build and test hypotheses and turn insights into trading strategies, working alongside researchers and technologists in an environment where an idea on a whiteboard can reach live trading quickly.
This isn't a role where the answers are in a textbook. The problems are open-ended, the data is enormous, and finding the answers is the job.
Ideal candidates are rigorous thinkers who genuinely enjoy mathematics, programming and figuring out things that aren't obvious, based in our Singapore, London, Amsterdam or US offices.

You'll work across quantitative research and systematic trading, taking ideas through the full lifecycle: question, hypothesis, experiment, model, validation, strategy, production. Depending on your team and research interests, your work would include:
• Discovering predictive patterns and sources of alpha from billions of market events
• Formulating hypotheses about market behaviour and designing experiments to test them
• Applying probability, statistics, optimization and machine learning to build predictive models and quantitative signals for systematic trading
• Designing robust backtests and statistical tests to distinguish genuine signals from noise
• Working with large and complex datasets to uncover patterns that aren't immediately visible
• Investigating market microstructure and how markets behave at different timescales
• Evaluating strategy performance, identifying weaknesses and continuously refining models
• Developing research infrastructure and AI-powered tools and agents that make experimentation faster and analysis deeper
• Working closely with technologists to translate research ideas into efficient, production-ready systems
• Exploring new techniques in machine learning, statistics and quantitative finance to uncover new sources of edge
No two research problems are the same. Good research finds patterns. Great research understands why they exist.

Successful researchers at Graviton discover new sources of alpha and turn them into robust trading strategies, build models that hold up under real market conditions and not only in backtests, develop a deep understanding of market behaviour, create research frameworks and tools that make the broader team more effective, work with technologists to take ideas from research into production, and communicate complex quantitative ideas clearly and rigorously. Your impact isn't measured by how many models you build. It's measured by the quality of the ideas you discover and what those ideas enable.
We're looking for exceptional problem solvers who genuinely enjoy mathematics, programming and figuring out things that aren't obvious.
• Degree in a quantitative discipline such as mathematics, physics, computer science, statistics, operations research or machine learning
• Strong programming skills in Python and/or C++

• Solid grounding in probability, statistics, linear algebra and optimization, with experience in machine learning, statistical modelling or data analysis, whether through coursework, research or personal projects
• Comfort working with large, complex datasets, and strong analytical thinking
• A passion for applying quantitative thinking and rigorous research to solve open-ended problems in markets
• Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain complex ideas clearly

Prior exposure to quantitative research, algorithmic trading, market microstructure, competitive mathematics or machine learning is valuable, but we care more about how you think than whether you've worked in finance before.

More than specific tools or techniques, we care how you think. We look for people who are curious enough to keep asking why, analytical enough to separate signal from noise, persistent enough to pursue difficult problems, intellectually honest enough to abandon an idea when the evidence says so, and humble enough to keep learning.

At Graviton, researchers sit alongside technologists on specialized trading teams that operate with significant autonomy. You'll have meaningful ownership of research problems from day one: forming your own hypotheses, challenging existing approaches and following the evidence wherever it leads, with the infrastructure and datasets to test ideas at scale, competitive compensation, and a culture where the best idea wins regardless of who proposed it.

Markets are among the most complex systems humans have ever created, and they never stop changing. Neither should our thinking. Every day, someone asks a better question and finds an answer nobody had. That someone could be you.

Wat ga je doen?

Samen met de CEO en COO werk je aan de verdere strategische en financiële ontwikkeling van de organisatie. Als CFO vertaal je de ondernemingsstrategie naar concrete groeikansen door schaalbare verdien- en prijsmodellen te ontwikkelen. Per markt, regio, entiteit, businessunit en klantsegment analyseer je waar kansen liggen, op basis van verwachte klantwaarde, omzetpotentieel, kosten, marge, cashflow, risico en schaalbaarheid. Deze inzichten verwerk je in businesscases waarin zowel het perspectief van de klant als van Voortman Steel Machinery naar voren komen.
column2: Daarnaast ontwikkel je heldere investeringskaders en breng je passende financieringsmodellen in kaart die aansluiten op de aard van de activiteiten en de internationale context. Daarbij weeg je beschikbare financieringsopties zorgvuldig af op impact, liquiditeit en rendement. Op basis daarvan adviseer je de board over prioriteiten en zorg je dat middelen terechtkomen bij de initiatieven die het meest bijdragen aan de strategische en financiële doelstellingen van Voortman Steel Machinery. Als onderdeel hiervan bepaal je ook onder welke financiële en organisatorische voorwaarden pilots kunnen worden gestart en opgeschaald. Met heldere go/no-go-momenten per fase zorg je ervoor dat de ontwikkeling en implementatie van nieuwe verdien- en prijsmodellen niet sneller gaat dan wat de organisatie kan adopteren. Daarnaast monitor je de financiële resultaten van nieuwe verdien- en prijsmodellen en bepaal je of de uitrol moet worden versneld, voortgezet, bijgestuurd of afgeschaald. Tegelijkertijd borg je dat contracten allesomvattende afspraken en een evenwichtige risicoverdeling bevatten, evenals uitvoerbaar zijn in alle landen waar Voortman Steel Machinery actief is. Zo werk je gericht aan verdien- en prijsmodellen die commercieel aantrekkelijk, financieel gezond en schaalbaar zijn.

About BSI

BSI Merch & Artist Services runs design, supply, fulfilment and e-commerce for artists and their labels and management. We build and run official artist web stores on Shopify for the UK and EU, ship from our warehouses in Leamington Spa and Berlin, and support album campaigns from pre-order through to release week, for artists including Franz Ferdinand, Kneecap, Frank Turner and We Are Palace.

Every order through those stores is a fan buying something from an artist they care about. Customer Services is where that relationship is won or lost.

The Role

You'll answer customers across our artist stores, resolve order, delivery and returns issues end to end, and feed what you learn back to the wider e-commerce team so problems get fixed at the source.

What we are looking for

You bring professional experience in customer service, clear communication skills, and a practical approach to resolving support requests in a fast-paced environment.

Key Responsibilities

Customer support

  • Respond to customer tickets by email and chat through Gorgias, across multiple artist stores and in each store's tone.

  • Handle order queries end to end: tracking, delivery delays, address changes, missing items, pre-order dates and cancellations.

  • Manage returns, exchanges, refunds and reships, including damaged and faulty items, collecting photo evidence and processing returns through Loop Returns.

  • Resolve complaints fairly and within our service standards (acknowledgement within 2 working days, resolution within 14 calendar days), escalating to the CS Lead where needed.

  • Apply UK and EU consumer rights correctly, including the 14-day cancellation period and its exceptions.

Working with the wider team

  • Chase stock and fulfilment issues with the warehouse and Product team, and flag anything that needs a reship or a hold on stock.

  • Raise patterns early to the Head of Customer Service and/or relevant department

Housekeeping and reporting

  • Keep the queue clean: tag tickets accurately, close spam and auto-replies, and keep macros and Help Centre articles up to date where required.

  • Log refunds, reships, common issues and recurring problems so they feed into the monthly CS report for each client.

  • Help maintain and improve the AI Agent's guidance and the CS Help Centre for new stores.

Launches and release weeks

Our workload follows the music. A store launch, a pre-sale or an album release can bring hundreds of tickets in a few days, and the questions shift with each stage of the campaign.

  • Pre-order and pre-access: questions about access codes, dispatch dates and what's included in bundles.

  • Release week: high volume around delivery timing, signed items and chart-eligible bundles, where getting media to customers on time matters.

  • After release: returns, damaged items, missing parcels and reship requests.

You'll need to stay calm and accurate under pressure, prioritise the tickets that matter most, and occasionally flex your hours around a launch.

Skills and experience

Essential

  • At least 1 year in customer service, ideally for an e-commerce or retail brand.

  • Clear, warm written English and German, with the judgement to adjust tone for different artists and fanbases.

  • Comfortable working a busy ticket queue and hitting response times.

  • Organised and detail-focused: order numbers, SKUs, addresses and refunds need to be right first time.

  • Confident using helpdesk software and picking up new systems quickly.

  • Knows when to resolve and when to escalate.

Desirable

  • Experience with Gorgias, Shopify or Loop Returns.

  • Knowledge of UK and EU consumer rights for online purchases.

  • Experience in music, merchandise or entertainment retail.

  • An interest in music and the artists we work with.

What we offer

  • Work with a wide range of artists, from emerging acts to established names

  • A great, fast-growing team

  • A modern office in Kreuzberg

  • Discounts on a monthly BVG ticket and Urban Sports Club membership

Parallel treibst du unser zweites großes Thema voran: unser Warenwirtschaftssystem auf Automatisierungsniveau zu heben. Bestände, Beschaffung, Materialflüsse und Projektzuordnung sollen künftig KI-gestützt und weitgehend automatisch laufen statt manuell gepflegt zu werden.

Kurz gesagt: Du behandelst nicht nur die einzelnen Projekte – du behandelst die Warenwirtschaft selbst als Projekt. Wer bei uns Einblick will, wie ein Betrieb Schritt für Schritt KI-basiert aufgestellt wird, bekommt ihn hier aus der ersten Reihe.
• Projektbegleitung: Du unterstützt unseren Projektmanager im Tagesgeschäft – von der Auftragsübergabe über die Terminierung bis zur Fertigmeldung.
• Projektprüfung: Du gehst laufende Projekte gemeinsam mit ihm durch: Sind alle Unterlagen da? Stimmen Material, Termine und Kalkulation? Wo hakt es – und warum?
• Warenwirtschaft automatisieren: Du analysierst, wie unsere Warenwirtschaft heute läuft, findest die manuellen Bremsklötze und baust mit uns den Weg zur Automatisierung.
• KI & Tools einsetzen: Du testest und implementierst KI-gestützte Lösungen und Schnittstellen – von automatisierten Bestandsabgleichen bis zu Auswertungen, die vorher niemand hatte.
• Prozesse dokumentieren: Du hältst Abläufe sauber fest, damit aus Wissen im Kopf ein System wird, das auch ohne dich funktioniert.
• Auswertungen & Reporting: Du bereitest Zahlen so auf, dass Projektmanagement und Geschäftsführung schnell entscheiden können.

• Du bist eingeschriebener Student (m/w/d) – z. B. Wirtschaftsinformatik, BWL, Wirtschaftsingenieurwesen, Supply Chain / Logistik, Informatik oder ein vergleichbarer Studiengang. Wichtiger als der Titel ist, wie du denkst.

• Du arbeitest strukturiert, eigenständig und verbindlich – wenn du etwas zusagst, kommt es auch.
• Du bist kommunikativ und traust dich, im Team nachzuhaken, wenn Informationen fehlen.
• Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift.
• Du hast ca. 20 Stunden pro Woche Zeit (in der vorlesungsfreien Zeit gerne mehr) und willst länger als ein Semester bleiben.
Kein Muss: Vorkenntnisse in Photovoltaik. Die Technik bringen wir dir bei – Kopf und Motivation bringst du mit.

We're looking for an Engineering Manager to lead a Product Engineering team in our Automation Domain in Berlin.

The Automation Domain is responsible for building and owning Nelly’s SaaS and AI products - everything from onboarding new medical practices, the Doctor, Patient, and Back Office portals, to automating bureaucracy and practice workflows, and the AI Scribe, Billing Agent, and Treatment Plan generation products.

The role

You'll lead a fast moving AI enabled team that is building a new, but central, product. You’ll ensure the team is able to explore, experiment, and iterate quickly - testing new features and ideas internally and with our customers.

The product is new, giving you the opportunity to define the product with the team based on experimentation. The team needs to learn fast and be able to let go of ideas that don’t work. You’ll guide the team through this process, striving to improve how the team operates and enabling it to move faster.

The team is growing quickly, giving you an opportunity and responsibility to hiring a high performing team and define how it operates.

About Nelly

We are building the AI-Driven Financial Operating System for European healthcare, solving the biggest challenges for patients and practices. We create what no bank or software platform can handle. Our all-in-one platform transforms chaotic administrative processes into intelligent, automated workflows, from patient care to billing to next-generation payments. Because we truly believe: healthcare should be less about paperwork and more about people.

Why? Because Europe is facing a massive shortage of medical professionals. And if we don't rethink the way practices work, the system won't be able to keep up. With our Series B funding of over €50 million from world-class investors, we are turning our vision into reality.

What sets us apart: We work with the best team, which is why we give everything together every day. We believe in Talent Density, because exceptional people make everyone around them better. At Nelly, we move fast and expect everyone to keep up. Stagnation isn’t an option, which is why we invest heavily in growth. AI is an essential part of how we work at Nelly. We expect you to use it every day and give you everything you need to do so. You get trust and ownership and we expect you to speak up, even when it's uncomfortable.

What you'll do

  • Lead, inspire and grow a high-performing team of 3–6 software and AI engineers.

  • Collaborate closely with a product manager to iteratively build, launch, and improve new products

  • Own hiring for your team, building a team of high performing engineers.

  • Keep your team at the cutting edge of LLM and AI based engineering, testing new ideas and tech as it’s released

  • Own the quality, reliability, and security of your team’s products. Delivering high availability production systems

  • Stay hands on, developing with your team

  • Contribute to engineering-wide initiatives as a member of Nelly’s engineering leadership team

What we're looking for

  • 1+ years of experience as an Engineering Manager and 8+ years of overall experience in software development

  • A strong technical background, building customer facing products

  • Experience working in the TypeScript or similar ecosystems and a drive to proactively learn both.

About Allica Bank

Allica is the UK’s fastest growing company - and the fastest-growing financial technology (Fintech) firm ever. Our purpose is to help established SMEs, one of the last major underserved opportunities in Fintech.

Established SMEs are the backbone of local communities - representing over a third of our economy - yet have been largely neglected both by traditional high street banks and modern fintech providers.

Department Description

The Modelling team sits within the Credit Portfolio Management (CPM) function and is at the heart of building the measurement and decisioning models behind Allica’s lending products. The team builds and owns the bank’s IFRS9 model estate (including PD, LGD, SICR and economic response models), the statistical and machine learning models and credit policy rules used for automated underwriting, and the credit-linked GenAI solutions used to automate processes.

Role Description

This role will be part of the team building, implementing, monitoring and optimising two sets of models: the IFRS9 impairment models that measure our credit risk and support accurate reporting to auditors and investors, and the decisioning models and policy rules behind automated lending, which are critical to delivering fast, consistent and well-controlled credit decisions and a better customer journey as the bank grows.

The role requires the technical ability and practical mindset to take models and decisioning changes from initial problem definition through data identification, cleansing and analysis to model development, implementation and ongoing monitoring. The successful candidate will be comfortable moving between structured model development and fast-paced ad-hoc analysis, working closely with Finance, Credit Risk, Underwriting, Collections, Product, Data, Engineering, Capital Markets and Model Risk colleagues. They will communicate complex concepts clearly to stakeholders with different levels of technical expertise and work with third-party suppliers where required. We are looking for a hands-on modeller who can turn data into reliable, scalable solutions, and help make data a key strength for the bank.

Principal Accountabilities

  • Take a hands-on role in the design, build, implementation and continuous refinement of the bank’s credit risk models, spanning the full suite of IFRS9 impairment models (PD, LGD, SICR and economic response) and the statistical and machine learning models that support automated lending decisions.

  • Develop and deploy models in Python across the full model lifecycle, including data preparation, feature engineering, model fitting, validation, implementation and ongoing performance assessment.

  • Perform ad-hoc analysis to optimise credit policy rules and decisioning flows, using rule-firing, decision and outcome data to identify redundant, overlapping or mis-calibrated rules.

  • Produce regular monitoring, covering population stability, discriminatory power, calibration, and segment and vintage performance, as well as decision rates and alignment with underwriting outcomes for decisioning models.

  • Recalibrate or redevelop models as portfolio experience matures, comparing predicted and actual outcomes and adjusting model scaling, score cut-offs or policy thresholds where evidence of drift or mis-calibration exists.

  • Lead root-cause investigations into model, rule or decisioning-flow underperformance by tracing issues through decision logs, data lineage, feature calculations, production pipelines and implementation logic.

  • Build well-controlled, reproducible modelling processes and drive improvements to the data, tooling and infrastructure required for future model development and deployment.

  • Document models, rules, assumptions, limitations and changes to a high standard, supporting governance, independent review and validation, and stakeholder review.

  • Work closely with Credit Risk, Finance, Underwriting, Collections, Product, Data and Engineering teams to track model requirements and translate business needs into practical solutions, while complying with all mandatory policies and maintaining a strong internal control environment.

Hi, we’re Griffin. We’re a fully regulated UK bank that powers the accounts and payments offerings of product-led fintechs and platforms like Uber, Yonder, Prosper, and Sidekick. By doing the heavy lifting behind the scenes, our customers can focus on what they do best - delivering amazing customer experiences.

We’ve grown rapidly since our launch in 2024, and today provide the banking backbone behind products in remittance, payroll, wealth, insurance, proptech, payments, neobanking and more.

We’re moving into card issuing, stablecoin infrastructure, and agentic finance next as we continue to support the next generation of product-led companies.

Our culture

We believe that smart, motivated, conscientious people thrive in high-trust, high-autonomy environments and have done our best to create such an environment at Griffin. People who thrive here don’t require much hand-holding, and go out of their way to figure out how to contribute in the most valuable way possible.

We've been remote-first since we were established in 2017 and we remain so today. Work here is asynchronous and fully flexible - because we want to be a part of your life in a way that helps you to get the most out of both your work and home life.

We understand that our culture and ways of working aren’t for everyone, and we’re very intentional about our hiring process as a result. We won't hire people who don’t seem like a strong fit for our core values, even if they're otherwise extremely qualified.

Our strong culture has helped us to remain a mission-driven company as we have scaled, and gives our people a clear, explicit operating framework and the space to focus on delivering real value for our customers.

With card issuing and other launches coming up, there's plenty to get stuck into.

In your first year, you’ve taken ownership of our data protection agenda. You’ve gone looking for ways to improve, made the changes happen, and given our senior leaders an honest picture of where we stand. You’ve sought out our operations, sales and product teams and shown them that working with you makes things smoother, not slower. Now they bring you in early by default. You’ve guided at least one major launch, like card issuing, from first idea to go live. Support Engineer

Edinburgh

Wordsmith

Wordsmith is building the legal operating system for in-house teams, and we are growing fast.

We believe in-house legal is becoming one of the most important functions in the AI era. Every business is moving faster, but legal work is still too often scattered across inboxes, chats, documents and disconnected systems.

Wordsmith brings that work into one system. Requests come in from across the business, AI agents handle the routine, lawyers stay in control where judgement matters, and every step is captured as work happens.

We are built for in-house legal, not law firms. Our goal is to help legal teams move faster, reduce unnecessary external counsel spend and become a function the business can run with.

More than 500 companies, including Financial Times, Safelite, Trip.com, Canva, Starling and Sage, use Wordsmith. Backed by over $100M from Index Ventures, General Catalyst, Highland Europe and others, we are building one of the defining companies in legal AI.

The role

We’re hiring a Support Engineer to provide fast, thoughtful and technically rigorous help to Wordsmith customers.

You’ll own technical questions and incidents from first response through to resolution. You’ll understand what the customer is trying to achieve, reproduce reported behaviour, investigate the underlying cause and explain the outcome clearly.

This is more than scripted customer support. You’ll be expected to investigate application behaviour at a technical level, including reading logs and tracing issues through the product and its codebase. Where appropriate to your experience, you may also propose and submit code fixes through our normal engineering review and release process.

Wordsmith supports customers globally through a follow-the-sun model. You’ll work the standard hours for your region and hand over unresolved issues clearly to colleagues in other regions. There is no routine expectation that you work another region’s hours.

What you’ll do

  • Own technical support requests — triage, investigate and resolve customer questions and incidents from first response to confirmed resolution.

  • Diagnose problems thoroughly — gather the right context, reproduce reported behaviour, inspect logs and data, and trace issues through the product and codebase.

  • Resolve technical issues — correct configuration or usage problems directly and collaborate with Engineering when a product or infrastructure change is required.

  • Contribute code fixes where appropriate — depending on your experience, propose and submit well-tested fixes through the standard engineering review and deployment process.

  • Communicate clearly — give customers timely and accurate updates, explain technical issues without unnecessary jargon and set honest expectations.

  • Manage escalations — bring in Engineering, Product or other specialists when needed while retaining ownership of the case and its communication.

  • Support global handovers — document investigation, impact, current status and next actions so colleagues in another region can continue work without losing momentum.

  • Protect service quality — recognise high-impact incidents quickly, follow the appropriate escalation process and contribute to incident reviews.

  • Build customer knowledge — create and maintain troubleshooting guides, known-issue documentation and help-centre content.

  • Reduce repeat problems — identify patterns in support demand and recommend improvements to the product, documentation, tooling and customer experience.

  • Improve support operations — help develop service levels, escalation paths, reporting and technical-support processes as the function scales.

What we’re looking for

  • Experience in technical support, product support, software engineering, solutions engineering or another customer-facing technical role.

  • Strong diagnostic ability — you can work methodically from symptoms to root cause rather than relying on guesswork.

  • A working understanding of modern web applications, APIs, authentication, integrations and common browser or network issues.

  • Experience using diagnostic information such as application logs, monitoring tools, browser developer tools and database queries.

  • Enough familiarity with software code to navigate a codebase, follow application logic and use it to investigate reported behaviour.

  • Clear customer communication — you can remain calm under pressure, set expectations honestly and explain complex issues at the right level of detail.

  • Strong ownership — you remain responsible for moving an issue forward even when other teams need to contribute.

  • Sound prioritisation — you can assess urgency and customer impact and recognise when an issue requires immediate escalation.

  • Care and precision — you document what you tested, avoid unsupported conclusions and confirm that the customer’s problem has actually been resolved.

  • Interest in AI systems — you’re curious about how AI-enabled products behave and comfortable investigating issues that may not always be deterministic.

  • No legal background is required, but you should be motivated to learn how in-house legal teams work.

Desirable, but not essential

  • Experience writing and debugging production software.

  • The ability to create automated tests and submit code fixes for engineering review.

  • Experience supporting AI-enabled or data-intensive applications.

  • Familiarity with incident-management and observability tools.

How we work

We’re an in-person team based in Edinburgh. You should expect to work from the office as your default.

We support customers globally using a follow-the-sun model. You’ll work the normal hours agreed for your region and create clear handovers when an issue needs to continue beyond them. Any exceptional on-call or out-of-hours arrangements would be agreed and communicated separately.

We set a high bar, move quickly and give people meaningful ownership. Support is a core part of the product experience, and we expect it to be technically credible, responsive and human.

You’ll work closely with Engineering, Product, Transformation and Customer Success. Customer Success owns adoption and customer health

You’ll have the opportunity to shape our support tooling and operating model, influence the product through direct customer evidence, and develop towards senior support engineering, support leadership, solutions engineering or product engineering.

About Foundation Health

Foundation Health is an AI operating system for pharmacy - built by a team who lived the problem firsthand, not one that came to healthcare from the outside. Every day, prior authorizations delay prescriptions, pharmacists lose hours to paperwork instead of patients, and prescriptions slip through the cracks between health systems. We believe thoughtfully applied AI can finally change that - deep, integrated infrastructure that streamlines how care is coordinated, purpose-built for the complexity of specialty pharmacy.

We're building toward a world where pharmacy teams spend their time on patients, not paperwork - where AI handles the routine so clinicians can focus on what only humans can do. Getting there takes the right people. We're looking for curious, ambitious folks who want to help solve healthcare's hardest problems - for our patients, our partners, and each other.

The team: AI-native by design

Our VP of Engineering comes from DeepMind/Google, and we're building with AI from day one, both in the product and in how we engineer. We use AI tools to move faster, automate repetitive work and spend more time on problems that need real engineering judgement.

What you'll actually be doing

  • Designing and building the back-end systems that connect pharmacies, health systems and insurers

  • Solving hard distributed-systems problems: event-driven workflows, retries, idempotency, data consistency and failure recovery

  • Owning substantial features from the initial problem through architecture, build, deployment and production

  • Making pragmatic technical decisions as we scale, without overengineering for problems we don't have yet

  • Building AI-powered capabilities into a live product, where reliability and correctness matter as much as speed

  • Working directly with product and engineering leadership to shape the roadmap, architecture and what we build next

Manchester: where our core engineering team works

Our core engineering team is based in Manchester city centre. We're in the office together 1–2 days a week to work through hard problems and debate technical decisions. The rest of the week, work wherever you're most effective.

Not in Manchester yet? If you'd consider relocating, we can help with the move.

Why you'd leave your current role

  • Your work reaches real users. We're live with enterprise customers, so what you ship gets used, not lost in a backlog.

  • Interesting engineering problems. We're connecting fragmented healthcare systems, where data integrity and correctness really matter. This isn't a CRUD app with an AI feature bolted on.

  • Real ownership. You'll shape solutions, challenge assumptions and influence the roadmap and architecture. We want you making important technical decisions, not just implementing someone else's.

  • No legacy baggage. We're on a modern Node.js, TypeScript and GCP stack. You don't need to know it already. We care far more about the systems you've built than the tools you used.

  • Equity. You'll own a stake in the company you're helping build.

What we do care about

  • Strong engineering judgement. You can take an ambiguous problem, work out what matters, make sensible trade-offs and deliver without every step mapped out.

  • Back-end depth. You've built and operated production systems and know what happens beyond the happy path: distributed systems, databases, performance, observability and failure recovery.

  • Ownership beyond the code. You think about how a feature behaves in production, how customers use it and what could go wrong. You've made technical decisions with real consequences and can explain why you made them.

  • A builder's mindset. You've taken meaningful projects from idea to reality, at work or in your own time, and can explain the decisions and trade-offs you made.

  • Curiosity about AI. You've built AI products, use AI to improve how you work, or are actively exploring what's possible. You don't need to be an ML researcher.

  • Strong fundamentals. You reason from first principles and pick up unfamiliar tech quickly. A degree in Computer Science, Maths, Physics or Engineering is useful, but depth of engineering ability matters most.

Interested?

The funding's in place, the product is live and customers are asking for more than we can build. We're hiring engineers in Manchester to help close that gap.

Help us use technology to make a big green dent in the universe!

Kraken powers some of the most innovative global developments in energy.
