By optimising renewable generation, building a more intelligent grid, and empowering utilities to deliver an exceptional customer experience, our operating system is transforming the industry worldwide.

It’s an incredibly exciting time to work in energy. Join us on our mission to improve the lives of ONE BILLION humans within the decade and shape a cleaner, better future for everyone.

AI is a key investment area for Kraken Technologies. You’ll join Autonomous Agents, the team building AI-powered customer service for the energy industry. We connect conversational AI to Kraken’s customer platform so agents can do more than answer questions: they can use account information and approved tools to resolve real customer needs, like understanding a bill or submitting a meter reading, and hand over to a person, with full context, when it matters.

We’re launching autonomous agents with our utilities clients and the demand is growing quickly. The team is moving from initial trials to long-term production use, and we’re scaling from client-specific builds to a reusable product that can serve many clients. We’re growing the team to make that happen.

🏡 Where you'll fit in:

You’ll join a cross-functional team of around 10 engineers, alongside product and machine learning specialists, working closely with Kraken platform teams. The work spans two connected areas, and you’ll contribute to both:

  • Build: the reusable core of the product. This covers client-agnostic agent journeys and tooling, MCP interfaces into Kraken, email, messaging and voice capabilities, and the observability, feature toggles and guardrails that let us roll out safely.

  • Implementation: taking that core to individual clients. You’ll work with client teams to understand their customer journeys, configure and extend what we’ve built, and feed what you learn back into the shared product.

This is a hands-on engineering role. You’ll work alongside senior engineers and leads who will support your growth, while owning meaningful pieces of work from the first few months.

👾 What you'll own:

  • Connect the dots: Investigate customer support queries, get to grips with regulatory and business processes, and turn them into clear technical plans.

  • Bring agents to life: Build integrations between Kraken, Model Context Protocol (MCP) interfaces and our AI agent setup, using Python on the Kraken side and TypeScript on the agent side.

  • Build once, reuse everywhere: Spot patterns across customer journeys and client needs, and turn them into reusable, client-agnostic components rather than one-off fixes.

  • Make it safe and reliable: Build authentication, permissions, validation and human handoff into the design, and help us test and monitor behaviour that is less predictable than traditional software.

  • Roll out with confidence: Ship features behind toggles, tested and documented, so they can be introduced gradually across clients and teams.

  • Work with clients and teammates: Take part in client conversations, explain technical details clearly, document decisions and keep your commitments on track.

  • Operate what you build: Contribute to dashboards, monitoring and runbooks so the services you ship are observable and supportable in production.

🧠 What you bring to the party:

  • Solid software engineering: You have shipped and supported production software, and you’re comfortable with testing, code review and working in a team codebase.

  • Python and TypeScript: You write clean, maintainable code in both and are happy moving between tools and environments.

  • Problem-first thinking: You take time to understand the problem before jumping to the first solution.

  • Curiosity about AI: You’re interested in LLMs, autonomous agents and MCP, and in how to give agents the right context and tools. Hands-on experience is great, but you don’t need to have all the answers.

  • Customer and client awareness: You’re comfortable talking to non-engineers, asking good questions and translating messy real-world processes into software.

  • Reliable delivery: You’re organised, write clear documentation and follow through on what you take on.

  • Learning agility: You welcome feedback, ask questions when things are ambiguous and enjoy learning alongside others in a field that changes fast.

🚀 What success looks like:

  • Delivery: You ship well-scoped features and integrations that make it into production and are used by real clients.

  • Reusability: Your work strengthens the shared product, so the next client is easier to onboard than the last.

  • Trust: Agents you help build behave safely, resolve customer needs correctly and hand over to people when they should.

  • Growth: You take on increasing ownership and become a go-to person for part of the platform.

⭐️ Bonus points:

  • AI engineering: Building with LLMs, agent frameworks or MCP servers

  • Conversational AI: Experience with customer service automation, voice or messaging channels

  • Evals and monitoring: Testing, evaluating or monitoring non-deterministic systems

  • Backend: Django

  • Observability: Datadog, Sentry

  • Client-facing experience: Working directly with customers or partners on technical delivery

Help us use technology to make a big green dent in the universe!

Kraken powers some of the most innovative global developments in energy.

We create the technology that redefines utilities and unlocks a new energy system of the future. By optimising renewable generation, building a more intelligent grid, and empowering utilities to deliver an exceptional customer experience, our operating system is transforming the industry worldwide.

It’s an incredibly exciting time to work in energy. Join us on our mission to improve the lives of ONE BILLION humans within the decade and shape a cleaner, better future for everyone.

🏡 Where you'll fit in

You'll own strategic technology negotiations end to end. That covers tier-1 SaaS, outsourcing, and core billing platform deals for regulated utilities and energy retailers. You'll report to the Chief Commercial Officer and carry board-level accountability for deals above $100m.

You'll lead a cross-functional deal team and make sure every seat is filled by the right person:

  • Executive sponsor and deal owner: holds the mandate and budget, and breaks deadlocks fast.

  • Lead negotiator: runs the table, controls pacing and concessions, and stays separate from the delivery owner. This is the seat you'll usually hold.

  • Commercial and pricing lead: builds the should-cost model and covers pricing structures, benchmarking, and total cost of ownership (TCO).

  • Legal and contracts counsel: covers liability caps, intellectual property (IP) ownership, indemnities, termination, data protection, and step-in rights.

  • Technical and solution architect: tests feasibility, scope, service levels (SLAs), and integration and security claims.

  • Operations and service owner: brings realistic requirements, transition plans, and governance from the business.

  • Finance and procurement: covers payment terms, currency and indexation, and audit and benchmarking rights.

  • Risk, security, and compliance: handles regulatory, data residency, and resilience requirements.

🚀 What you'll own

  • Lead negotiation of multi-year technology and outsourcing agreements worth $250m to $1bn+ in total contract value, from selection through signature.

  • Set the commercial playbook: pricing structures, walk-away positions, a concession log, and fallback positions on liability, service levels, and exit.

  • Agree one position before you sit down. Rank priorities as must-have, trade, or give, and define your walk-away point (your best alternative to a negotiated agreement, or BATNA).

  • Structure deals that fit the risk: fixed price, time and materials, outcome-based, and gain-share, with volume bands, rate cards, indexation, and price-down glide paths.

  • Decide which risks to transfer, share, or keep, and put a price on each one.

special-projects-lead-category-expansion-london-23097,Fleek,Special Projects Lead - Category Expansion,"

Can you help us fix the world's most broken supply chain?

The fashion industry produces over 100 billion garments a year. 60% end up in landfill, not because people don't want these clothes, but because the supply chain for getting secondhand fashion from donation to resale is completely offline, manual and broken.

Fleek is fixing this. Our mission is to make secondhand the first choice. We're building the infrastructure powering the global secondhand clothing trade, through a B2B marketplace and the AI systems digitising the supply chain behind it.

Through Fleek, vintage stores, online resellers and retail buyers source graded secondhand inventory directly from wholesalers and rag houses across multiple countries. Our key enabler is FleekSort, an AI model fine-tuned on secondhand fashion that can grade, price and categorise items with just a photo. Turning what has historically been an opaque and manual trade into a structured, searchable and tradable global inventory layer.

Since 2022, we've saved 9 million items from landfill while tripling in size year-on-year. We're backed by some of the world's best investors, including a16z, Y Combinator and HV Capital, alongside world-class angels who helped build Depop, Shopify, and Postmates.

Today, we serve thousands of resellers and retailers across the UK, Europe and the US. With the secondhand fashion market projected to reach $350B by 2027, Fleek is building the AI-native operational and financial backbone for secondhand commerce globally.

We're looking for people who want to build something that matters and move fast doing it. Sounds good? Keep reading.

About the Role

We're hiring a Special Projects Lead to take Fleek's new category bets from thesis to proven economics. Each is a new business line that could add £5M+ in GMV, opening a new supply category or a new sourcing geography for the marketplace. Here's what makes these bets unusually winnable. Fleek already owns the demand. Most of the live bets sell to buyers who transact on Fleek today, so they're a supply-first test rather than a two-sided cold start. Your job on a new bet is to find and onboard the supply, sell it into demand that already exists and read the economics fast.

Every bet runs through the same gates. If a bet misses its gates, you kill it with evidence and move to the next one. If it works and you're running it well, you don't have to hand it off. You scale into owning the category, with supply, acquisition and ops building out under you. Think of this seat as a venture builder inside Fleek.

One thing this is not. We're not building a sales team or a sales culture, and this is not an AE or account manager role with a new title. You'll work directly with the founders and our commercial lead, close to the centre of the company.

What You'll Do

  • Run bets through the gates: take each bet from market research to first suppliers to first GMV to a feasible-or-not call, with win metrics and kill metrics defined before you start.

column18: >Les technologies de captage et stockage du CO2 sont des technologies clés pour la décarbonation du secteur industriel. Or, la proximité de ces sites avec les populations rend leurs déploiements incertains et soulève des questions relatives à l’acceptabilité sociale.
column19: >La surveillance à long terme des sites de stockage de CO2, exigée par la directive européenne CCS, constitue une opportunité pour renforcer la transparence et l’acceptation locale du stockage en engageant les parties prenantes dans l’acquisition et l’interprétation des données. Le projet CO2MET vise à développer et faire progresser des unités ou éléments clés pour préparer un futur système intégré de surveillance numérique à long terme améliorant la fiabilité et l’acceptabilité du stockage géologique de CO2.
column20: >Pour atteindre ces objectifs, le consortium CO2MET a été constitué et est composé de l'IFPEN, du BRGM, de Mines Saint-Etienne et de Cerema.
column21: >La surveillance à long terme nécessite des outils fiables et performants, notamment dans le domaine des capteurs environnementaux, ce qui soulève la question de la mise en œuvre de mesures correctives pour traiter le signal, ainsi que celle de l'influence des variations à long terme des paramètres externes sur la réponse des capteurs (et de l'impact du changement climatique). Étant donné que les signaux de concentration en CO₂ peuvent, à eux seuls, ne pas être suffisamment discriminants (les concentrations biologiques dans les sols pouvant dépasser 10 % vol.), compte tenu de leurs origines diverses (sources profondes, provenant du stockage ou de l’interaction gaz-roche
column23: oxydation du méthane), la prévention des faux positifs dans la surveillance des sites de stockage doit s'appuyer sur des capteurs de CO₂ (NDIR ou photoacoustiques) et sur d'autres capteurs (par exemple, un capteur chimique d'O₂), ainsi que sur des capteurs environnementaux (humidité, pression, température) afin de permettre une attribution correcte de la source de CO2.

    • Context

    Vocca builds AI voice agents for medical practices: they answer patient calls, book and reschedule appointments, and free up time for care teams. 250 healthcare organizations use Vocca today, and we are a team of 50+ across Paris and New York.

    In France we sell to imaging centers, to networks and health centers, and to independent practices. We have tested many acquisition channels without measuring them properly, so we can't say which one works best or for which type of practice. Our website is made to be read: a visitor can't try the product, estimate a return on investment or compare us with the alternatives. In the US, paid acquisition starts from zero.

    The target is set: 100 MQLs in Q4 2026, then +30% every quarter. We are hiring the person who will own that number. You report to Pierre, Head of Marketing.

    Your mission

    Build Vocca's inbound lead engine. You own paid acquisition and website conversion, in France first and then in the US, and you are accountable for the quarterly MQL target: 100 in Q4 2026 and about 285 per quarter by the end of 2027.

    Expected outcomes

    After 1 months:

    • Tracking and attribution work: every lead has a source and a cost, and can be followed in the CRM up to the signed deal

    • Google Ads and Meta accounts audited and rebuilt, with campaigns live for each segment

    • A first ranking of channels by cost per MQL, and budget moved accordingly

    • The first conversion pages live on the website

    After 3 months:

    • The quarterly MQL target is met and on the +30% trajectory

    • Cost per MQL and MQL-to-opportunity rate known for each channel and segment

    • ROI calculator, comparison pages and a way to try the product live on the website

    • Email and SMS nurturing running on leads who are not ready to buy yet

    • A tested approach to practitioner communities, starting with dentists' Facebook groups

    After 9 months:

    • About 285 MQLs per quarter, close to three times the Q4 2026 level

    • Paid acquisition live in the US, with a first read on cost per lead

    • A channel mix the sales team trusts, with lead quality reviewed with them on a regular basis

    What you will own

    Paid acquisition (the core of the job)

    • Run the Google Ads and Meta campaigns yourself, and test other paid channels when the numbers justify it

    • Own the budget: split it by segment and channel, and cut what doesn't convert

    • Write and test ads and landing pages without waiting for a brief

    • Open paid acquisition in the US

    Website and conversion

    • Turn the website into something visitors can act on: ROI calculator, comparison pages, product trial, lead magnets

    • Build and test landing pages for each segment and specialty

    • Work with our web agency, which runs SEO and GEO, so that paid and organic use the same keywords and pages

    Nurturing and communities

    • Run email and SMS campaigns to leads and prospects. RevOps owns the tools and the CRM sync, you own the messages and the calendar

    • Join the communities where practitioners talk to each other and turn them into a source of leads

    • Try new channels as they appear and drop them quickly when they don't pay

    Measurement

    • Report cost per MQL, conversion to opportunity and revenue for each channel

    • Agree with sales on what a qualified lead is, and review lead quality with them

    • Tell the team every month where the next euro should go

    This role is for you if

    Must have:

    • 4 to 7 years in growth or performance marketing with paid acquisition as your strongest skill. You have run Google Ads and Meta accounts yourself, on real budgets, and you can show the results

    • You are a generalist out of curiosity. Beyond ads, you have built landing pages, set up tracking and written email sequences, and you prefer learning a tool to briefing someone else on it

    • Fluent French and professional English.

    What we will assess:

    • Numbers: you think in cost per lead, conversion rate and payback, and you can explain a campaign you stopped and why

    • Doing it yourself: you build the campaign, the page and the automation, with AI and no-code tools when they save time

    • Curiosity: you test channels nobody asked you to test

    • Ownership: you have one number, and you say so early when it is off track

    • Closeness to sales: you care about what happens to a lead after the form is filled in

    • B2B lead generation for a SaaS product, experience marketing to healthcare professionals or small businesses

    • Nice to have: paid campaigns on the US market.

    This role is NOT for you if

    • You want to specialize in one channel and stay on it

    • You manage agencies and freelancers and no longer operate the accounts yourself

    • You are looking for a brand or content role

    Compensation and benefits

    • 60-75K package

    • Equity (BSPCE)

    • Executive contract (cadre) on a forfait-jours basis, with 8 to 12 RTT days per year

    • Hybrid: 3 days per week at our Paris office

    • MacBook provided

    • Meal vouchers: €9 per working day (55% covered by the company)

    • Health insurance: 50% of Alan covered

About Dust

Work is being rewritten, and the people holding the pen are the ones who actually run it.

With enterprise-grade governance, flexible model choice, and a collaborative interface for humans and agents to work together, Dust empowers AI Operators at the world’s fastest-moving companies to rewire how work gets done.

With 70%+ weekly active users, people stick with Dust as much as they do with Slack and Notion. We don't get piloted and shelved. We land once, and spread. We're at an exciting stage of our journey, and growing fast.

We're serving great customers like Datadog, 1Password, Cursor, Clay, Vanta and Persona, and aim to x5 our growth by the end of 2026.

Dust is backed by Sequoia with a determined team of optimists (coming from Stripe, OpenAI, and Stanford) who like to focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously while doing so. The Generalist named us among the Future 50.

The role

Dust is growing fast, and we want every person who joins us to feel welcome, supported, connected and able to do their best work. As our People Experience Manager, you'll shape how people experience Dust, from their first day and the moments that bring us together to the way our offices in Paris, London, New York and San Francisco support the team.

We're looking for someone who is operationally excellent and creatively ambitious. You'll handle the details carefully, and you'll also look for ways to make the employee experience much better. One day you might be redesigning part of onboarding, the next planning a company offsite, acting on survey feedback, or working with a site lead to improve one of our offices.

This role works as a partner across the company. You'll work most closely with People Operations, who lead on the core people processes. Together, you'll make sure the employee experience is well run behind the scenes and thoughtful in how people actually experience it. In Paris, you'll also work closely with our Office Manager, who runs our HQ on site and leads much of our day-to-day office life and events. In London, New York and San Francisco, you'll coordinate with local site leads. You'll also work with IT, Finance, Legal, Marketing, leadership and outside partners. Your guiding principle: consistency where it matters, local adaptation where it creates a better experience.

What you will do:

Own the employee journey

  • Own the onboarding experience end to end, working closely with our People Ops Specialist, from pre-boarding and equipment to first-day logistics and the first few weeks, so new joiners can contribute from day one in every location.

  • Work with People Ops, IT, Finance, hiring managers, our Paris Office Manager and site leads so every handoff in the employee journey is smooth.

  • Partner with People Ops and IT on offboarding, so people leave with the same care they got when they joined.

  • Be a trusted point of contact for everyday employee questions and needs, and know when to bring in People Ops.

Build culture and community

  • Run and improve our team rituals, including weekly lunches, team drinks, dinners and company gatherings.

  • Organise one or two company offsites or retreats each year.

  • Create moments that help people connect, celebrate progress and feel they belong, across offices and time zones.

  • Pay attention to the details that make experiences feel personal and inclusive, such as dietary needs, accessibility, preferences and team milestones.

  • Partner with People and Marketing on selected external and brand-building events.

Listen and turn feedback into action

  • Build feedback loops (surveys, conversations, informal check-ins) to understand how people experience Dust.

  • Turn what people tell us into concrete recommendations and visible improvements.

  • Define and track simple, useful measures of employee and workplace experience.

  • Communicate clearly and consistently about updates, events, practical information and team norms. Be assertive when needed.

Shape our workplaces

  • Make sure our offices are safe, welcoming, functional and ergonomic, and that they reflect how we want people to feel at Dust.

  • Work with our office manager on day-to-day operations: supplies, maintenance, access, equipment and services.

  • Manage workplace vendors, contracts and budget, and look for efficient ways to improve the experience.

  • Spot operational needs early and fix issues before they disrupt anyone.

Scale the experience as Dust grows

  • Help shape how our physical, hybrid and digital environments evolve as the company grows.

  • Set up simple, scalable processes and clear ownership across People, IT, Finance and Legal topics.

  • Keep the employee experience personal and high quality without making it bureaucratic.


What success looks like

After your first 100 days, you will have:

  • Built a smooth, consistent onboarding experience for every new joiner, in every location.

  • Delivered team rituals, events and offsites that strengthen connection and culture.

  • Set up feedback loops and a practical set of metrics that guide People Experience decisions.

  • Created well-run, welcoming offices where operational issues are handled quickly and proactively.

  • Established clear processes and ownership across People, workplace, IT, Finance and Legal.

  • Helped Dust grow its employee experience without it becoming bureaucratic or impersonal.

What we are looking for

  • 4+ years of experience in People Operations, People Experience, Workplace Experience in a fast growing, globally distributed environment

  • A proactive generalist who can handle many kinds of work at once without losing sight of the bigger picture.

  • Real ideas, sound judgement and the confidence to improve how things work today.

  • Strong operational ownership, project management skills and attention to detail.

  • Warmth, empathy and a genuine interest in helping people feel comfortable and connected.

  • Clear, direct, thoughtful communication, and discretion with sensitive situations.

  • Confidence working with vendors, budgets and outside partners.

  • The ability to build simple processes that scale, and to keep a high bar for quality while staying pragmatic.

  • Comfort with a fast-moving environment where priorities can change, working on your own while collaborating across the company.

Location

We're prioritizing building our team with an in-person culture at our offices in Paris, London, San Francisco, and New York because we value the magic that happens when talented people work closely together.

We have an office-first culture. Some of the best things about building at Dust are the energy, the fast decisions, and the unexpected conversations that unlock a hard problem, which happen because we are in the same room. Being together is not a formality, it is how we do our best work, and it is something we actively protect.

That said, we hire people with strong judgement and we extend that trust to how they manage their time. When working from home makes more sense for what you need to get done that day, we trust you to make that call.

Why Dust

The models are powerful enough. What's missing is the product layer where AI meets how companies actually work. That's what we're building: the infrastructure that lets any team turn scattered knowledge and tools into coordinated execution with agents they build, own, and run themselves.

We use Dust ourselves every day. We get to shape how humans and agents collaborate while solving our own problems with the product we ship. That loop is rare, and it's why we move fast.

If you're excited about defining a new category and want to join a determined team of optimists who focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously, we'd love to talk.

Even if you don't check every box in our requirements, we encourage you to apply. We value diverse perspectives and backgrounds, and we're more interested in your potential and passion than a perfect match to our checklist.

Learn how we think and work.

  • Your Next Co-Worker Isn’t Human, Stanislas Polu, VivaTech 2026. A conversation about AI agents taking on larger parts of work and how teams collaborate with them.

  • Dust: Gabriel Hubert on Enterprise AI, Gabriel Hubert, Nasdaq, published May 7, 2026. On Dust’s approach to enterprise AI and building the company in Europe.

Direction de Projets – Ingénierie, Construction & Infrastructures Critiques

1. Présentation du poste

Intitulé : Directeur de Projet Data Center (Data Center Project Director)

Rattachement hiérarchique : Directeur des Opérations / Directeur de Programme / Direction Générale

Périmètre : France et International

Secteur : Data Centers – Infrastructures critiques – Construction – Ingénierie

2. Mission principale

Le Directeur de Projet Data Center assure le pilotage stratégique, technique, opérationnel et financier de projets complexes de conception, de construction, d'extension ou de transformation de Data Centers.

Il garantit la bonne exécution des projets dans le respect des engagements contractuels, des budgets, des délais, des exigences de qualité, de sécurité, de performance énergétique et de disponibilité des infrastructures.

Il intervient sur l'ensemble du cycle de vie des projets, depuis les études de faisabilité jusqu'à la réception des installations, leur mise en service et leur transfert aux équipes d'exploitation.

Véritable chef d'orchestre, il coordonne les différentes parties prenantes et assure l'interface entre la maîtrise d'ouvrage, la maîtrise d'œuvre, les bureaux d'études, les entreprises de construction, les fournisseurs et les exploitants.

3. Responsabilités principales

A. Direction et pilotage stratégique des projets

  • Définir la stratégie globale d'exécution et les objectifs du projet.

  • Piloter des projets de Data Centers neufs (Greenfield), d'extension ou de rénovation (Brownfield).

  • Superviser toutes les phases du projet, de la faisabilité à la livraison.

  • Définir les jalons, les livrables et les indicateurs de performance.

  • Mettre en place la gouvernance et les instances de décision.

  • Arbitrer les choix techniques, économiques et organisationnels.

  • Anticiper les risques et définir les plans d'atténuation.

  • Assurer le reporting auprès de la Direction Générale, des investisseurs et des clients.

B. Management technique et coordination des études

Superviser et coordonner l'ensemble des disciplines techniques :

Électricité – Courants forts et faibles

  • Réseaux HTB/HTA/BT et postes de transformation.

  • Tableaux électriques, TGBT et distribution électrique.

  • Groupes électrogènes et systèmes d'alimentation secourue.

  • Onduleurs (UPS), batteries et systèmes de distribution.

  • Architectures de redondance N+1, 2N et autres configurations adaptées aux exigences de disponibilité.

  • Coordination des protections électriques, sélectivité et continuité de service.

CVC – Refroidissement et traitement d'air

  • Production et distribution frigorifique.

  • Groupes froids, free cooling et refroidissement adiabatique.

  • CRAH, CRAC et Fan Walls.

  • Systèmes de refroidissement liquide (Liquid Cooling).

  • CDU et solutions de Direct-to-Chip Cooling.

  • Optimisation des performances thermiques et énergétiques.

Bâtiment et infrastructures

  • Génie civil, structure et architecture.

  • VRD et raccordements aux réseaux.

  • Sécurité incendie et systèmes de détection/extinction.

  • Contrôle d'accès, vidéosurveillance et sûreté physique.

  • BMS, DCIM, GTB et supervision technique.

  • Intégration des infrastructures IT et télécoms.

Assurer la cohérence technique des études, la gestion des interfaces et la conformité aux exigences contractuelles et réglementaires.

C. Pilotage des études et de la conception

  • Superviser les études de faisabilité et les avant-projets.

  • Piloter les phases de conception selon les référentiels contractuels applicables, notamment RIBA 0 à 4 pour les projets concernés.

  • Valider les choix architecturaux et techniques.

  • Organiser les revues de conception et les analyses de risques.

  • Superviser la coordination BIM et les études de synthèse.

  • Garantir la constructibilité, la maintenabilité et l'exploitabilité des installations.

  • Piloter les démarches de Value Engineering.

  • Optimiser le CAPEX sans compromettre les exigences de performance et de résilience.

D. Direction de la construction et de l'exécution

  • Définir la stratégie de réalisation et le phasage des travaux.

  • Superviser les entreprises générales, les lots techniques et les sous-traitants.

  • Coordonner les équipes de maîtrise d'œuvre et de construction.

  • Garantir le respect des plannings et des jalons contractuels.

  • Piloter les interfaces entre génie civil, électricité, CVC et infrastructures IT.

  • Superviser les procédures de contrôle qualité.

  • Veiller au respect des exigences HSE.

  • Gérer les modifications, non-conformités et situations critiques.

  • Organiser les opérations préalables à la réception.

E. Gestion financière et contractuelle

  • Construire et piloter le budget global du projet.

  • Superviser les engagements financiers et le suivi des dépenses.

  • Piloter les CAPEX et les prévisions à terminaison (Estimate at Completion).

  • Identifier les dérives budgétaires et mettre en œuvre les actions correctives.

  • Superviser les consultations, appels d'offres et négociations.

  • Piloter les contrats de maîtrise d'œuvre, d'ingénierie, de construction et de fourniture.

  • Gérer les avenants, réclamations contractuelles et risques financiers.

  • Optimiser les coûts et préserver les marges du projet.

  • Assurer un reporting financier fiable et régulier.

F. Commissioning et mise en service

  • Définir et superviser la stratégie de commissioning.

  • Coordonner les essais des équipements et systèmes techniques.

  • Superviser les essais fonctionnels et les essais intégrés (Integrated Systems Testing).

  • Vérifier les scénarios de fonctionnement normal, dégradé et secouru.

  • Piloter la levée des réserves et la clôture des non-conformités.

  • Garantir la remise des DOE, procédures et documentations techniques.

Résumé

Nous recherchons un(e) Associate Team Lead Support N2 / Chef(fe) d’équipe Support N2 pour rejoindre l’équipe Support Niveau 2 de Pennylane, au service des dirigeants d’entreprise et des cabinets comptables.

Pennylane est une plateforme de gestion financière et comptable qui accompagne les dirigeants d’entreprise et les cabinets d’expertise comptable dans leur quotidien. L’équipe Support Niveau 2 intervient sur les demandes les plus complexes ou nécessitant une expertise métier et produit approfondie, en lien avec les équipes Support Niveau 1, Support Technique, Produit et Tech.

Ce rôle est un poste de management de proximité : tu seras le relais opérationnel du Team Lead Support N2 et accompagneras une équipe de 6 à 12 agents au quotidien pour leur permettre de répondre aux utilisateurs avec efficacité, qualité et empathie. Tu contribueras également au pilotage de l’activité, à l’amélioration continue du support et à des projets transverses.

Notre culture

Au sein du Support, nous valorisons la transparence, la bonne ambiance, l’entraide et la résilience.

Nous restons proches de la réalité de nos utilisateurs, notamment des dirigeants d’entreprise et des professionnels de la comptabilité, afin de traiter chaque demande avec expertise métier, maîtrise du produit et empathie. Cette approche s’inscrit dans la culture Pennylane de Supporting SMEs et de proximité avec les utilisateurs.

Nous encourageons le feedback dans les deux sens, le développement de chacun et la prise d’initiative. Nous accordons de l’importance à l’autonomie, à la responsabilité et à la confiance, dans l’esprit de Community of Builders et de Radical Trust.

Concrètement, ton quotidien ressemblera à ça

  • Animer les points d’équipe et suivre la charge quotidienne.

  • Accompagner les agents sur leurs tickets, leurs priorités et leurs situations complexes.

  • Réaliser des écoutes ou analyses de conversations pour donner du feedback constructif.

  • Suivre les indicateurs de performance et de qualité de l’équipe, comme le temps de première réponse, le temps de résolution, la satisfaction client et le volume de tickets traités.

  • Participer aux rituels de pilotage opérationnel : suivi de la charge, priorisation des demandes, identification des alertes et coordination avec les autres équipes Support.

  • Remonter les irritants utilisateurs aux équipes Produit, Tech ou Ops.

  • Contribuer à améliorer les process, la documentation et les outils internes.

Responsabilités

  • Manager une équipe de 6 à 12 agents sous la supervision du Team Lead Support N2, en les accompagnant dans leur activité quotidienne, leur progression et leur épanouissement professionnel.

  • Donner des feedbacks clairs, réguliers et transparents, réaliser des écoutes et analyses de conversations, suivre les bilans et plans d’accompagnement individuels, proposer des coachings et identifier les besoins de formation.

  • Suivre les indicateurs de l’équipe et contribuer à la qualité du support, notamment le temps de première réponse, la satisfaction client, le temps de résolution, le volume traité, la prise en charge des nouveaux tickets et le suivi des tickets en cours.

  • Participer aux rituels de pilotage et à la gestion des files de demandes communes, notamment lors des rotations de permanence, en identifiant les alertes et en remontant les besoins de renfort ou d’arbitrage.

  • Être force de proposition pour optimiser les process, les outils, la documentation et les modes de fonctionnement du Support.

  • Collaborer avec les équipes support de niveau 1, l’équipe technique, les équipes opérationnelles ainsi que les équipes produit et tech, faire remonter les irritants utilisateurs et contribuer aux projets transverses.

  • Partager les bonnes pratiques avec les autres Associate Team Leads et contribuer à maintenir une communication fluide au sein du Support.

  • Prendre ponctuellement en charge des demandes internes urgentes ou des situations complexes nécessitant l’expertise du Support Niveau 2, en sachant orienter ou escalader lorsque cela est nécessaire.

Ce poste est fait pour toi si

  • Tu aimes accompagner une équipe et faire progresser les autres.

  • Tu sais garder du recul dans des situations opérationnelles parfois urgentes.

  • Tu es à l’aise avec les indicateurs, tout en gardant toujours en tête la qualité de l’expérience utilisateur.

  • Tu sais communiquer avec clarté, même quand les sujets sont complexes.

  • Tu as envie de contribuer à structurer une équipe Support dans un environnement en forte évolution.

Qualifications

  • Diplôme Bac+2 ou Bac+3 minimum en comptabilité, management ou dans un domaine équivalent.

  • Expérience d’au moins 1 an en management ou en accompagnement d’équipe, idéalement dans le secteur du support.

  • Bonne capacité à analyser une situation, prendre une décision mesurée et proposer des solutions concrètes.

  • Excellentes capacités de communication et de collaboration, avec assertivité et diplomatie.

  • Goût pour le feedback, la pédagogie et l’accompagnement individuel.

  • Aisance avec les outils informatiques, notamment les outils de ticketing et de documentation comme Intercom, Zendesk ou Notion.

  • Capacité à s’adapter à un environnement en évolution rapide.

  • Sens du service et attention portée à l’expérience utilisateur.

Les nice to have

Ces éléments sont un plus, mais ne sont pas indispensables si tu as une forte appétence pour le support, le management de proximité et l’apprentissage produit/métier.

  • Connaissances en comptabilité.

  • Expérience préalable en tant que contributeur individuel au sein d’une équipe Support.

  • Expérience dans un environnement SaaS ou start-up.

  • Expérience dans le management d’une équipe principalement à distance.

  • Expérience de collaboration avec des équipes Produit, Tech ou Ops.

  • Anglais niveau B1 minimum.

  • Utilisation de l’IA pour optimiser ses tâches.

Modalités pratiques

  • Tu reporteras au Team Lead Support N2.

  • Le rôle combine management de proximité, pilotage opérationnel et contribution ponctuelle sur des situations complexes ou urgentes.

  • L’équipe collabore principalement en français, avec des interactions possibles en anglais selon les sujets et les équipes.

Pennylane traite vos données pour gérer votre candidature et évaluer votre adéquation au poste. Si votre candidature n’aboutit pas, vos données peuvent être conservées 2 ans à compter de notre dernier échange ou de la clôture du recrutement afin de constituer &

En tant que Spécialiste Support Pilotage et Comptabilité, tu te positionnes comme un expert métier et plateforme. Tu es l'interlocuteur privilégié de notre base client qui a choisi Pennylane comme logiciel central de leur gestion comptable et financière.

Tu te trouves donc au cœur de l'expérience client 360 et fais profiter les clients et leurs comptables de la pleine puissance de Pennylane au service de leur croissance.

Comment vas-tu contribuer au projet ?

En tant que membre de l'équipe Support applicatif et technique comptable, tu es le point de relais central entre nos clients Dirigeants, leurs Comptables internalisés et les Cabinets Comptable. Tu es en contact quotidien avec les utilisateurs et tu cherches à comprendre les problèmes qu'ils rencontrent.

Après investigation, ton but est d'apporter une réponse ou solution à ton interlocuteur, ou quand cela est nécessaire, d'escalader le problème aux équipes techniques. Tu as aussi la charge d'aider les comptables d’entreprises et de cabinets à intégrer leurs données sur Pennylane afin de faciliter leur migration.

Quelles seront tes missions au quotidien ?

3 premiers mois :

- Tu te formes sur le produit et les rouages de l'équipe.

- Tu apprends tout ce qu'il faut savoir sur notre entreprise, notre vision, et nos différents départements.

- Tu apprends à identifier toutes les parties prenantes et à collaborer efficacement au sein de ton équipe, ainsi qu'avec les différents départements.

- Tu commences à répondre à des demandes liées à la comptabilité : tu réceptionnes les demandes, les qualifies en t’appuyant sur une compréhension approfondie des principes comptables et apportes des réponses rapides et impactantes.

- Tu commences à gérer des demandes clients de plus en plus complexe.

- Tu partages à tes collègues tes connaissances comptables et ton expérience ""terrain"".

- Tu portes la voix comme l’usage du client et tu partages aux équipes produit des retours construits.

- Tu deviens un expert produit et fais gagner en efficacité ton équipe en identifiant les axes d'amélioration.

- Tu prends le contrôle et mène au succès des projets qui te tiennent à cœur et qui te font progresser.

VAULTED AG is a Swiss deep-tech scale-up born out of research at ETH Zurich and the EMPA innovation ecosystem. We combine world-class engineering, computational design, digital fabrication, and advanced manufacturing to rethink how buildings are designed and delivered, at a time when AI, automation, and data-driven design are transforming the industry.

Our core technology is the Rippmann Floor System® (RFS), a lightweight, prefabricated structural floor system that reduces concrete use by up to 70%, steel use by up to 90%, and embodied carbon by up to 75% compared with conventional concrete slabs. After years of research and technology development, VAULTED is entering a major growth phase across Switzerland, Belgium, the UK, and the US.
Location: Dübendorf ZH, Switzerland · Start date: Q1 2027 · 100% · Reporting to the CEO

We are hiring a Chief Operating Officer to build the operational engine that turns confirmed projects into reliable, profitable, and scalable delivery. This is a senior leadership role for someone who combines deep project and construction industry understanding with strong operational and commercial judgement, but also someone who is very hands-on and enjoys setting up the systems and processes behind our operations.

The COO takes ownership once a project is won and oversees project delivery, project management, supplier and prefabrication partnerships, operational contracting, and project economics. The role ensures that scope, timelines, quality, risks, resources, costs, and margins are transparent and actively managed, while giving project teams the structure and support they need to deliver.

A core mandate is to make VAULTED better with every project: translate project learnings into stronger processes, supplier setups, handovers, delivery standards, and feedback to engineering and R&D. The COO builds the operational capabilities required to scale across Switzerland, Belgium, the UK, and the US without adding unnecessary complexity. This is a 100% role.

• Operational leadership & project delivery: Build and lead the operating model required to deliver VAULTED projects reliably and efficiently. Oversee the project management function, set clear execution standards, and support escalation and decision-making on active projects.

• Project economics & controlling: Establish disciplined project controlling across budgets, costs, forecasts, changes, and margins, ensuring deviations and commercial implications are visible early and actively addressed.

• Supplier, production & prefabrication ecosystem: Identify, evaluate, negotiate, and manage production partners, suppliers, and prefabricators across relevant markets, ensuring quality, capacity, cost competitiveness, and delivery reliability.

• Contracting, procurement & operational risk: Shape supplier and operational contracts, procurement approaches, and partnership models that improve delivery certainty, manage risk, protect margins, and maintain strategic flexibility.

• Cross-functional leadership & resources: Connect project management, engineering, design, R&D, commercial teams, and external partners. Create clarity on priorities, responsibilities, capacity, and trade-offs, and ensure smooth handovers from sales into execution.

• Continuous improvement & international scaling: Turn project learnings into better processes, standards, supplier setups, and execution methods, while building operational readiness for Switzerland, Belgium, the UK, the US, and future markets.
• Typically 8+ years of relevant experience in project delivery, operations, construction, architecture, or prefabrication, preferably with an engineering background.
• Proven responsibility for complex, multi-stakeholder projects or project portfolios, with the ability to oversee execution while staying close enough to intervene when needed.
• Strong practical understanding of how construction or engineered products move from design and procurement through production, coordination, and delivery.
• Strong commercial and financial discipline, including project budgets, cost drivers, forecasting, margins, change management, and operational risk.
• Experience negotiating and managing suppliers, production partners, contracts, and long-term operational relationships.
• Strong leadership skills with high empathy and high standards: able to build trust, set clear expectations, challenge constructively, make decisions, and hold teams and partners to commitments.
• Strategic and hands-on working style: able to build scalable systems and processes while staying pragmatic, close to project realities, and comfortable solving difficult execution issues.

You will define the security risk appetite, lead our response to an evolving threat landscape, and ensure security and resilience are embedded by design as our technology landscape develops.&lt

Establish and lead security governance, including policies, standards and control frameworks, with clear accountability across the Group. Report on security posture and material incidents to executive leadership and, where relevant, the Board.&lt

Ensure regulatory and compliance alignment, including GDPR, DORA and relevant sector obligations, advising the business on required adaptations and coordinating audits and certifications.&lt

A Bachelor’s degree in Information Security, Computer Science or a related field. A relevant Master’s degree is an advantage.&lt

10–15 years of progressive experience in information security and cybersecurity, including at least 5 years in a senior security role, with ownership of enterprise security strategy, governance and risk management.&lt

Strong knowledge of security frameworks and standards, including ISO/IEC 27001, NIST Cybersecurity Framework and CIS Controls, with practical experience implementing them.&lt
Good understanding of data protection, regulatory and compliance requirements, including GDPR, DORA and standards such as SOC 2.&lt
Professional certifications such as CISSP, CISM or CISA, or equivalent, are highly desirable.&lt

Strong analytical, communication and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to translate complex security risks into clear business implications and advise technical teams, executives, business stakeholders and clients.&lt
If you meet these criteria and are ready to contribute your expertise to a dynamic and challenging environment, we encourage you to apply.&lt

About Intero Integrity

Intero Integrity is an internationally operating specialist in the inspection, maintenance and emission monitoring of pipelines and industrial assets. We develop our inspection technology entirely in-house: from ultrasonic measurement systems and FPGA signal processing to the software our analysts use to interpret hundreds of kilometres of pipeline data.

The inspection results our software produces are used for safety-critical decisions about the integrity of pipelines and industrial installations such as heat exchangers. Reliability and correctness are therefore not a nice-to-have, but an absolute requirement.

An inspection shows a client what is wrong. You show them what to do about it.

Are you the integrity engineer people turn to when the inspection data is in and a decision has to be made? We are growing our Integrity team and are looking for our first Senior Integrity Engineer based in Europe.

About Intero

Intero Integrity Services helps pipeline operators and industrial companies keep their assets safe, compliant and running. With our own in-line inspection technology (including MFL and UT) we inspect pipelines and installations all over the world and tell clients exactly what condition their assets are in. Headquartered in Tricht, the Netherlands, we have over 40 years of experience and 650+ professionals from 25+ nationalities.
Learn more about our Inspection service line in this video: Intero - The Power of Integrity.

Your team

You join a close-knit Integrity team of five, including you: a Principal Integrity Engineer and Team Lead in Vancouver, an Integrity Engineer in Mexico City and two Junior Integrity Engineers in Toronto and Calgary. The team is part of our Data Analysis (DA) department.

An inspection delivers a list of findings. For our clients, especially in highly regulated markets, a list of problems without a solution is not enough. That is where you come in. Requirements

Qualinx is looking for a result-driven and conscientious senior SoC Architect. Someone who thrives in an environment where your proactive and can-do attitude is highly appreciated. The ideal candidate for this role must have:

  • Minimum of 12 years experience in RTL Design, RTL Verification, CPU-based Chip/Components Concepts and Architecture.

  • Deep understanding of ARM MCUs Subsystems, Memory Controllers, and memory architectures (e.g., SRAM, ROM, Flash, NVMe…).

  • At least 10 years’ experience with the Digital ASIC Flows, RTL design, Design Verification, Debug and Trace methodologies, Test (e.g., DFT, JTAG, Scan, BIST).

  • Solid understanding of chip packaging.

  • Proficient in hardware-software interface design, including device drivers, firmware, and low-level software optimizations.

  • Strong problem-solving skills to troubleshoot and resolve architectural issues related to SoC integration, performance, and power efficiency.

  • Experienced with silicon bring-up, validation, and post-silicon debug methodologies.

  • Practical experience with IP integration, including integration flows, interconnect design (e.g., AMBA, AXI, AHB), and managing key IP integration architecture tasks.

  • Deep understanding of peripherals, Pin Function Assignment, and multiplexing, as well as familiarity with various communication protocols (e.g. MIPI, LVDS, SPI, I2C, UART).

  • Experience in analog-digital interface design, including RF and Analog components like PLL, ADC, DAC, LNA, PA, DCDC, LDO… integration, and layout constraints for minimizing noise and signal interference.

  • Knowledge of low-power design techniques, including clock gating, power gating, and multi-voltage domains (UPF/CPF).

  • Deep understanding of library selection and design, with a focus on leakage power-aware methodologies to optimize performance and power trade-offs.

  • Hands-on experience with IP selection to meet the specific needs of the design.

  • Strong experience in selecting appropriate I/O technologies and designing for signal integrity, noise resilience, and power efficiency.

  • Strong knowledge of pad ring placement and ESD strategy.

  • In-depth expertise in clock and reset architecture design, including low-jitter clock distribution networks, clock domain crossing issues, and reset synchronization.

  • Solid understanding of power management units and implementing various power sequencing schemes, including wake, sleep, and deep sleep modes for power efficiency.

  • Solid Knowledge in signal processing, communication system.

  • Exposure to all aspects of RFIC system design.

Je bewaakt kosten, adviseert over haalbaarheid en zorgt dat plannen financieel realistisch én toekomstbestendig zijn. Ons bureau is groot genoeg om op topniveau te opereren, maar overzichtelijk genoeg om je echt thuis te voelen. column2: Binnen onze projecten groeit de behoefte aan betere budgetcontrole en sturing op kosten. Met jouw analytisch inzicht, projectervaring en overtuigingskracht adviseer je over kosten, waarde en haalbaarheid.

Heb jij diepgaande ervaring in werktuigbouwkundige installaties en wil je bijdragen aan de meest kritische en innovatieve datacenterprojecten van dit moment? Als Senior Mechanical Engineer Datacenters bij Deerns werkt je aan high-tech, schaalbare en energie-efficiënte faciliteiten die de digitale wereld draaiend houden. Jij ontwerpt de installaties die maximale betrouwbaarheid, duurzaamheid en continuïteit waarborgen precies waar de datacentersector om vraagt.
column3: Als Senior Mechanical Engineer binnen onze Datacenter afdeling ben je verantwoordelijk voor het ontwerp, de engineering en de technische coördinatie van complexe werktuigbouwkundige installaties. Denk aan geavanceerde koelconcepten (zoals indirect/direct evaporative cooling, liquid cooling en chiller‑oplossingen), luchtbehandeling, warmte‑terugwinning, water‑ en gassystemen en klimaattechnische infrastructuur die 24/7 betrouwbaar moet functioneren.
column4:

Vanaf de eerste conceptfase denk je mee over technische strategieën en ontwerpkeuzes die aansluiten op schaalbaarheid, energie‑efficiëntie, beschikbaarheidsnormen (Tier III/) en de steeds strengere duurzaamheidsdoelen. Je werkt nauw samen met andere disciplines zoals elektrotechniek, bouwkunde en security en bewaakt de technische integriteit en samenhang van het totaalontwerp. Dankzij jouw senioriteit fungeer je als inhoudelijk aanspreekpunt voor klanten, ontwerpteams en leveranciers. Je stuurt waar nodig bij, begeleidt junior en medior engineers en draagt actief bij aan kennisontwikkeling binnen het datacenterteam.
column5: Tot je verantwoordelijkheden behoren:
column6:
• Ontwerpen van mechanische gebouw gebonden systemen, waaronder HVAC (verwarming, ventilatie en airconditioning), koeling en andere Datacenter specifieke installaties.

  • Meedenken in de concept‑ en ontwerpfase en vertalen van klantwensen naar haalbare en schaalbare technische oplossingen.

  • Coördineren van ontwerpactiviteiten met andere disciplines en bewaken van planning, kwaliteit en integrale samenhang.

  • Technisch aanspreekpunt zijn voor klanten, partners, leveranciers en interne stakeholders/junioren.

  • Begeleiden van engineers binnen het project en bijdragen aan kennisontwikkeling in het team.

  • Ondersteunen bij aanbestedingen, kostenramingen en kwaliteitscontroles (zowel ontwerp als uitvoering).
column7:
Waar werken we aan

We hebben meegewerkt aan de bouw van diverse nieuwe datacenters in o.a. Milaan, Amsterdam. We hebben ondersteuning geboden bij het ontwerp van de mechanische, elektrische en sanitaire installaties voor de bouw. Na het ontwerp van de mechanische, elektrische en sanitaire installaties heeft Deerns toezicht gehouden op de bouwplaats om de kwaliteit van de installaties te controleren en heeft het als Commissioning manager voor de hoofdaannemer gefungeerd. Deerns heeft ook ondersteuning geboden bij de bouw om een Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED)-certificering te behalen. LEED-certificering betekent dat een gebouw gezond en zeer efficiënt is en betere milieuprestaties levert.

Als Teamleider Brandveiligheid bij Deerns sta jij aan het roer van een groeiend team van specialisten en geef je richting aan de verdere ontwikkeling ervan. Het team bestaat momenteel uit een mix van ervaren experts en talentvolle adviseurs en bevindt zich in een fase van sterke groei. Je combineert strategisch leiderschap met inhoudelijke diepgang en bent bepalend voor de kwaliteit, koers en groei van het team. Je creëert een omgeving waarin professionals excelleren, kennis wordt gedeeld en innovatie wordt gestimuleerd.

column6:
2 van Schiphol, zo’n 40% van de gehele terminal: De huidige installaties die zorgen voor een aangenaam binnenklimaat, maken gebruik van fossiele brandstoffen. Wij werken aan het ontwerp van de nieuwe installatie, die warmte en koude opslag combineert met warmtepompen zodat Schiphol energieneutraal de toekomst tegemoet kan. De uitdaging van dit project zit met name in het toepassen van nieuwe techniek in een bestaand gebouw waar ruimte moet worden gecreëerd om alle apparatuur en leidingen goed onder te brengen en te zorgen dat elke ruimte wordt voorzien van voldoende verwarming en koeling. Dit moet zorgen voor een aangename passagiersbeleving maar ook voor het aanbieden van een prettig werkklimaat voor de medewerkers op Schiphol, rekening houdend met hun dagelijkse activiteiten.

  • We werken aan het nieuwe operationele gebouw van DC ANSP, de luchtverkeersleiding van het Nederlandse luchtruim in de Cariben. Dit is een faciliteit voor de luchtverkeersleiders die verantwoordelijk zijn voor area control, waarbij de operations room en de ruimte waar de apparatuur staat opgesteld aan strenge bouwfysische en klimaateisen moeten voldoen met een hoge mate van redundantie. De omgeving vraagt daarnaast om een robuust ontwerp dat bestand is tegen orkanen en aardbevingen.

  • We werken op Schiphol aan diverse grote en kleine projecten waarin klimaatbeheersing een grote rol speelt door intensiever gebruik van diverse ruimtes en toename van de apparatuur. Schiphol is een unieke klant om voor te werken, vanwege de omvang van de luchthaven, de continue operationele eisen en de aanwezigheid van verschillende beveiligingszones. Wij worden veel ingezet om de oorzaak van klachten te achterhalen en de juiste oplossing te bieden, of om de juiste oplossing te vinden voor nieuwe apparatuur die hogere eisen stelt aan de installaties. Vrijwel altijd gaat het hier om locaties waar zich passagiers bevinden en Schiphol deze een comfortabele omgeving wil bieden, of waar medewerkers taken uitvoeren die essentieel zijn voor het primaire proces van de luchthaven, waarbij een prettig klimaat een belangrijke voorwaarde is.

Legal AI is only as good as the knowledge behind it. At Lefebvre Sdu, we’ve been building that knowledge for 200 years. Day in, day out. Law by law. Word by word. Other legal AI tools run on our data and software. As the Dutch heart of Lefebvre Group, the European leader in legal and tax knowledge, we’re also developing our own platform: GenIA-L, where lawyers and tax professionals don’t just get an answer, but an answer they’re willing to put their name to. More than 75,000 professionals use it every day, accounting for over €100 million ARR across Europe. We’re looking for a Senior AI Engineer to help shape how the intelligent core of that platform evolves.

HOW YOU'LL MOVE US FORWARD

GenIA-L is a research platform for legal professionals. A user asks a question. The platform searches our trusted sources and turns them into a usable answer. This is done with agents: specialised AI components that each take on part of the question and work together. In the legal domain, an answer can’t just sound convincing. It has to be correct, and you need to be able to see which source it comes from. This isn’t a pilot: the platform is in production and used heavily every day.

As a senior, you build alongside the team, but you also keep the bigger picture in view. You know the different parts of the platform and how they affect one another. You help prioritise, spot obstacles early and make sure we’re heading in the right direction, both in how we work and technically. You look ahead: where could we go, and what do we need to know to get there? And you help medior colleagues grow by seeing exactly where they’re stuck, without taking the work off their hands.

  • You give direction to the agent architecture of GenIA-L: which specialised agents are needed and how they work together.

  • You break down legal processes and translate them into technical solutions. You decide how the components are best connected.

  • You make sure our knowledge packages and the pipelines behind them can scale and stay up to date. A knowledge package is an expert-reviewed set of commentary, case law, legislative history and practical guidance for each article of law.

  • You build the way we measure quality. Using evaluation sets, observability and metrics, you show that answers, source attribution and reliability are genuinely improving. Not based on gut feeling, but on evidence.

  • You help prioritise the team’s work and flag technical or process risks early.

  • You explore new developments, test ideas in practice and turn them into proposals that make the product sharper or faster.

  • You coach medior engineers and work directly with editors and subject-matter experts.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

You have a realistic view of LLMs. You see what they can do, but you also know their weak spots. You follow new AI developments closely, but you don’t just follow the herd: you stay critical and aren’t afraid to say so. You can break a complex problem down into smaller pieces and keep oversight of a system with many moving parts. You take ownership, show initiative when things aren’t yet clear and think from the customer’s problem. You enjoy helping others move forward without taking over. And you like working with lawyers and editors, because they know what a good answer looks like.

  • Extensive experience in software or ML engineering, around 5 years or more. Depth in recent projects counts for more than the number of years.

  • In-depth knowledge of Python and experience with relevant machine learning libraries.

  • You’ve built LLM applications and run them in production.

  • Solid experience with agent frameworks such as LangGraph and LangChain, tool calling, MCP or similar orchestration. Our entire product is built around this. Experience with only a simple search-and-answer setup (RAG) isn’t enough.

  • You’ve made the quality of LLM systems measurable with evaluation sets and observability, and can give concrete examples. Experience with tools like MLflow and LiteLLM is a plus.

  • Strong backend experience, including REST APIs and Postgres databases.

  • Experience with Kubernetes.

  • Experience in the legal, tax or another knowledge-intensive domain is a plus.

Legal AI is only as good as the knowledge behind it. At Lefebvre Sdu, we’ve been building that knowledge for 200 years. Day in, day out. Law by law. Word by word. Other legal AI tools run on our data and software. As the Dutch heart of Lefebvre Group, the European leader in legal and tax knowledge, we’re also developing our own platform: GenIA-L, where lawyers and tax professionals don’t just get an answer, but an answer they’re willing to put their name to. More than 75,000 professionals use it every day, accounting for over €100 million ARR across Europe. We’re looking for a Medior AI Engineer to help shape how the intelligent core of that platform evolves.
column2:
>

HOW YOU'LL MOVE US FORWARD

GenIA-L is a research platform for legal professionals. A user asks a question. The platform searches our trusted sources and turns them into a useful answer. It does this with agents: specialised AI components that each handle part of the question and work together. In the legal domain, an answer can't just sound fluent. It has to be correct, and you must be able to see which source it comes from. This is not a pilot project: the platform runs in production and is used heavily every day.

As a medior, your focus is on building. You work independently, on challenges that come from customers and on challenges we spot ourselves. You break down a legal process, translate it into a technical process and work out how to best connect the pieces. Stuck on something? You say so, and your colleagues think along with you.

You build and improve the agents of GenIA-L and the way they work together.

You build and maintain our knowledge packages: for each legal article, an expert-validated set of commentary, case law, parliamentary history and practical interpretation. You also work on the pipelines that create these packages and keep them up to date.

You make quality measurable. With evaluation sets, observability and metrics, you show that answers, source attribution and reliability really improve. Not by gut feeling, but with evidence.

You build features for customers, such as analysing their own documents and new ways to search case law.

You work directly with editors and subject-matter experts, and check with them which parts of a legal question really matter.

You come up with and test ideas to make the product sharper or faster, and alternate AI experiments with back-end development.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

You have a realistic view of LLMs. You see what they can do, but you also know their weak spots. You enjoy following new AI developments, but you don't just follow the herd: you stay critical. You think in a structured way and can break a complex problem into smaller pieces. You work independently, take initiative when things are unclear and are eager to learn fast. And you enjoy working with lawyers and editors, because they know what a good answer looks like.

  • You have several years of experience in software or ML engineering. Depth in recent projects counts for more than years.

  • You have good knowledge of Python and experience with relevant machine learning libraries.

  • You have helped build an LLM application that runs in production. Not just prototypes, notebooks or courses.

  • You have hands-on experience with agent frameworks such as LangGraph and LangChain, tool calling, MCP or comparable orchestration. Our entire product is built around this. Experience with only a simple search-and-answer (RAG) setup is not enough.

  • You have measured the quality of an LLM system with evaluation sets or observability, and can give a concrete example. Experience with tools like MLflow and LiteLLM is a plus.

  • You have back-end experience, including building REST APIs.

  • You have experience in Kubernetes. Experience with Postgres is useful.

  • Experience in a legal, tax or other knowledge-intensive domain is a plus.

Description

QuantumDiamonds is building the world's first commercial quantum sensing tools for chip failure analysis. Our Quantum Diamond Microscope (QDm) images magnetic fields with micrometer resolution, and that capability could matter far beyond semiconductors. As our Technical Business Development Intern for Emerging Verticals in the Data Science &
column2:
Machine Learning team in Pre-Development, you help us find out where.

Working directly with our project lead for Emerging Verticals, who mentors you, you explore new application fields for widefield magnetic imaging. You dig into the science and the markets behind them, talk to potential customers and users, and help turn promising ideas into first feasibility studies with our magnetic field imaging system. You see how a deep tech company decides where its technology goes next, and help shape that decision.

This is a full-time internship for 6 months, starting as soon as possible.

Who we are

Founded in 2022 as a spin-off of TU Munich, QD leverages quantum sensors to rapidly capture three-dimensional current maps within multi-layer chips. Our strong, international team of over 70, including physicists, engineers, data scientists, and other experts, works side by side with major semiconductor manufacturers, supporting chip debugging and accelerating yield analysis. Backed by top-tier deep tech investors, semiconductor experts, and strategic public programs, we have ensured long-term stability, shifting from breakthrough to scale - and shaping the next chapter in chip testing.

Why join Quantum Diamonds?

Picture this:

  • Quantum sensors that see inside the most advanced chips on Earth, right where two frontier fields collide.

  • Nobel-Prize physics aimed at real customers with real problems, in production now, not someday.

  • Physicists, data scientists, and engineers building side by side, turning deep science into tools the industry actually runs on.

  • An international team that runs at hard problems for fun, where knowledge moves fast and so do you.

Still unsure about why joining us?

  • You'll get to build a company together with a brilliant and welcoming team on a product that has never been done before.

  • From Day 1, you'll own your own topics end to end and see the direct impact of your work on how the world sees QuantumDiamonds.

  • Our technology is the cutting edge of tomorrow, starting today and not in 10 years.

  • You’ll be part of a high-growth company backed by top-tier investors.

Let’s make the invisible visible!

  • Map and evaluate application areas for magnetic field imaging beyond semiconductors: key players, customer segments and structured comparisons of use cases.

  • Review scientific literature and patents to understand the state of the art, competing measurement methods, and where NV-based imaging offers a real advantage.

  • Prepare and join discovery conversations with researchers and companies to understand their measurement challenges, and keep contacts and opportunities up to date in our CRM.

  • Support feasibility studies with our experts, from defining suitable samples to interpreting first measurement results.

  • Turn your findings into clear deliverables such as application one-pagers, decision memos, and presentations.

About HappyRobot

HappyRobot is the infrastructure for enterprises to build and orchestrate AI workforces. Our platform is battle-tested in the most demanding environments, where AI has real consequences. We started in logistics, built our own voice stack, models, and orchestration layer from the ground up, and are now bringing that infrastructure to every enterprise that runs the real economy. Role Overview

We are looking for a Deployment Strategist to join our team. In this role, you'll partner with Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) across the full deployment lifecycle, from first discovery conversation to live production. You'll lead use case discovery and scoping with senior customer stakeholders, ship prototypes hands-on to prove value early, then stay close to the build through delivery to bring the strategic, business-value lens to every decision. You're the partner who keeps the work pointed at the highest-impact outcomes, ready to pick up the keyboard alongside the FDE when the moment calls for it.

We're looking for engineers with strategic instincts: people who can write code, but whose deepest strength is the strategic, opinionated lens they bring across every phase of a deployment - spotting where value lives, scoping it realistically, and partnering with engineers to capture it from prototype to production.

At HappyRobot, there's no role seniority or hierarchy. We operate as a team of builders. We execute, we build, we own, and we care deeply about our customers and their success.

What You'll do

  • Strategic Leadership and Use Case Discovery: Partner with Global and Regional C-Level executives and VPs to assess AI opportunities and prioritize the highest-impact use cases. Lead curiosity-driven discovery that surfaces the workflows where AI creates the most business value, well beyond what the customer thought to ask for. Build the trusted relationships that let you present findings and challenge assumptions at the most senior levels, keeping technical delivery aligned with their business priorities.

  • Scoping: Frame impact versus effort with rigor on both axes. On business value, pressure-test the realistic upside, question whether the use case as posed will actually deliver the most impact, and explore whether reframing it or pivoting to an adjacent process would unlock more. The art is deeply understanding how to maximize value of this use case for the customer, not just delivering what was asked for. On technical effort, map integrations, data, and platform constraints, and surface the edge cases and dependencies that shape timelines. Land on a plan that's realistic on both.

  • Prototyping: Build prototypes and demos hands-on. Use our platform and AI-powered coding tools to test ideas end-to-end at light scope. Prove value early, before the customer commits.

  • Program Management: Coordinate work across the active deployments in an account. Be the escalation point for the customer and the watchout partner for the FDE. Stay close enough to the build that you both understand the use case deeply, spot opportunities to capture more value, and catch when work is drifting from the highest-impact path.

  • Prioritization: Sequence use cases within an account so each deployment compounds the next. Make the call on what gets built when, what gets parked, and where to invest discovery and building time.

  • Customer Partnership: Be the main business-side point of contact for the account. Build trust with operational and executive stakeholders day-to-day. Translate AI capabilities into language they can act on.

  • Onsite Embedding: Travel onsite for kickoffs, mapping sessions, and key moments where being on the ground changes the outcome.

  • Product Feedback Loop: Bring field signal back to Product and Engineering. Identify reusable patterns, common edge cases, and where the platform needs to evolve.

Must Have

  • Background that mixes technical depth with strategic instinct, and a real history of building things. Common paths include engineering (Computer Science, electrical, industrial, systems), data science, founding a tech startup, product management, or technical / strategic consulting.

  • Comfortable coding -mostly Python- using LLMs and AI-powered tools like Claude Code to ship prototypes fast.

  • Working understanding of APIs, integrations, and how AI agents sit inside enterprise workflows.

  • Strategic instinct: ability to spot the business value behind a workflow and translate it into impact, effort, and prioritization terms a C-level can act on.

  • Excellent communication skills with both executives and operators. Comfortable translating between business and technical without losing either side.

  • Proven ability to prioritize ruthlessly across multiple workstreams and drive outcomes, not just activity.

  • Founder mindset: highly independent, takes ownership, and thrives in a fast-paced environment.

Why join us?

  • Join a world-class team of engineers and builders.

  • Backed by top investors including a16z, Y Combinator, Base10, Prysm Capital and Eurazeo.

  • Have ownership and autonomy of projects and are encouraged to ship.

  • Comprehensive Benefits including healthcare, dental, vision coverage.

  • Competitive salary + equity in a high-growth startup.

Our Operating Principles


Extreme Ownership

We take full responsibility for our work, outcomes, and team success. No excuses, no blame-shifting — if something needs fixing, we own it and make it better. This means stepping up, even when it’s not “your job.” If a ball is dropped, we pick it up. If a customer is unhappy, we fix it. If a process is broken, we redesign it. We don’t wait for someone else to solve it — we lead with accountability and expect the same from those around us.

Craftsmanship

Putting care and intention into every task, striving for excellence, and taking deep ownership of the quality and outcome of your work. Craftsmanship means never settling for “just fine.” We sweat the details because details compound. Whether it’s a product feature, an internal doc, or a sales call — we treat it as a reflection of our standards. We aim to deliver jaw-dropping customer experiences by being curious, meticulous, and proud of what we build — even when nobody’s watching.

We are “majos”
Be friendly &
column2: have fun with your coworkers. Always be genuine &amp

Urgency with Focus
Create the highest impact in the shortest amount of time. Move fast, but in the right direction. We operate with speed because time is our most limited resource. But speed without focus is chaos. We prioritize ruthlessly, act decisively, and stay aligned. We aim for high leverage: the biggest results from the simplest, smartest actions. Talent Density and Meritocracy
Hire only people who can raise the average

First-Principles Thinking

This is an on-site/hybrid role in Munich, close to engineering and assembly.

  • Define clear quality criteria for suppliers and components together with Engineering

  • Give the assembly team the forward visibility they need to plan builds

  • Turn supply analysis into input for Leadership’s volume commitments

  • Once supply is robust, reduce component prices toward a leaner bill of materials

About you

  • Several years in supply chain, procurement or sourcing for hardware products (e.g. robotics, automotive, machinery, electronics)

  • Proven experience moving products from prototype to series production

  • Full ownership of a function you build yourself, with direct impact on getting the robots into series production

  • A small, ambitious team where initiative leads to responsibility

  • An on-site/hybrid role in Munich, close to Engineering and Assembly

Bei GALVANY ist es unser Ziel, klimaneutrales Wohnen für alle zur Realität zu machen. Wir setzen auf Umsetzung und entwickeln konkrete, smarte Lösungen, indem wir Wärmepumpen, Batteriespeicher und Smart Metering einfach zugänglich, zuverlässig und bezahlbar machen.

Du sorgst für Klarheit, Verbindlichkeit und einen professionellen ersten Eindruck – und stellst sicher, dass sich unsere Kund:innen jederzeit gut aufgehoben fühlen. Du arbeitest eng mit Sales, Marketing und unseren technischen Teams zusammen und trägst maßgeblich zur Kundenzufriedenheit bei.

  • Entgegennahme und Bearbeitung eingehender Kundenanrufe als zentraler, telefonischer Erstkontakt.

  • Direkte, strukturierte Lösung von Anliegen am Telefon – von allgemeinen Fragen bis zu spezifischen Problemen.

  • Einhaltung von Service-Levels (Erreichbarkeit, Anrufannahme, Bearbeitungszeit) mit klaren Zielwerten.

  • Lückenlose Dokumentation jedes Gesprächs im CRM-System direkt im Anschluss an den Call.

  • Enge Abstimmung mit Sales, Marketing und technischen Berater:innen zur Sicherstellung der Kundenzufriedenheit.

  • Mitwirkung an der Optimierung von Gesprächsleitfäden, Skripten und Telefonie-Prozessen.

Dein Profil

  • Erfahrung im telefonischen Kundenkontakt, z. B. im Kundenservice, Inside Sales, Vertrieb oder in der Bestandskundenbetreuung.

  • Sicherer Umgang mit CRM-Systemen und digitalen Tools.

  • Fließendes Deutsch in Wort und Schrift (C2).

Zusätzlich sind uns folgende Fähigkeiten und Eigenschaften wichtig:
