Designing lifecycle evaluation for nondeterministic domain-specific AI systems.

EggAI Labs

We're opening the EggAI Labs in Tübingen. The Labs purpose is to test new AI capabilities, identify what works, how they'd improve delivery, and then build assets to support teams and clients. EggAI's mission cannot be achieved through one-off client projects alone and the Labs is the way to adapt and scale.

As part of the first cohort, you will join a small peer group and work directly with EggAI's CAIO, a Tübingen alumnus. You will also collaborate with our engineering, product, and project leads, who will bring you insights from client problems, help you understand their context and challenge your solutions for them. Your fellow AI Builders will be deliberately chosen to span different passions and strenghts. You will have room to explore and be expected to turn that exploration into something useful. This is not a client-facing role.

The problem: EvalOps

How do we prove an AI system acts as expected under various conditions?

We will explore EvalOps: the methods and tools used to check whether domain-specific AI systems meet their behavioral requirements. Among the key challenges for operating AI systems are nondeterminism, ground-truth curation, evaluation metric-design, latency and costs. EvalOps need to overcome all of them in a disciplined way.

These questions will guide the initial work:

  • Regression suites: How can domain experts turn traces, code, and prompts into useful evals in a way that scales?

  • Coverage estimation: How can we quantify the gaps between an eval suite and the range of expected agent behaviors?

  • Live monitoring: Is it possible to detect anomalous behaviour in production with a similar precision to regression evals?

  • Eval analysis: How much evidence is enough to act (e.g., deploy, debug, roll back a feature, choose a different model)? You will help refine them, test approaches, create assets, and pose new questions.

The role

As an AI Builder, you will take an open EvalOps problem from investigation to a working prototype, ready to be tested. Whatever your focus, you will be expected to take a problem through to a useful result. Here is what that means in practice:

  • Research emerging AI and evaluation capabilities and distinguish substance from hype.

  • Understand the user, workflow, domain, and organisational problem around the work.

  • Evaluate usefulness, quality, safety, and reliability with appropriate evidence.

  • Communicate decisions and learning clearly.

  • Create assets that other people can understand, use, and improve.

  • Code and build end to end.

This shared foundation leaves room for different strengths and interests. Each AI Builder will then develop greater depth in one of three pillars.

Wir bauen die Marke, auf die unsere Eltern gewartet haben. Bau sie mit uns! ✨

Die meisten Menschen denken bei Muskeln an Fitnessstudio und Bodybuilding. Wir denken an Lebensqualität. Denn Muskeln sind das Fundament eines aktiven Lebens. Sie halten uns beweglich, unabhängig und leistungsfähig im Alltag.

Fortisana ist unsere Antwort darauf: ein wissenschaftlich fundierter All-in-One-Drink rund um Muskelerhalt und ein aktives Leben. Wir stehen am Anfang – und du kannst mitprägen, wie Menschen uns kennenlernen.

Hinter Fortisana stehen Piran, Leon und Max:

  • Piran hat KoRo mitgegründet und über neun Jahre zu einer der erfolgreichsten Lebensmittelmarken Deutschlands aufgebaut.

  • Leon ist Ernährungsberater und in der Welt der Nahrungsergänzung aufgewachsen. Seine Familie produziert seit über 25 Jahren Nahrungsergänzungsmittel in Deutschland.

  • Max hat bereits mehr als sechs Startups begleitet und zuletzt bei 1KOMMA5° gelernt, wie aus einer Vision ein operativ exzellentes Unternehmen wird.

Was du bei uns machst

  • Du übernimmst unseren Markenauftritt auf Social Media. Von der Strategie über die kreative Idee bis zum fertigen Beitrag entwickelst du Inhalte mit einer klaren Handschrift.

  • Du setzt selbst um. Du entwickelst starke Einstiege, planst Drehs, filmst und schneidest Kurzvideos – von Produktaufnahmen über Interviews bis zu Einblicken hinter die Kulissen.

  • Du lernst aus den Ergebnissen. Du veröffentlichst, hörst der Community zu und nutzt ihre Fragen und die Leistungsdaten deiner Beiträge, um die nächsten Ideen besser zu machen.

Was du mitbringst

  • Du verstehst Social Media. Du kannst Geschichten erzählen und bei Menschen eine Reaktion auslösen. Dein Portfolio zeigt, was du selbst umgesetzt hast.

  • Du hast ein gutes Gespür. Für Ästhetik, Sprache, Timing und die Details, die aus einem ordentlichen Video ein richtig gutes machen.

  • Du denkst mit. Sport, Ernährung und Markenaufbau interessieren dich. Du vermittelst Gesundheitsthemen verständlich und sorgfältig, ohne übertriebene Versprechen.

  • Du packst an. Du bringst eigene Ideen ein und hast Freude daran, sie selbst auf die Straße zu bringen.

  • Du kommunizierst sicher. Ausgezeichnete Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift sind Voraussetzung. Du formulierst in beiden Sprachen sicher, präzise und zielgruppengerecht.

  • Du bist vor Ort. Du bist in Berlin oder bereit, für mindestens sechs Monate hierherzukommen.

  • Du arbeitest AI-native und mit Qualitätsanspruch. Du testest eigenständig neue KI-Tools und kreative Ansätze und integrierst sie sinnvoll in deine Workflows. Dabei prüfst du die Ergebnisse kritisch und hältst unseren Qualitätsstandard bei Inhalt, Gestaltung und Genauigkeit hoch.

  • Ein Plus: Erfahrung mit Animation oder Sounddesign.

Was wir dir bieten

  • Verantwortung ab dem ersten Tag. Deine Ideen und deine Arbeit prägen die Marke. Du bekommst Freiraum, Dinge auszuprobieren und eigene Entscheidungen zu treffen.

  • Du lernst, wie ein Startup entsteht. Mit direktem Feedback von Gründern, die wissen, wie man starke Verbrauchermarken aufbaut. Achterbahnfahrt inklusive.

  • Du arbeitest mit uns. Wir sind ein kleines Team. Gute Ideen werden gehört, Einsatz wird wertgeschätzt und du siehst, was deine Arbeit bewegt.

  • Du entwickelst dich weiter. Von Markenstrategie und Zielgruppenverständnis über Storytelling bis zu Produktion, Schnitt und KI.

  • Du wächst mit uns. Unsere Ambition ist groß. Wenn wir abheben, fliegst du mit uns.

Lust, dabei zu sein?

Uns interessiert, wie du denkst und was du richtig gut kannst. Ein perfektes Anschreiben brauchen wir nicht. Zeig uns lieber deine Arbeit. 🤎

Schick uns drei Arbeiten, auf die du stolz bist. Sag bei jeder Arbeit konkret, was von dir stammt: Idee, Skript, Dreh, Schnitt oder Veröffentlichung – und ob sie im Job, für einen Kunden oder als eigenes Projekt entstanden ist. Wenn vorhanden, ergänze Ergebnisse und was du daraus gelernt hast. Dazu brauchen wir deinen Standort, deinen möglichen Starttermin und ein kurzes Profil oder einen Lebenslauf.

About REPLUG

REPLUG is a Mobile Revenue Growth partner that helps companies turn mobile into a measurable driver of revenue, customer value, and long-term business growth.

From global app publishers to established brands looking to unlock more value from mobile, we partner with companies that want to grow more efficiently, reduce dependency on saturated acquisition channels, and build sustainable growth.

Our work combines strategic thinking with hands-on execution across App Store Optimization, Paid User Acquisition, CRM, measurement, and mobile growth consulting.

We are looking for a Senior Sales Manager to win new business for REPLUG’s performance advertising offering, working directly with the co-founder.

Your focus will be helping app advertisers acquire users through performance-based campaigns, including fixed CPI/CPA models, OEM advertising, and alternative acquisition channels.

This is a senior individual contributor role with ownership of the full sales cycle. You will identify opportunities, open conversations, understand advertisers’ growth challenges, and turn qualified prospects into active clients.

We are looking for someone with a hunter mentality and the commercial judgment to build lasting business. You know how to create your own pipeline, earn the attention of experienced buyers, and move deals forward.

Your responsibilities

Generate new business

  • Build and manage your own pipeline through targeted outbound, industry relationships, referrals, and relevant inbound opportunities.

  • Identify app advertisers whose acquisition objectives, budgets, and technical setup fit our performance advertising offering.

  • Develop relationships with decision-makers across user acquisition, growth, and marketing teams.

Own the full sales cycle

  • Lead discovery calls to understand acquisition challenges, existing channel mix, performance targets, and buying criteria.

  • Build proposals that connect our offering to the advertiser’s business objectives.

  • Negotiate pricing and commercial terms, balancing client expectations with profitable business for REPLUG.

  • Own follow-ups and deal progression through to signature and campaign handover.

Sell with a strong understanding of delivery

  • Explain our traffic sources, buying models, measurement approach, and campaign requirements clearly.

  • Work with our supply and operations teams to validate opportunities and set realistic expectations around performance and scale.

  • Ensure a clear handover covering agreed KPIs, budgets, attribution requirements, and commercial commitments.

Improve how we sell

  • Keep HubSpot updated with accurate opportunities, next steps, and revenue forecasts.

  • Use results and prospect feedback to improve targeting, outreach, and proposals.

  • Share market intelligence with the founders and delivery teams, including advertiser needs, competitor positioning, and emerging opportunities.

Represent REPLUG

  • Attend relevant industry events to develop relationships and generate business.

  • Build a credible presence in the mobile advertising ecosystem through informed conversations and consistent follow-through.

What you bring

  • 3-5 years of relevant sales experience, with a proven track record selling mobile performance advertising to app advertisers or agencies.

  • Experience selling performance-based campaigns, including CPI/CPA models, with familiarity across OEM advertising, ad networks, DSPs, rewarded traffic or other alternative acquisition channels.

  • Evidence of personally sourcing and closing new business.

  • The ability to run the full sales cycle independently, from first contact to commercial negotiation and close.

  • A practical understanding of mobile attribution, MMPs, traffic quality, fraud prevention, and advertiser KPIs such as CPA, ROAS, retention, and LTV.

  • The judgment to qualify opportunities properly and challenge expectations when the commercial or delivery fit is weak.

  • A relevant industry network and the ability to build relationships beyond your existing contacts.

  • A structured approach to prospecting, follow-ups, CRM management, and forecasting.

  • Business-fluent English. Additional European languages are a plus.

Benefits

  • Home Office support for your remote setup.

  • Mentoring sessions to support your professional development.

  • Remote work flexibility based across the European Union.

  • Vouchers and discounts.

  • 24 vacation days per year.

  • High autonomy, zero bureaucracy

Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

🛠️ About our Engineering Teams

Robot Software builds the on-vehicle software platform that Wayve’s AI Driver runs on. Within it, the Experiment Platform team owns the systems that let our researchers develop driving models on the road: deploying models to vehicles, running experiments, and collecting the data that trains the next model.

The team builds a portable development platform that connects to partner vehicles and brings Wayve’s model development capabilities to them, including data collection, experiment control, telemetry and over-the-air updates. It is used across our own fleet and on pre-production vehicles with OEM partners in Europe and Japan, and is central to how Wayve adapts its AI Driver to new vehicles. You will lead a team of engineers based in London, working alongside the Runtime Platform, OS, Sensors and Platform Integration teams in Robot Software.

🧠 Your day-to-day

You will lead the team’s people, plans and partnerships. Most of your time goes to your engineers: regular 1:1s, clear expectations, feedback, performance and promotion cycles, and helping technical leads take on more scope. You will work with your tech leads on technical decisions, own the outcomes, and make sure the team responds well when issues come up in the field. You will maintain the team’s mission, charter and twelve-month roadmap, turn them into quarterly and six-week plans, and keep delivery on track.

You will be the team’s main point of contact for partner engineering teams, programme managers, operations and OEM customers, and you will make it clear what the team owns.

You will stay technically capable and aware of the team’s work across the codebase. You will monitor the architecture, guide the team through technical blockers when needed, and engage with technical leaders in other teams at a technical level.

🧩 What you’ll be working on:

Growing the platform: Take the development platform from its first stable release to a product used across many vehicle types, with predictable releases and validation in CI and on HIL benches.

Experiment control and fleet orchestration: Own model and controller download, the robot state machine, and over-the-air deployment of software, configuration and calibration.

Self-serve experimentation: Make the platform self-serve, so research teams can run their own experiments on vehicles without waiting for platform changes.

Scaling data collection: Onboard and event-based logging, data quality, and data offload over

New vehicles and OEM integrations: Deploy the full platform on Wayve’s next-generation vehicles, and support new OEM integrations through configuration rather than new releases.

Building the operating model around the platform: Releases, support rota, on-call, metrics and observability.

Building the team: Own hiring and onboarding, and grow the team as adoption of the platform expands.

🙌 You should apply if:

You have managed software engineering teams, including hiring, coaching and performance management.

You have owned a platform or product that other teams or customers relied on, and shipped it to devices in the field.

You are technically capable, with hands-on experience in embedded Linux systems software (C++ or Python), and stay close enough to the code to review your team’s work, guide architecture and help resolve technical blockers.

You understand connected device fleets, such as vehicles, robots or IoT, including data logging and offload, over-the-air updates and observability.

You are comfortable leading delivery across many stakeholders, including external partners, and can engage with other technical leaders as a technical peer.

You care about operational reliability and release quality.

Experience with autonomous vehicles or robotics, automotive ECUs (for example NVIDIA Jetson or DRIVE, QNX), Yocto, IPC middleware such as ROS 2 or DDS, or containerised workloads on embedded systems is desirable.

🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.

More about Wayve:

🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.

Über uns
Hausverwalter.ai ist eine All-in-One-Plattform für Hausverwaltungen, mit Funktionen wie Inbox, CRM, Dokumenten, Telefonie, Video Calls, Team Chat und KI-Agenten. Unsere Mission ist es, alles zu automatisieren, was ein Hausverwalter tut.
column3:
>

Über die Rolle
Unsere Plattform ist von Tag eins an agentisch gedacht. Bevor wir überhaupt die UI geplant haben, haben wir geplant, wie Agenten mit der Software arbeiten. Denk dran – unser Ziel ist, die ganze Branche zu automatisieren, und das meinen wir ernst.
Heute gibt es für fast alles, was der Nutzer in der UI machen kann, ein Agenten-Tool, und der Co-Pilot (der tägliche Assistent des Nutzers) kann alles für ihn übernehmen, sogar den Dark Mode an- und ausschalten.
Aber der Co-Pilot ist erst der Anfang. Die eigentliche Herausforderung sind die autonomen Agenten. Dazu unten mehr.
column4:
>

Woran du arbeiten wirst

  • Inbox-Agents: Autonome Agenten, die anspringen, sobald in einem Ticket etwas Neues passiert. Kunden trainieren sie selbst ODER nehmen einfach eine der Vorlagen, die du für sie baust. Diese Agenten können heute schon komplette komplexe Abläufe allein übernehmen und sind einer der Hauptgründe, warum sich Kunden für unsere Software interessieren. Aber wann sollte ein Agent an einen Menschen abgeben, statt selbst zu Ende zu machen? Wie stellen wir sicher, dass er sich an den Prozess hält? Das sind deine Fragen.

  • Harness Engineering: Der Agent hat über 100 Tools. Aber er muss eine Anfrage so verstehen, wie ein Hausverwalter sie versteht, und nicht so, wie die Begriffe außerhalb der Branche klingen. Was gehört in den System Prompt, was in Skills?

  • Knowledge Base: Unsere Plattform hat eine eigene Knowledge Base, ähnlich wie Notion. Komplett selbst gebaut und gedacht als kollektives Gehirn des Unternehmens. Aber sollte die KI auch von selbst „lernen""? Und wenn ja, wann? Und wie machen wir die Suche in der Knowledge Base besser — über bessere Tools, System Prompts oder Skills?

  • Voice-Agents: Dieselben Agenten, nur am Telefon — auf LiveKit gebaut, die Anrufe genauso abwickeln wie unsere Text-Agenten Tickets.

  • LLM Infrastructure. Das richtige Modell für die jeweilige Aufgabe wählen, per Caching und Streaming die Latenz drücken, bei Provider-Ausfällen sauber neu versuchen, Context kompakt halten, die RAG-Suche optimieren, Usage über alle Provider tracken, Kosten senken und mit Evals prüfen, was wirklich besser ist.

About Platform Engineering

Platform Engineering (platformengineering.org) is home to the world's largest community of platform engineers. Through PlatformCon and AgenticCon, one of the world's largest conferences dedicated to platform engineering, we bring together thousands of platform engineers, platform leaders every year. Alongside our events, we run a university, a newsletter read by hundreds of thousands of engineers, and Weave Intelligence, our research arm.

About the Role

We’re looking for an Events Growth Marketing Manager to own registration and attendance growth across our entire events portfolio. That starts with our flagship conferences, PlatformCon and AgenticCon, the biggest conferences in the platform engineering world, which travel to San Francisco, London, Sydney, New York and Berlin, and extends to our roadshows, roundtables, workshops, House of Kube (the largest party in the cloud native world) and the satellite events we run in cities around major conferences such as AWS re:Invent, KubeCon and Google Cloud Next. Your goal is to bring platform engineering leaders into the room and keep them coming back. This is a systems and relationships role, not a one off campaign role. You’ll build the growth loops, the audience, and the repeatable playbook needed to fill these events and drive high attendance every time. You’ll report to the Head of Growth.

What you'll do

  • Own registration and attendance growth for PlatformCon and AgenticCon ticket sales, and for every other event we run, across San Francisco, London, Sydney, New York, Berlin and Amsterdam.

  • Build growth loops and long term relationships with the platform engineering community, its practitioners and its leaders, so we have an audience to pull from in every city.

  • Own our event pages on Luma and the end to end campaigns that fill them.

  • Plan campaigns designed for a high attendance rate, so the right people do not just register but actually show up.

  • Use HubSpot and Luma to build and target the right audience segments for each event.

  • Collaborate with design team to ensure high quality event pages and with content for strong copy and assets.

  • Brief and work with our performance marketing and lifecycle managers to get paid and email support behind each event.

  • Build the systems and the playbook that let us fill these events repeatedly, so the approach compounds instead of starting from scratch each time.

What success looks like

Within your first 90 days, we want you to come back to us with a proposed playbook: how we should run our in person events, and the exact workflow you would follow every time a new event brief lands, from audience to event page to campaigns to attendance. By 180 days, we want that playbook proven on live events, with a rising attendance rate and a reusable audience building in each city.

What you'll bring

  • A systems thinker who works in growth loops, not one off tactics.

  • Experience in B2B SaaS marketing. Even better if you have worked somewhere whose core business is running events.

  • A track record of building and growing audiences and driving real attendance at in person events, not just registrations.

  • Strong hands on experience with CRM tools such as HubSpot for segmentation and targeting.

  • Comfort running social campaigns and briefing paid campaigns.

  • The ability to work independently with complete ownership, and to build a repeatable system rather than firefighting each event.

  • Work closely with the design team to produce strong event visuals, both for our Luma pages and website pages, so every event looks as good as it performs.

  • Comfortable with occasional travel to our event cities when an event calls for it.

Nice to have

  • Experience with Luma as an event platform.

  • Experience marketing events for a company whose primary business is events.

You do not need experience with data or automation tooling such as zapier, n8n or similar data flow systems. Our ops team supports all of that.

The company

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.

The team

The Acquisition Strategy and Tech team is the integrated growth engine for iwoca in Germany. We bridge the gap between high-level commercial strategy and the technical systems that power our customer journey. By combining growth analytics, performance modeling, and full-stack engineering, we own the end-to-end acquisition funnel – from the very first touchpoint to a completed loan application. Our Core Focus:

Strategic Growth & Analytics: We serve as the central hub for our Direct Marketing and Sales channels. We translate complex data into actionable strategies, ensuring our outreach is both scalable and profitably managed.

Technical Infrastructure: We build and maintain the proprietary systems and models that drive our German operations. This includes optimizing the ""User Experience"" (UX) to ensure a frictionless onboarding process for small businesses.

Operational Excellence: We connect the dots between data-driven decision-making and real-world commercial impact. Our mission is to ensure every potential customer receives a clear, relevant, and rapid understanding of how iwoca can fund their business.

We are a fast-moving, cross-functional unit designed to turn strategic hypotheses into measurable results. Whether it’s refining a marketing model or shipping a new feature in the application journey, we ensure that iwoca’s expansion in the German market is backed by robust tech and a clear commercial North Star.

The role

This role sits at the intersection of commercial strategy, data, and technology. Reporting into the Head of Direct Acquisition, you will lead a high-performing, interdisciplinary team of three and own acquisition and activation outcomes for the German market. Your primary objective is to co-define the growth strategy and partner closely with engineering and data teams to build the systems, onboarding journeys, and experiments that bring that strategy to life.

The scope of this role is broad and we're not looking for someone with deep expertise in every domain the team covers – spanning strategy, analytics, product development, and data science – but rather someone intellectually curious, and skilled at asking the right questions.

You'll define hypotheses, lead cross-functional initiatives, and own the roadmap for how iwoca engages with German businesses. You will be accountable for measurable impact on acquisition and conversion, bringing ideas to life through rigorous commercial insight, strong customer empathy, and practical delivery. As a Lead, you will also be responsible for coaching your team and establishing the operating rhythm for this new unit.

Market and problem understanding

  • Deeply understand the German SME lending landscape, customer needs, and competitive context to sharpen our go-to-market strategy.
  • Translate market and customer insight into clearly defined product problems and prioritised commercial opportunities.
  • Inform targeting and segmentation strategies to help Marketing and Sales reach the right customers.

Product build and optimisation

  • Own the roadmap for acquisition and onboarding, working with engineers and data scientists to develop tools such as lead scoring systems, eligibility checkers, and onboarding journeys.
  • Work with marketing and sales to evolve website content, sign-up flows, and decisioning logic to increase conversion.
  • Influence future team capability by helping define priorities, roles, and processes as we scale.

Experimentation and insight

  • Design, run, and interpret A/B tests across messaging, targeting, onboarding tools, and product flows.
  • Identify opportunities using first-principle reasoning supported by data, customer research, and funnel analysis.

Cross-functional collaboration

  • Manage, coach, and develop a team of at the beginning two commercial strategy analysts and a data scientist focused on acquisition strategy and operational excellence.
  • Lead cross-functional initiatives, aligning engineering, data, marketing, and commercial stakeholders around clear goals, hypotheses, and success metrics.
  • Translate high-level business goals into testable hypotheses and actionable briefs for our technical teams.
  • Help establish the operating rhythm, rituals, and roadmap processes for this new team.

The requirements

Essential:

  • Strong commercial mindset with proven experience driving go-to-market strategy and measurable acquisition growth.
  • Experience in growth strategy, revenue operations, or a highly analytical commercial role with a track record of driving tech-enabled or product-led growth.
  • Proven people management or team leadership experience, with the ability to build culture and establish operating rhythms in a newly formed team.
  • Fluency in German and strong written communication skills tailored to customer-facing environments.
  • Strong analytical capability and experience with experimentation frameworks and A/B testing tools.
  • Experience working with (or a strong desire to learn about) technical models such as lead scoring, predictive targeting, or qualification logic.
  • Ability to work from first principles and thrive in ambiguity with curiosity and autonomy.

Bonus:

  • Experience in fintech, lending, B2B SaaS, or regulated products.
  • Experience working closely with engineering, product, or data science teams to ship features or models.
  • Knowledge of the German SME ecosystem or B2B financial products.

The culture

At iwoca, the best idea wins. We model our culture on independent thinking, challenging untested logic, and evidence-based decisions. We prioritise learning and growth, and give people the autonomy to develop in the direction that makes them most effective.

We're a tech company and believe in the power of AI to help us work faster and better. We provide the infrastructure where every iwocan always has access to the best models and where those models have access to all of our data. We will help our people to learn how to use and grow with the new tools available to them.

The offices

We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work:

  • Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.
  • Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.

The benefits

A smart, motivated and international team (we represent over 35 different nationalities) with ridiculous growth-mindset.

26 days of vacation a year plus a free day for your birthday.

One-month fully paid sabbatical after 4 years.

Mental health support with direct access to certified psychologists via our partner OpenUp.

iwoca takes over a ski chalet in winter so that you and your team can ski or snowboard (and work) for a week. During summer we are drawn to the sun. We’ve been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield.

Access to the gym membership program, €25 for either Fit711 or Urban Sports Club.

€30 contribution towards the Deutschlandticket.

Company Pension with Canada Life.

Great office locations. In Frankfurt in the middle of the city, our Berlin office is located in Prenzlauer Berg.

A paid volunteer day that gives you the opportunity to invest time to support a charity of your choice.

Corporate Benefits discounts.

’iwocans’ also benefit from fully stocked fridges in our offices with whatever is needed to strengthen them. There are snacks (both healthy and less healthy) for the whole day.

And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer:

  • A learning and development budget for everyone, including a book budget.
  • Learning German budget.
  • Company-wide talks with internal and external speakers.
  • Access to learning platforms like Treehouse.

The company

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4.5 billion in funding. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.

The team

The Partner Acquisition Germany team builds the partner channel through which iwoca reaches small businesses in Germany: comparison platforms and brokers, banks, payment providers, business software providers and financial advisors who offer iwoca's finance to their customers at the moment it is needed. The team works with three partnership models, from a co-branded referral link and a partner portal to a full API integration, and measures its success by partners that are live and funding customers.

The team is small and works closely together: the Head of Partner Acquisition Germany, a Strategy & Data Manager who owns market analysis, business cases and the CRM, and the partner managers who own the relationships. The team prioritises partners by strategic fit, works through warm introductions and existing networks wherever possible, and stays close to every new partner until the first customers are funded. It works hand in hand with Relationship Management and the product and engineering teams in London / Berlin / Frankfurt that build the integrations.

The role

This is a senior role with full ownership of the partners you pursue. Three things matter more than anything else: You will qualify before you sell, because the best partnerships begin with a genuine customer need. You know how to activate networks and create warm introductions rather than relying solely on cold outreach. And you consider a deal complete only when the partnership is live, working well and funding its first customers. You'll travel across Germany one to two days a week for face-to-face partner meetings, industry events and trade fairs.

Ownership and impact

  • Own a portfolio of the highest-value partnership prospects in Germany, from first conversation to signed contract and live integration.

  • Lead negotiations with founders, managing directors and heads of product or partnerships at banks, payment providers, business software platforms and financial intermediaries.

  • Design the cooperation model and commercial terms for each partner so that the partnership works for both sides over years, not quarters.

  • Bring every partner to go-live with a committed internal promoter and a first concrete use case, so that your work turns into funded customers and long-term value.

Autonomy, backed by a dedicated strategy and data function

  • Spend your time on relationships and deals, with a Strategy & Data Manager who builds target models, business cases and CRM automation alongside you for your prospects and partners.

  • Own your pipeline end to end and keep it transparent, so that forecasts and decisions rest on input and numbers everyone trusts.

  • Decide together with the Head of Partner Acquisition which segments and partners you pursue and where you say no.

Influence on product and strategy

  • Feed what you learn from partners directly into our partnership models, the integration roadmap and the go-to-market plan for Germany.

  • Shape the activation playbook for new partners and the handover to Key Account Management together with the Head of Business Development.

  • Represent iwoca at the industry events, trade fairs and partner roundtables that matter for SME finance in Germany.

The requirements

Essential:

  • At least five years of experience in B2B partnerships, business development or key account management in fintech, banking, payments or business software. You can show a proven track record of closing complex deals with six to twelve month sales cycles at C-Level, founder, board or head-of-department level.

  • A working understanding of how a financing product is integrated into a partner's platform: APIs, embedded finance and how a partner's customer data can be used in the application journey. You won't build integrations yourself (our engineering teams do that), but you need to lead that conversation credibly.

  • Professional-level German and English.

  • Demonstrates curiosity to use and learn more about AI tools. You’ll already be comfortable using AI tools in practical ways to help solve problems, increase productivity and improve quality of work, showing good judgement about when to use them and the ability to explain the reasoning behind that use.

Bonus:

  • An existing network among German banks, payment providers, brokers or business software platforms.

  • Experience with lending, working capital or other financial products for small businesses.

  • Experience managing a partner pipeline in HubSpot and using data to prioritise targets.

Don’t take this list as prescriptive: it’s just to give you a sense of who might do well at the job. We’d still love to hear from you if you don’t hit every point on the list, or if you have other experience.

The salary

We expect to pay from €70,000 - €85,000 base salary plus a performance-related bonus for this role. But, we’re open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews.

The culture

At iwoca, the best idea wins. We model our culture on independent thinking, challenging untested logic, and evidence-based decisions. We prioritise learning and growth, and give people the autonomy to develop in the direction that makes them most effective.

We're a tech company and believe in the power of AI to help us work faster and better. We provide the infrastructure where every iwocan always has access to the best models and where those models have access to all of our data. We will help our people to learn how to use and grow with the new tools available to them.

The offices

We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work:

  • Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.

  • Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.

The benefits

  • A smart, motivated and international team (we represent over 35 different nationalities) with a ridiculous growth-mindset.

  • 26 days of vacation a year plus a free day for your birthday.

  • One-month fully paid sabbatical after 4 years.

  • Mental health support with direct access to certified psychologists via our partner OpenUp.

  • iwoca takes over a ski chalet in winter so that you and your team can ski or snowboard (and work) for a week. During summer we are drawn to the sun. We’ve been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield.

  • Access to the gym membership program, €25 for either Fit711 or Urban Sports Club.

  • €30 contribution towards the Deutschlandticket.

  • Company Pension with Canada Life.

  • Great office locations. In Frankfurt in the middle of the city, our Berlin office is located in Prenzlauer Berg.

  • A paid volunteer day that gives you the opportunity to invest time to support a charity of your choice.

  • Corporate Benefits discounts.

  • ’iwocans’ also benefit from fully stocked fridges in our offices with whatever is needed to strengthen them. There are snacks (both healthy and less healthy) for the whole day.

  • Access to learning platforms like Treehouse.

fal is the generative media ecosystem powering the next generation of AI products. We build the infrastructure, tools, and model access that teams need to move from idea to production, and do it at scale without compromise. For developers and enterprises, fal is the foundation that makes generative media not just possible, but practical: a unified platform where high-performance inference, orchestration, and observability come together to unlock new categories of AI-native products.

As generative media reshapes industries across a market projected to grow by hundreds of billions over the next decade, fal is becoming the ecosystem that ambitious teams build on.

About fal

fal is the generative media platform for developers. We give the world's most ambitious AI teams the fastest way to run image, video, audio and 3D models in production. We also provide the GPU infrastructure they need to train, fine-tune and serve models of their own.

Our inference engine was built from the ground up for generative media. It has made fal the platform builders reach for when speed, scale and reliability matter. Our customers range from the fastest-growing AI companies in the world to the Fortune 500. More and more of them are coming to us for raw compute as well as inference and model APIs.

We're a small, high-output team, and we're growing fast. If you want to be in the room while the infrastructure layer of generative AI gets built, this is that room.

About the Role

As an Account Executive on our Compute team, you'll own new-logo acquisition across AI-native startups and neolabs. You'll sell fal's full compute offering: dedicated GPU clusters, reserved and on-demand capacity, and the inference platform that developers already build on. This is a pure hunter role. You won't inherit a book. You'll build one, and with it you'll help define how fal takes compute to market.

What You'll Do

Build and own your pipeline

  • Own all net-new logo acquisition across a defined set of AI-native startups, neolabs and research-driven model builders.

  • Run the full cycle from first conversation through negotiation and signature, keeping momentum through commercial, technical and legal review.

Grow with your customers

  • Land with an initial workload, then expand as customers scale from experimentation to large training runs to production inference.

  • Build multi-threaded relationships so fal is the first call when a customer's next capacity need appears.

  • Hand off smoothly and stay aligned with Account Management and Customer Success as accounts mature.

Shape the business

  • Bring structured customer and market feedback to Product, Infrastructure and Leadership: what's winning, what's missing, and what competitors are doing.

  • A builder's approach to pipeline. You've generated a large share of your own pipeline and you're energized, not intimidated, by a blank territory.

  • Strong commercial judgment. You know when a long-term reservation is the right answer for a customer and when flexibility matters more. You structure deals that set customers up to grow.

Die Position

Deine Aufgaben

Produktmanagement

  • Du entwickelst unsere Cyber-Versicherungsprodukte in Deutschland, den Niederlanden, Österreich und weiteren Ländern weiter und verknüpfst sie eng mit unserem Cyber-Guard- und Incident-Response-Angebot. Bei Bedarf koordinierst du externe Partner.

  • Du treibst die Einführung eines modularen Produktkonzepts voran und skalierst Abläufe durch Automatisierung.

Carrier Management

  • Du steuerst das Carrier Management rechtlich und strategisch. Du verhandelst und verantwortest den Abschluss von Assekuradeurverträgen in der EU und im Vereinigten Königreich und steuerst Kapazitäten für KMU und Großrisiken.

  • Du baust eine stabile, langfristige und diversifizierte Carrier-Basis auf, die unserem Geschäftsmodell bestmöglich entspricht.

  • Du verantwortest alle MGA-Verträge, koordinierst Verlängerungen und baust ein Claims-Management auf, das unsere Profitabilitätsziele mit den Anforderungen der Carrier verbindet.

Dein Profil

  • Du verfügst über fundiertes juristisches Wissen im Bereich Cyber-Versicherung in Deutschland, den Niederlanden oder einem anderen EU-Land. Eine juristische Qualifikation als Rechtsanwalt beziehungsweise vergleichbare juristische Expertise ist ein Plus.

  • Du bringst mehrjährige Erfahrung mit Cyber-Produkten und Bedingungswerken aus dem Underwriting und/oder der Schadenabwicklung mit.

  • Du verstehst Cyber-Compliance und regulatorische Anforderungen und hast praktische Erfahrung mit Incident-Response- und Präventionslösungen.

  • Du denkst unternehmerisch, arbeitest strukturiert und detailorientiert und möchtest etwas aufbauen und skalieren.

  • Du arbeitest selbstständig, trittst sicher auf und bist verlässlich. Es gelingt dir, andere mitzunehmen.

  • Du verhandelst souverän mit Kunden und Partnern, bist belastbar und übernimmst Verantwortung.

  • Du kommunizierst sicher auf Englisch sowie auf Deutsch oder Niederländisch.

Das bieten wir dir

  • Eine Schlüsselrolle in einem der am schnellsten wachsenden Cybersecurity-Scale-ups Europas.

  • Die Möglichkeit, eine innovative Cybersecurity-Produktlinie mitzugestalten, die wirksame Cybersicherheit und Cyber-Versicherung global verbindet.

  • Ein attraktives Vergütungspaket inklusive Bonus.

  • Flexible Arbeitszeiten für eine ausgewogene Work-Life-Balance.

  • Wahlfreiheit bei deiner Ausstattung: MacBook oder Dell Laptop sowie iPhone oder Android-Smartphone.

  • Aktive Unterstützung deiner persönlichen und fachlichen Weiterentwicklung.

  • Die Zusammenarbeit mit erstklassigen Cybersecurity-Expert:innen in unserem internationalen CERT-Team.

Über Eye Security

Eye Security bietet Unternehmen in Europa Cybersicherheit mit integrierten Cyberversicherungslösungen. Unser Team vereint Fachleute mit Erfahrung in den Bereichen Nachrichtendienst, Militär, Technologie und Beratung. Sie alle verbindet eine gemeinsame Mission: Cybersicherheit auf Enterprise-Niveau für jedes Unternehmen zugänglich zu machen – nicht nur für die Großen.

Eye Security wurde 2020 in Den Haag gegründet und vereint Managed Detection and Response, ein rund um die Uhr von Menschen betriebenes Security Operations Center (SOC), schnelle Incident Response und eine eigene Cyberversicherung auf einer einzigen Plattform. Das Unternehmen betreut Organisationen in den Niederlanden, Belgien und Deutschland und baut seine Plattform sowie den Marktzugang in ganz Europa aus.

Eye Security wird von Bessemer Venture Partners, J.P. Morgan Growth Equity Partners und TIN Capital unterstützt. Zuletzt nahm das Unternehmen in einer von Sofina angeführten Series-C-Finanzierungsrunde 60 Millionen Euro auf.

Why SDK Engineering at Langfuse

Your work will have an outsized impact.

Our SDKs are downloaded 26M+ times per month. When you ship a new integration or improve SDK performance, thousands of developers benefit the same day — and they'll tell you about it in GitHub issues, on Twitter, and in our community channels. Everything you build is open source (MIT-licensed) and immediately visible.

The SDK is often the very first thing a developer touches when they try Langfuse, so your work directly shapes their first impression.

You will also have direct exposure to how cutting-edge LLM-applications are built. The users you serve are some of the best and most ambitious software engineers in the world and that leverage Langfuse to improve their applications. Deeply understanding the problems they solve will help you design the best possible SDK experience and along the way makes you an expert on LLM engineering yourself.
column3:
margin-bottom:0px""> 

You will grow at Langfuse by

  • Owning our SDKs. We maintain SDKs in Python and TypeScript both built on OpenTelemetry. You'll be responsible for their reliability, performance, and developer experience. These SDKs run inside our users' production systems, which means they must never fail, must have minimal impact on CPU and memory, and must work flawlessly across every environment — from serverless functions to long-running agent loops. You'll think deeply about the exposed interfaces, error handling, batching, async flushing, and graceful degradation.

  • Designing APIs that developers love. How are functions named, how are parameters structured, how are breaking changes communicated, how does the documentation read? Developer experience is a core differentiator for Langfuse and you'll own every detail of it. When we shipped the Python SDK v3 and TypeScript SDK v4, both were full rewrites on OpenTelemetry — that's the kind of thoughtful, high-impact SDK work you'll lead. Apart from tracing, we also support core workflows of engineers building with LLMs with our SDKs, see our Experiment Runner SDK for example.

  • Integrating with every major AI framework: Langfuse integrates with 40+ frameworks and model providers: OpenAI SDK, Vercel AI SDK, AI SDK, LangChain, LlamaIndex, Pydantic AI, OpenAI Agents, CrewAI, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, LiveKit, and many more. You'll maintain these integrations, ensure new Langfuse features are supported across all of them, and add new integrations as the ecosystem evolves. When a new framework gains traction, you'll be among the first to instrument it.

  • Maintaining our OpenTelemetry endpoint: some users send traces directly to our OTLP endpoint instead of using our SDKs. You'll ensure this path is robust, well-documented, and supports the full range of Langfuse features. This also extends our language support to Java, Go, and any language with an OpenTelemetry SDK. You can work with the OpenTelemetry community to steer the GenAI conventions.

  • Writing public documentation: you'll own the SDK docs, integration guides, and migration paths. At Langfuse, docs are part of our core product. When you ship a new SDK version or integration, the docs ship with it.

What we're looking for

  • Strong engineer who gets excited about developer experience, API design, and writing code that runs reliably in other people's production systems

  • Experience building or maintaining SDKs, client libraries, or developer tools — ideally in Python and/or TypeScript

  • Deep understanding of performance: you know how to profile, benchmark, and minimize CPU/memory overhead in hot paths

  • Someone who can manage projects themselves — you know how to develop strong conviction about what to build and how to ship it

  • Thoughtful about versioning, backwards compatibility, and migration paths

  • Interest in open source software and genuine excitement about talking to developers about their integration challenges

  • Thrives in a small, accountable team where your output is visible and matters

  • CS or quantitative degree preferred

column7: Put your software skills to work testing how AI and machine learning workloads run on Graphcore accelerator hardware.&lt

column7: Put your engineering foundations to work on the electronic systems behind Graphcore’s AI compute platforms.&lt

This role spans Hardware Design and Signal Integrity. Depending on your interests, project needs and developing strengths, you could focus on either area or work across both. You’ll build broad board-level engineering skills while developing deeper expertise.&lt

In Hardware Design, you could develop circuits, select components, create schematics and work with PCB layout through review, bring-up and validation. Projects may involve digital and analogue circuitry, power sequencing, monitoring, board management or interfaces such as I2C, SPI and GPIO. As you grow, you’ll take ownership of scoped circuits or subsystems through to controlled design release.&lt

In Signal Integrity, you could analyse PCIe and Ethernet links, DDR memory interfaces, clocks and other timing-critical signals. Work may span feasibility studies, PCB stack-up, materials, controlled impedance, routing and layout reviews, alongside pre-layout and post-layout simulation. You’ll compare simulations with laboratory measurements, investigate issues and take increasing ownership of defined analyses and interface reviews.&lt

Hardware Design and Signal Integrity engineers work closely with PCB layout, silicon, validation, firmware, mechanical and thermal engineering, manufacturing and system teams. Together, they turn requirements into buildable hardware and investigate how it behaves in practice.&lt

Staff Hardware Engineers and Team Leads will support you through design reviews, laboratory work and day-to-day collaboration. You’ll learn how the team identifies risks before boards are built and resolves issues during development.&lt

Bring your questions and ideas, explain your reasoning and use evidence to challenge assumptions constructively. Take responsibility for your work and speak up when you spot a problem or need support.&lt
During the two-year programme, you’ll develop the judgement to connect circuit design and interconnect behaviour with the performance of a complete board.&lt

You’ll gain experience with tools such as Mentor Expedition for hardware design, and Ansys HFSS and Keysight ADS for electromagnetic and circuit simulation. Comparing models with measurements will help you test hypotheses, understand trade-offs and investigate faults methodically.&lt
Following work through review, implementation, validation and release will help you build confidence in your decisions, document your reasoning and see where you’d like to deepen your expertise.&lt

member-of-scientific-staff-cell-culture-and-functional-assays-london-68194,Substrate Bio,"Member of Scientific Staff, Cell Culture and Functional Assays","

LOCATION: King's Cross, London · PATTERN: Lab-based, full-time

The opportunity

We're a stealth startup in AI and bio, building infrastructure for data generation. The team is small and elite, the problems are hard, and the foundations are being laid right now. You'd help write them from the first line, with real ownership and a direct line to the founders.

This role covers the cell side of our protein characterisation work. You would keep the cell lines healthy and run the assays that show how a designed protein behaves on a living cell, week after week, to the same standard.

About us

AI for biology has a data problem. The data that matters most doesn't exist yet, so we're building the infrastructure to produce it, with quality and traceability built in from day one.

We're in stealth and heads-down on execution. We'll share more about what we're building once you've spoken with the team.

The role

You will run cell culture and the cell-based assays for our protein characterisation work. That means the mammalian lines the assays depend on, from thaw through routine passage to a banked and documented stock, and the weekly rhythm of seeding, treating, reading and reporting plates.

Most of it runs in 384-well plates with imaging-based or flow cytometry readouts. You will run those assays as designed, with the controls and replicates that make a curve defensible, and you will be the person who notices when a plate, a line or a reagent lot has started to drift.

Assay design and the shape of the cascade sit with the scientist who leads this work today, so you are not being asked to invent the panel. You are being asked to make it run the same way every week, to record what you did in a form the rest of the system can read, and to tighten the protocols as they settle, including moving them towards the plate formats our automation will take on.

Your first 90 days

FIRST 30 DAYS

◆ Take over routine culture and banking for the protein cell lines, working to the protocols we already run.

◆ Learn the panel end to end by running each assay alongside the scientist who owns it.

DAYS 30 TO 60

◆ Run at least one assay in the panel independently, including its controls and acceptance criteria.

◆ Revise one culture or assay protocol so that someone else could follow it without asking you.

DAYS 60 TO 90

◆ Hold the weekly assay schedule on your own and return results on the agreed turnaround.

◆ Bring one protocol to a tighter precision bar, or into a plate format ready for automation.

Who you are

You are a hands-on cell biologist who takes assay variability personally. You have run the same assay often enough to tell a real effect from a bad plate, and you would rather find the cause than repeat the run.

The week has a rhythm in this job: cells to feed, plates to seed, runs to finish, numbers to return. You are happy with that, you keep records someone else can pick up, and you say early when something looks wrong rather than at the end of the week.

We do not hire people into boxes. The team is small, and early hires here end up owning work beyond the job they joined for. Nobody arrives with every part of this role. If you are strong in most of it and quick to learn the rest, we want to hear from you.

MUST HAVE

◆ Strong hands-on mammalian cell culture: adherent and suspension lines, aseptic technique, and thawing, passaging and banking to a high and consistent standard.

◆ Experience running cell-based assays end to end, including relevant controls, replicates and dose-response curves behind a reported number.

◆ Comfort with plate-based work and the arithmetic that goes with it, such as dilution series, plate maps and normalisation.

◆ Careful, traceable record-keeping that someone else can follow without asking you.

◆ A PhD in cell biology, pharmacology, immunology or a related field, or an MSc and two to three years of relevant lab experience.

NICE TO HAVE

◆ Reporter cell line bioassays for binding or blockade.

◆ Receptor internalisation, lysosomal trafficking or cytotoxicity assays.

◆ High-content or fluorescence imaging, and the image analysis behind it.

◆ 384-well formats, liquid handlers or other plate-based automation.

◆ Flow cytometry, for example for surface receptor quantification.

Why this is unusual

Most cell-based assay roles sit inside a discovery project. You build an assay, you answer a question with it, and the assay goes quiet. This one is closer to running an instrument. The same assays run every week against a stream of new molecules, and the number that comes out is the product.

That changes what good looks like. Precision matters more than novelty, a protocol is only finished when someone else can run it and get your answer, and every passage, plate and reagent lot is captured as structured data, because a result is only as trustworthy as the cells behind it.

Some people find that energising
column2:
some find it outside their lane. Worth knowing in advance which one you are.

How we work

This is a lab-based role at our site in King's Cross, London. The cells are in the lab, so most of your week will be too, with room for writing and analysis away from the bench. The wider team is distributed and travels, so you will work with people who are not always in the building.

We work in the open. Decisions are written down, work happens centrally rather than scattered across tools, and the week opens with a session the whole company attends. There is a quarterly offsite. Each person owns their area and makes the call inside it, and we will expect that of you early rather than late.

UK benefits are 30 days of annual leave plus public holidays, a pension with a 10% employer contribution, and top-tier Bupa private health cover. More is added as the team grows.

The team you will join

You will join the protein characterisation team and report to its lead. Day to day you will work with the scientist who designs the assay cascade, with the protein production and molecular characterisation scientists upstream of you, with the functional genomics team who share the cell culture suite, and with the engineers building the software and automation the lab runs on.

We are a small, elite team, and this is the first seat given entirely to the cell-based side of the work.

Our process

Our process has four stages. A short screening call about the role and the practicalities. A behavioural interview about how you work, run from the same template for every candidate, before anything technical. A technical stage with the protein characterisation team, built around real work rather than a puzzle, including time with us in person at the lab. Then references, aimed at whatever we still want to understand.

If you are not sure whether you match every line above, apply anyway. We would rather read it and decide.

We are an equal opportunity employer. We make hiring decisions on merit, scope-fit, and the strength of the working relationship we expect to build with each hire. Applications welcome from candidates of any background.

You will make proteins, many of them at once. The work runs from DNA through to purified, quality-checked protein in 96-well format, ready for the binding and biophysical assays downstream of you.

On the DNA side you will prepare expression templates from synthetic gene fragments, by PCR and by Golden Gate or Gibson assembly, and check them before they go forward. Our Company
At Quantum, we connect global brands with high-intent consumers. We turn intent into action and complexity into clarity.

Our Mission is clear, to help smarter, faster buying decisions. Our vision, to be the world’s most used digital comparison service, delivering value and simplicity to millions.

We drive growth through data-driven affiliate marketing built for performance from day one. Every campaign is measurable, optimised in real time, and designed to scale.

With in-house tech, full-stack analytics, and a compliance-first mindset, we give our partners an edge. We drive confident decisions and growth in regulated and high-growth sectors. We’ve helped ambitious brands grow faster, smarter, and globally.

The Role

We're hiring for a Head of SEO to own organic search presence across our iGaming and Rewards propositions in the UK and US. This is a build role: you'll set the strategy, hire the team and put the tooling and processes in place to execute.

You'll turn organic search into a predictable, compliant growth channel measured on commercial outcomes, not just rankings. That means registrations, FTDs and revenue for iGaming, and sign-ups and active members for Rewards.

You'll look after four sites: cashback.co.uk, joincustard.co.uk, strikewild.co.uk and slotswise.com.

Key Responsibilities

Strategy and ownership

  • Set and own the organic search strategy for iGaming and Rewards across the UK and US, with clear targets and a 12-month roadmap

  • Prioritise by commercial value: focus effort on the verticals, states, merchants and page types that drive FTDs, revenue and member growth

  • Own the SEO budget and make the case for investment in people, tools, content and links

  • Work closely with commercial, paid, CRM, brand and compliance teams so SEO priorities match merchant deals and launch plans

Building the team

  • Hire and lead a team from scratch, starting with the roles the roadmap needs most (for example, technical SEO, content SEO, outreach)

  • Decide what to build in-house and what to outsource, and manage agencies and freelancers where it makes sense

  • Set the processes, playbooks and tooling the team runs on

Technical SEO

  • Own site health across our properties: crawlability, indexation, site architecture, Core Web Vitals, structured data and internal linking

  • Work with product and engineering to put SEO into templates, releases and migrations from the start

  • Build scalable page frameworks for reviews, comparisons, offers and state or market landing pages

Content and authority

  • Set the content strategy and editorial standards, with E-E-A-T and YMYL expectations built in

  • Lead a safe, sustainable approach to digital PR and link acquisition in competitive, closely watched SERPs

  • Shape our approach to AI-powered search, AI Overviews and generative engine optimisation (GEO) so our brands are cited and trusted

Markets and compliance

  • Run distinct UK and US plans that reflect each market's regulation, search behaviour and competition

  • Plan US state launches so content and authority are ready ahead of go-live

  • Make sure every page meets UKGC, ASA/CAP, US state and responsible gambling requirements

Measurement

  • Build reporting that links organic traffic to clickouts, registrations, FTDs and revenue

  • Track rankings, share of voice and competitor movement, and act on what the data shows

  • Report performance and forecasts to the leadership team

About You

Essential

  • 8+ years in SEO, with at least 3 years leading SEO strategy and people

  • A track record of growing organic revenue in iGaming, affiliate or another highly competitive, regulated vertical

  • Hands-on depth in technical SEO, and the credibility to work as a peer with engineering

  • Experience hiring and building a team, or a clear plan for how you'd do it

  • Working knowledge of UK and US gambling regulation and what it means for content and marketing

  • Deep understanding and practical application of AI, GEO and the impact on organic search visibility

  • Commercial sense: you can forecast, build a business case and tie your work to revenue

  • Strong command of the core toolset, for example Google Search Console, GA4, Ahrefs or Semrush, Screaming Frog, and BigQuery or SQL

  • Clear communication with senior, commercial and technical audiences

Nice to have

  • Experience launching in newly regulated US states

  • Background in rewards, cashback, loyalty or comparison sites

  • Experience with programmatic or templated SEO at scale

  • Experience running site migrations or consolidations

Join us in our mission to transform the way people shop and eat, where impact, innovation, and growth drives everything we do. Our Site Operations team powers the physical side of our marketplace through HOP (our rapid grocery delivery service) and Editions (our network of delivery-only kitchens). From launching new sites to ensuring operational excellence across markets, we combine retail and hospitality expertise with operational rigour. Get to know our Site Operations team — what drives us, how we work, and what you can expect.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Execute precise order fulfillment by picking customer essentials quickly and accurately to meet delivery deadlines.

  • Maintain product integrity by ensuring all goods received and dispatched meet our high standards for freshness and quality.

  • Facilitate seamless logistics through clear communication with riders to ensure prompt order handovers.

  • Drive inventory excellence by supporting the intake of daily stock deliveries and assisting with ongoing inventory management.

  • Champion site safety and standards by maintaining a clean, organized warehouse environment for the whole team.

What You’ll Need to Thrive

Our ideal candidate will bring strong expertise in some of these areas and curiosity to grow in others:

  • Adaptability in fast-paced environments, with the ability to remain focused under pressure.

  • Strong attention to detail to ensure order accuracy and high-quality stock control.

  • Effective communication skills to collaborate with teammates, managers, and riders.

  • A proactive, hands-on mentality with a drive to solve problems as they arise on-site.

  • A customer-first mindset, understanding that your speed and accuracy directly impact the user experience.

  • Previous experience in FMCG, Retail, or Warehouse environments is valued but not required.

Why Join Us?

At Deliveroo, operations are central to how we build trust across our marketplace. You’ll work in a fast-paced environment where service excellence drives real impact.

  • 🔧 See the impact of your work in real time: Solve problems as they happen, turning challenges into positive experiences across our three-sided marketplace.

  • 🌱 Grow through doing: Develop problem-solving, communication, and leadership skills with structured progression pathways and real opportunities to move into management.

  • 🤝 Be part of a tight-knit culture: Work collaboratively to achieve shared goals in an environment that values support, ownership, and resilience.

  • 🕒 Flexibility that works for you: Enjoy the benefits of shift-based work that fits your schedule.

Our Interview Process

We aim to create a fair process that lets your skills shine:

  • Step 1: Apply – Apply for any role you’d like to be considered for. We’re looking forward to hearing from you.

  • Step 2: Online assessment – If your application is successful, you’ll receive an assessment from our AI hiring assistant, Maki People. Please note: this must be completed to continue.

  • Step 3: Initial conversation – One of our Recruitment team will get in touch to talk through your experience and what you’re looking for next.

  • Step 4: Final Onsite interview – You’ll be invited to an onsite interview with one of our Site Managers.

  • Step 5: Outcome – We’ll get back to you quickly after your interview to let you know the result!

Our Global Structure

Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we’re unlocking new possibilities as one global team.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

At Deliveroo, we know that a great workplace reflects the world around us and that true diversity and inclusion make us stronger, more creative, and better at what we do. We’re committed to fostering an environment where everyone can do their best work and feel they belong.

We believe in equality of opportunity and welcome candidates from all backgrounds regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, socio-economic background, religion, or belief.
